cases.name: Adam and Eve
cases.charge: Hearkening to the serpent’s doctrine that breaking the commandment would not bring death, and eating the fruit of lies; Adam hearkening to the voice of his wife against the commandment
cases.summary: Adam was the chosen of the Most High, formed of the dust of the ground and given the breath of life, which is the commandments (Genesis 2:7). The serpent is Satan, who taught Eve doctrine, that she would not die, and played on her envy, the desire to be equal (Genesis 3:1-5; Wisdom of Solomon 2:24). The fruit she ate was the lie, and she taught her husband what the serpent had taught her (Genesis 3:6). Their nakedness was sin, and the sin was idolatry (Genesis 3:7; Exodus 32:25). The Lord covered them with the first sacrifice and drove them out of the garden (Genesis 3:21-24).
offenseFull: Adam was the chosen: out of all the people the Most High created on the earth, he had a favourite from the beginning, and he formed him of the dust of the ground (Genesis 2:7). The breath of life breathed into him is the commandments (2 Esdras 3:5; Proverbs 7:2). Formed from the soil, Adam was a very dark man, for the richer the soil, the darker; the original man and woman were black. He was formed from the ground and then put in the garden, eastward in Eden, where the Gihon, the Blue Nile, compasses Ethiopia (Genesis 2:8-14).

The Most High looked at the women on the earth and there was no help meet right for Adam, which shows there were more people on the earth than Adam alone, and he made Eve from Adam’s rib (Genesis 2:18-23). Some of the trees of the garden are literal trees, and some represent men (Genesis 2:16-17; Mark 8:24).

The serpent is not a literal snake, for serpents do not speak; another word for serpent is deceiver, and the serpent is Satan in disguise (Genesis 3:1; 2 Corinthians 11:14). Satan taught Eve doctrine: she had been taught that if she broke the commandments she would die, and he taught her that she would not die (Genesis 3:4). He played on the words, not surely die meaning not immediately, and told her that her eyes would be opened and she would be as a god, equal with her husband (Genesis 3:5). Death came into the world through envy (Wisdom of Solomon 2:24): Satan played on Eve’s envy, the desire to be equal; there was one god in that house, and Eve wanted there to be two. The same doctrine is taught today, that you do not have to keep the commandments and you will not die; if you leave the commandments you are going to die.

Good for food means good to learn; enticed to break the commandments, she taught her husband the same thing the serpent taught her, and he broke them as well (Genesis 3:6; Hosea 10:13). Of the woman came the beginning of sin, because Satan came to her first, and through her death came, because Adam listened (Ecclesiasticus 25:24). Adam hearkened to his wife and broke the commandment (Genesis 3:17).
judgmentFull: They were not literally naked; nakedness represents sin, and they were in sin (Genesis 3:7; Lamentations 1:8). The sin was idolatry: Aaron made Israel naked to their shame by the calf, and idolatry causes nakedness, not so much physical as spiritual (Exodus 32:25; Wisdom of Solomon 14:12, 27). The fig leaves and aprons are Adam covering his transgressions, hiding his iniquity (Job 31:33). The trees they hid among are people: Adam and his wife tried to hide their sins among the other people in the garden with them (Genesis 3:8; Ezekiel 31:8).

The Most High was not looking for Adam as though he could not find him; he was calling him to examine himself, for Adam had begun to separate himself by hiding his sins (Genesis 3:9). Adam blamed Eve, and in saying the woman whom thou gavest he blamed the Most High also; then Eve blamed the serpent, and all accountability was removed (Genesis 3:12-13).

The serpent was cursed above all cattle and every beast of the field, and the cattle and the beasts are the nations; going on the belly and eating dust is a very low estate, a vagabond upon the earth, as Cain and Esau became (Genesis 3:14; Micah 7:16-17; Isaiah 49:23). Verse fifteen is prophecy: the woman is the nation of Israel; the enmity between Satan’s seed and Israel’s seed remains; bruising the heel is Satan making Israel stumble through evil communication; and the bruised head is Christ destroying the works of Satan (Genesis 3:15; Jeremiah 3:2; Romans 16:20).

To the woman: her desire, her learning, her desire of anything, was to be to her husband, and he would rule over her; this is one of the first commandments given, and a sister who does not allow her husband to rule over her is not entering the kingdom without fulfilling it (Genesis 3:16; 1 Corinthians 14:34). Because Adam hearkened to his wife, the ground was cursed for his sake, and in sorrow and sweat he would eat of it all his days (Genesis 3:17-19). Death was appointed in Adam the moment he listened to his wife, and in his generations; it was not immediate, but he died over time (2 Esdras 3:7).

The coats of skins are animal sacrifice to cover the sins; here the Most High ordained the sacrificial law (Genesis 3:21). The first sacrifice is twofold: a literal lamb was slain to clothe Adam and his wife, and that lamb slain from the foundation of the world represents Christ (Leviticus 16:27; Isaiah 61:10; Revelation 13:8). He was driven out of the garden, which is paradise, to till the ground from whence he was taken, and when Adam was driven out all were driven out with him; his boughs were delivered to death in the nether parts of the earth (Genesis 3:22-23; Ezekiel 31:14-18). The cherubims and the flaming sword turning every way at the east of the garden were placed there to cause confusion, so that no one can find the way back in, and to that same place Cain afterward went (Genesis 3:24; Genesis 4:16).

cases.name: Abel
cases.charge: Bringing the firstlings of his flock and the fat thereof, according to the sacrifice ordained when the Lord clothed Adam and Eve with skins; calling his brother to repentance
cases.summary: Abel was a keeper of sheep and Cain a tiller of the ground, and with them comes the birth of trade and of religion (Genesis 4:1-2). Abel brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof, in accordance with the sacrifice ordained when the Lord made coats of skins, and the Lord had respect unto him (Genesis 4:4; Genesis 3:21). Abel was a prophet, and when Cain talked with him he was trying to get Cain to repent; Cain slew him (Genesis 4:8; Matthew 23:35). His righteousness still speaks, though he is dead (Hebrews 11:4).
offenseFull: The sacrificial law was ordained when the Most High made coats of skins for Adam and his wife; the blood of the animal stood in for them, and the requirement of blood at the hand of every beast was still in place with Noah, passed down generation to generation (Genesis 3:21; Genesis 9:5). That is why Cain and Abel were bringing offerings: Abel and Cain were present and saw Adam and Eve sacrifice, and it was taught to the sons (Genesis 9:5). Abel brought of the firstlings, the best, of his flock and of the fat thereof, and the Lord had respect unto him because it was according to what was ordained (Genesis 4:4). Sacrifices are symbolic of your works: Abel went above and beyond, and Cain was mediocre; our sacrifices today are keeping the commandments, the work we put in, the alms we give, and the time we sacrifice. The Most High wants obedience, a broken and contrite heart, and Abel was obedient (Psalms 51:16-17).

By faith Abel offered the more excellent sacrifice and obtained witness that he was righteous; his works were righteous and his brother’s evil, and that is why Cain slew him (Hebrews 11:4; 1 John 3:12). Abel was a prophet; he was about God’s laws, and when Cain talked with him he was teaching his brother that he had offered the wrong thing and should follow his example (Genesis 4:8). There had to be correction in that talk for Cain to grow angry enough to put his brother to death; Abel was the wise man whose words are as goads, given to direct a man in the right path (Ecclesiastes 12:11). Abel did what was right, and Cain saw it, and that builds envy; no one is able to stand before envy, and Abel was not able to stand before it (Proverbs 27:4). Christ counts righteous Abel with the blood of the prophets, the first of all the righteous blood shed upon the earth (Matthew 23:35; Luke 11:50-51). Cain did not kill him with a single blow; he killed Abel brutally in his fury, and Cain perished in the same fury (Wisdom of Solomon 10:3).
judgmentFull: The Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering (Genesis 4:4). His righteousness speaks though he is dead: his good works were written down and passed from generation to generation as an example, and the blood of the prophets still cries out to the Most High to this day (Hebrews 11:4; Genesis 4:10). The scriptures record that Abel was faithful in all his works because he died doing the work; he was slaughtered for the work (Hebrews 9:16-17).

Seth was appointed another seed instead of Abel, Abel’s replacement of righteousness; through Seth men began to call upon the name of the Lord and keep the commandments, while the line of Cain went on in evil, and that is why the Most High chose the line of Seth (Genesis 4:25-26). Cain was not made in God’s image, but Seth was, and Abel was: the line of the sons of God (Genesis 5:3; Luke 3:38). The wickedness is always around, and the righteous is born within the evil, always.

cases.name: Cain
cases.charge: Bringing fruit of the ground when he knew the Most High required animal sacrifice; growing bitter under correction and refusing to repent; and murdering his brother Abel
cases.summary: Cain was the firstborn of Adam and Eve after they were cast out of the garden, a tiller of the ground and a man of the field (Genesis 4:1-2). He knew the Most High required animal sacrifice, and in process of time he brought fruit of the ground (Genesis 4:3-5). He lured his brother out to the field under the guise of brotherhood and slew him, then lied to the Lord and took no accountability (Genesis 4:8-9). Cursed from the earth and marked, he looked different, for the melanin was gone.
offenseFull: Cain was born first, just like Esau, a tiller of the ground who spent most of his time in the field; Abel was a shepherd (Genesis 4:1-2).

Cain knew that the Most High required animal sacrifice, because the sacrificial law was ordained when Adam and Eve were clothed with skins; his father taught him sacrifice (Genesis 3:21; Genesis 9:5). In process of time, gradually, Cain grew tired of bringing animals and came to resent offering to the Lord, and he brought fruit of the ground (Genesis 4:3). Under the law fruits could be offered, but what Cain brought was not the first; he did just enough, and not what was required (Deuteronomy 18:4). It was also about election, not about works, as with Jacob and Esau (Romans 9:13).

The Lord had not respect to his offering, and Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell (Genesis 4:5). What started it was correction: Cain forsook the way over a process of time, the correction became grievous, and that grievous spirit nourished the bitterness until it grew into murder (Proverbs 15:10).

The Most High was calling Cain to repent (Genesis 4:6-7). Sin, which is the devil, Satan, lies at the door in your mind; if Cain would not do well, he would become subject to Satan, and Satan would rule over him and use him as a vessel.

Abel was a prophet, and when Cain talked with him Abel was trying to get him to repent (Matthew 23:35). Cain acted like his friend, talked with him over a period of time, and lured him out to the field, and there he rose up and slew him (Genesis 4:8). He killed Abel savagely, not with a single quick blow. Cain was the first recorded hater in the scriptures, of that wicked one, Satan’s child in spirit (1 John 3:12). Satan murdered nobody; who killed in the beginning was Cain, and Christ called him the devil (John 8:44).

Asked where his brother was, Cain lied, which alone was disrespect, and then answered the Lord with contempt for his brother (Genesis 4:9). That is no accountability, and Esau shows the same today, when the slave trade is denied, blamed on the enslaved, or renamed a migration.
judgmentFull: His brother’s blood cried from the ground, and Cain was cursed from the earth (Genesis 4:10-11). Adam was made from the dust of the ground; the Lord cursed that ground and cursed Cain, and when that ground was cursed its colour changed, and so did his. The ground would not yield him her strength (Genesis 4:12), and the curse reaches his descendants: the nations of Esau, the so-called white man, have not stayed in Europe for their resources but have gone to the Americas and to Africa, where Israel is, to acquire them.

Made a fugitive and a vagabond, he was brought to the same low estate spoken of the serpent (Genesis 3:14). A vagabond wanders and sleeps where he does not belong; a fugitive escapes from the law and has not served his sentence; and that is the lot of Cain and his descendants.

Hidden from the Lord’s face, Cain was dealt with by God no more, but by Satan; he was a heathen now, and that curse fell upon him and his children (Genesis 4:13-14). Cain was not made in God’s image; Seth was, Abel was; God made him, but he was not God’s son; he was another’s son, of that wicked one (Genesis 5:3).

The mark set upon Cain changed him; at the beginning he looked like everybody else (Genesis 4:15). He looked different because the melanin was gone; in the so-called white man today the blood shows through the skin, red like the blood Cain shed in that ground. The mark is also sin, which preserves the wicked until their judgment (Job 10:14). No one had to touch him or avenge Abel’s blood; the Lord would deal with him himself, and his final curse, utter destruction, was deferred to a set time (Luke 21:24).

He went out from the presence of the Lord to the land of Nod, the same place the cherubims were with that flaming sword, and there he dealt with the devil (Genesis 4:16; Genesis 3:24). He found his wife there and built a city, and a city is not built for three people; he called it after his son Enoch, as the wicked call their lands after their own names, and Nimrod built on top of the ruins of Cain’s city (Genesis 4:17; Psalms 49:11; Genesis 10:8-10).

Cain’s line handled music, very powerful in the wrong hands, and Tubalcain’s brass and iron were the first weapons: power over entertainment and power over weaponry, warfare, which is Esau’s blessing too (Genesis 4:21-22). The Most High created the smith and the waster to destroy (Isaiah 54:16); the waster is nuclear fire, and God will end them with the weapon he let them make (Zechariah 14:12).

Cain was killed in the end, by the same violence with which he killed Abel (Wisdom of Solomon 10:3). The sons of God mingled with the daughters of men, Cain’s children, Cain gained dominion on the earth, and Cain’s evil was the cause the earth was flooded (Genesis 6:1-13; Wisdom of Solomon 10:4). Esau was the firstborn like Cain and a man of the field like Cain, came out red with that pigmentation gone, and purposed to slay his brother: same spirit (Genesis 25:25; Genesis 27:41). Colour alone does not settle it: a man can be black and still be of the seed of Cain.

cases.name: Lamech
cases.charge: Taking two wives, the first in scripture; slaying a young man with the weapon his son made; boasting of seventy and sevenfold vengeance when he knew the commandment against killing
cases.summary: Lamech of Cain’s line took two wives, the first time scripture records a man taking multiple wives, and it was the sons of the wicked who did it (Genesis 4:19). His sons held the trades of that line: cattle and produce, music, and weapons (Genesis 4:20-22). He killed a young man with a weapon his own son made, and boasted of seventy and sevenfold, complete vengeance (Genesis 4:23-24). He knew the commandment against killing was in force in his day. No sentence on him is recorded.
offenseFull: Lamech, of Cain’s line through Enoch and Methusael, took two wives, Adah and Zillah, the first time you read about a man taking multiple wives, and it is the sons of the wicked who did it; in the beginning it was one wife, and the sons of God in Genesis 5 are not read of taking multiple wives (Genesis 4:19; Genesis 2:24).

Adah bare Jabal, the father of such as dwell in tents and have cattle: power over resources and produce, dealing with pricing and unrighteousness (Genesis 4:20). Jubal was the father of all such as handle the harp and organ, and it was not holy music but songs about murder, drugs, debauchery and adultery, which is what was going on in that city (Genesis 4:21). Zillah bare Tubalcain, an instructor of every artificer in brass and iron: the first weapons you read of, and not regular weapons but high level weaponry, as his line creates weapons of mass destruction today (Genesis 4:22). So Cain had power over entertainment and power over weaponry and warfare; Esau was a man of war, and that was Esau’s blessing, and Cain’s blessing too (Genesis 27:40).

Lamech told his wives that he had slain a man to his wounding and a young man to his hurt (Genesis 4:23). He slew a young and strong man with the weapon his son had made him. Lamech was murdering men; Satan was working with the sons of the wicked. He knew the commandment thou shalt not kill was in force in his day; that is why he appealed to Cain’s sevenfold and claimed seventy and sevenfold for himself: they knew the commandments during that time (Genesis 4:24; Genesis 4:15). Seventy and sevenfold in the mouth of a murderer means complete, total, utter vengeance (Genesis 4:24). They did not kill only the one man who hurt Lamech; they wiped out that whole lineage, the family and the city, by the weaponry that line held, and that is how Esau moves. Murder became normal and celebrated.
judgmentFull: No sentence on Lamech is recorded; the account turns to Seth, while the line of Cain went on in evil and wickedness (Genesis 4:25-26). Lamech of Cain fathered Tubalcain, a son of destruction and death; Lamech of Seth’s line fathered Noah, a son of righteousness, purity and deliverance, who would spare life on the ark (Genesis 5:28-29). Good is set against evil and life against death, and the works of the Most High are two and two: Cain had his Lamech and his Enoch, and Seth’s line had its Lamech and its Enoch (Ecclesiasticus 33:14-15).

Lamech’s seventy and sevenfold was complete vengeance; Christ’s seventy times seven is complete, boundless, endless mercy to the Israelites who believe, and he told Peter to extend the same (Matthew 18:21-22). That spirit of perpetual hatred is still working in the earth. The spirit of Cain passed to Esau: Cain murdered his brother by deceit, his line made weapons, and Lamech boasted of killing; Esau lives by the sword and comforts himself with plans to kill Jacob (Genesis 27:40-41).

cases.name: Enoch
cases.charge: Walking with God three hundred years as a commandment keeper, and prophesying of the destruction to come upon the ungodly
cases.summary: Enoch was the seventh from Adam in the line of the sons of God, traced from Seth to Noah (Genesis 5:18-24; Jude 1:14). He walked with God, which means he was a commandment keeper, and in his time he prophesied of the destruction to come (Jude 1:14-15). He was an example of repentance, and the Most High took him up, as he took Elijah, so that he did not taste death (Ecclesiasticus 44:16; Genesis 5:24).
offenseFull: Chapter 5 is the direct lineage of Adam, and that lineage is the sons of God of chapter 6; Christ’s lineage on his mother’s side runs back through Seth to Adam, the son of God (Genesis 5:1-3; Luke 3:36-38). The chapter names one son in each generation because it traces the line of the sons of God: those children birthed prophets, and among the other sons and daughters there was wickedness. Cain also had a son named Enoch: there was a righteous Enoch and a wicked Enoch (Genesis 4:17; Ecclesiasticus 33:14-15).

Enoch walked with God three hundred years after he begat Methuselah, and begat sons and daughters (Genesis 5:21-24). Walking with God does not mean long walks and talks; it means walking in his ways and keeping his commandments, the charge given to Abram to walk before the Most High and be perfect (Genesis 17:1). Enoch was a commandment keeper, and he could not have been one if there were no commandments in his time; the Lord would not have flooded the earth if there were no standard for life. While the people of his time were doing wickedness, Enoch prophesied that the Lord would come with his saints to execute judgment upon the ungodly for their deeds and their hard speeches against him (Jude 1:14-15). The same word was preached by Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech and Noah to the wicked of their people mingled among the other people, and the flood came and killed them. He was an example of repentance to all generations, meaning he was involved in wickedness too, and repented (Ecclesiasticus 44:16).
judgmentFull: Enoch was not, for God took him: the Most High took him up, and he did not taste death, as Elijah was taken up by a whirlwind into heaven and Christ was taken up and received in a cloud (Genesis 5:24; 2 Kings 2:9-11; Acts 1:9). God took him up in a chariot; he did not die as other mortals die. He pleased God and was beloved of him, and living among sinners he was taken away speedily: the Lord took Enoch so that the world around him would not corrupt him, which shows how wicked it was in that time (Wisdom of Solomon 4:10-11). The people saw it and did not understand that his grace and mercy is with his saints and that he has respect unto his chosen: there was a chosen lineage from Adam down through Enoch to the Israelites (Wisdom of Solomon 4:15).

By faith he was translated, and before his translation he had the testimony that he pleased God; without faith it is impossible to please him, and Enoch’s faith was so sincere that his everyday walk showed he loved God (Hebrews 11:5-6). He is praised among the famous men, the fathers that begat us (Ecclesiasticus 44:1, 16).

cases.name: The sons of God and the giants
cases.charge: The sons of God, the lineage of Adam, leaving their first estate to take wives of the daughters of men, of the other nations, against the law already known
cases.summary: The sons of God are the lineage of Adam laid out in Genesis 5, and the daughters of men were of the other nations (Genesis 6:1-2). The law against marrying into the other nations began here in Genesis and Moses reiterated it, yet the sons of God took wives of all which they chose, dwelt in Cain’s city and learned his ways (Genesis 6:2; Deuteronomy 7:3). The giants came of that mixing (Genesis 6:4). These are the angels which kept not their first estate, reserved by the Most High unto the judgment of the great day, which has not yet come (Jude 1:6).
offenseFull: The men who began to multiply on the face of the earth were of the other nations, not the direct descendants of Adam; the sons of God are the lineage of Adam in chapter 5, and that is the distinction between the sons of God and the daughters of men (Genesis 6:1-2; Genesis 5:1-3). They are not angels coming down: the Lord said his spirit would not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh, and before we were called Israelites we were called the sons of God (Genesis 6:3; 1 John 3:1). The daughters of men came from Cain’s line: of Cain, Eve said she had gotten a man from the Lord, and Cain was not made in Adam’s image as Seth was (Genesis 4:1; Genesis 5:3). They were also the other children of Adam, outside the chosen line (2 Esdras 3:7).

The sons of God saw that the daughters of men were fair and took them wives of all which they chose: that is interracial marriage, and we started to marry the women of other nations (Genesis 6:2). All this took place within Cain’s city, Enoch; the sons of God went to dwell in it and learn his ways, as the sons of God dwell in Esau’s city today and learn his ways. That was the sin: leaving your race to have children with other people.

The giants came because the sons of God, who had that DNA from being made in the image of God, took wives of the other nations, which was forbidden, and their children became mighty men of renown (Genesis 6:4). The renown is the fame and the power; the might is the wickedness they did, as with Nimrod the mighty hunter, for they intermingled with Cain (Genesis 10:9). They are the titans and high giants of Judith, of great stature and expert in war, whom the Lord did not choose (Judith 16:7; Baruch 3:26-28).
judgmentFull: The Lord said his spirit would not always strive with man and shortened his lifespan to a hundred and twenty years; in chapter 5 the forefathers lived seven, eight and nine hundred years (Genesis 6:3). He was angry with his sons for marrying the daughters of men: because they wanted to be like the other people, they would die like them, for they were polluting his holy seed (Psalms 82:6-7).

The angels which kept not their first estate are these same men: another word for angel is messenger; they came from the lineage of Adam, and their first estate was sons of God; they are also the angels that sinned (Jude 1:6; 2 Peter 2:4-5). They left obeying God’s laws to deal with the women of the other nations, and did not stay according to his laws among themselves: that is leaving their own habitation. The chains of darkness are not angels tied up in the middle of the earth; they are darkness under sin, lies and deceit, and the spirits reserved in them will not wake up. The great day has not yet come, and those spirits are still here today: after the flood the same spirits came right back through the three sons, Shem, Ham and Japheth.

The earth was corrupt before God because the sons of God mingled with Cain’s children, and Cain gained dominion on the earth; it was filled with violence as Cain was violent, and for Cain’s cause the earth was drowned (Genesis 6:11-13; Wisdom of Solomon 10:4). The giants were destroyed by the flood (Baruch 3:28). The same word is preached today to the same wicked sons of God mixed with the same people, before the fire comes (2 Peter 3:7).

cases.name: Noah
cases.charge: Doing according to all that God commanded him, by faith; keeping the commandments before Moses, marrying his own kind, and preaching righteousness
cases.summary: Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord, a just man and perfect in his generations, who walked with God (Genesis 6:8-9). He was himself a son of God, and out of all the sons of God of his time who mingled with the daughters of men, Noah did not; he married his own kind (Tobit 4:12). By faith he built an ark for rain that had never been seen, and preached righteousness for around a hundred years (Genesis 6:22; 2 Peter 2:5). He knew the clean beasts from the unclean because he was keeping the laws, and with his household he was left as a remnant to the earth (Genesis 7:2; Ecclesiasticus 44:17).
offenseFull: Noah was righteous, perfect and just, which means keeping God’s commandments: the commandments Seth kept, he kept also; and walking with God means walking in his ways, as Abraham kept the Lord’s charge, commandments, statutes and laws just as Noah did (Genesis 6:9; Genesis 17:1; Genesis 26:5). He was a holy man and a just man, keeping the laws of God long before Moses. Noah was also a son of God, and out of all the sons of God of that time doing wickedness with Cain’s children, Noah did not (Genesis 6:1-5). He did not marry the daughters of men; he married his own kind, a daughter of God, and his sons’ wives were their own kind, as all the fathers from the beginning took wives of their own kindred (Tobit 4:12). He was found perfect and righteous, taken in exchange for the world in the time of wrath, and left as a remnant unto the earth (Ecclesiasticus 44:17-18).

Noah did all that the Most High commanded him by faith: up to that time rain had never been seen, for a mist went up and watered the ground, and it takes faith to build an ark for a thing that has never happened (Genesis 6:22; Genesis 2:5-6; Genesis 7:4). Faith is the evidence of things not seen, and with Noah the thing not seen was rain; building the ark was his works, proving his faith, for faith without works is dead (Hebrews 11:1, 7; James 2:20). He was five hundred years old when his sons were born and six hundred when the flood came, so he preached for around a hundred years (Genesis 5:32; Genesis 7:6). While the ark was preparing he was a preacher of righteousness, a teacher of the law, telling his people to repent, and the longsuffering of the Most High waited for them to repent (2 Peter 2:5; 1 Peter 3:20). They scoffed and thought he was playing as he built the boat, and they did not listen (2 Peter 3:3-4).

He took the clean beasts by sevens and the unclean by two (Genesis 7:2-3). The dietary law was not yet instituted, but the Most High had already defined the clean and the unclean, and Moses reiterated that law; Noah knew the difference because he was keeping the laws, the commandments, and that is how he walked with God and was found righteous and perfect (Leviticus 11:46-47).
judgmentFull: The Lord shut him in, because of what Noah would hear outside, for a man has a soft spot; they had a hundred years to repent and were warned (Genesis 7:16). Noah had to sit and hear the screaming and the begging, his own siblings among them, until he heard nothing more. Eight souls were saved; the ones in the water died. Of all that dwelt in the world only Noah and his household were left, of whom came all righteous men, through Shem’s seed to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and the Israelites (1 Peter 3:20; 2 Esdras 3:11). Christ opens and no man shuts, and shuts and no man opens: repentance is open now, and once the door is closed no one can open it (Revelation 3:7).

Noah built an altar and offered of every clean beast and every clean fowl, and the Most High smelled a sweet savour and said he would not again curse the ground for man’s sake (Genesis 8:20-21). Noah, Daniel and Job delivered their own souls by their righteousness, and so did Noah, his wife, his sons and their wives (Ezekiel 14:14). An everlasting covenant was made with him that all flesh should perish no more by a flood, and the bow in the cloud, bent by the hands of the Most High, is its token (Genesis 9:9-15; Ecclesiasticus 43:11-12). The world has taken that bow and turned it into the symbol of sodomy, and the great city is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt (Revelation 11:8). As he swore that the waters of Noah would no more go over the earth, he will never put Israel in captivity again once we are delivered: this is the last time (Isaiah 54:9-10).

The laws in these chapters stand from before Moses: replenish the earth with righteous children, for one just child is better than a thousand ungodly; eat no flesh with the blood; whoso sheds man’s blood, by man shall his blood be shed (Genesis 9:1-6; Ecclesiasticus 16:1-3). Noah drank too much after the flood, but he remained righteous: a just man falls seven times and rises up again (Genesis 9:20-23; Proverbs 24:16). Before it was water; next time it is fire (2 Peter 3:9-10). As Noah prepared the ark to the saving of his house, we must prepare our households for when Christ comes back with the same faith, for as the days of Noah were, so shall the coming of the Son of man be; we have to put on the spirit of Noah (Matthew 24:37-39; Hebrews 11:7).

cases.name: The generation of the Flood
cases.charge: Despising the commandments and walking after their own will; the sons of God taking wives of the daughters of men until the earth was corrupt and filled with violence
cases.summary: When men began to multiply, the sons of God, the lineage of Adam, took them wives of the daughters of men, which was forbidden, and the children became mighty men of renown, and wicked (Genesis 6:1-4). Every people walked after their own will and despised the commandments, and the earth was filled with violence, for Cain had gained dominion on the earth (2 Esdras 3:8; Genesis 6:11). Noah preached for a hundred years while the ark was preparing; then the Lord shut him in, and the first rain came with destruction (Genesis 7:16-23).
offenseFull: The men who began to multiply on the earth were of the other nations, not the direct descendants of Adam; the sons of God are the lineage of Adam through Seth, and the law against marrying into the other nations began here (Genesis 6:1-2; Luke 3:38; Deuteronomy 7:3). The daughters of men came from Cain’s line. The sons of God are not angels coming down, for the Lord said that man also is flesh, and he shortened man’s lifespan to a hundred and twenty years (Genesis 6:3).

The children born to them became mighty men which were of old, men of renown: powerful, fierce, renowned fighters, but wicked, because they intermingled with Cain (Genesis 6:4). The angels which kept not their first estate are these same men, whose first estate was sons of God, reserved unto judgment (Jude 1:6). The sons of God came to dwell in the city Cain built and to follow his ways, as the sons of God today mix with Esau, dwelling in his city and learning his ways (Genesis 4:17).

Every imagination of the thoughts of man’s heart was only evil continually (Genesis 6:5). Every people walked after their own will and despised the commandments of the Most High, which means the commandments were around then; that is how Noah knew the clean from the unclean (2 Esdras 3:8; Genesis 7:2). The earth was filled with violence through them, and that them goes back to Cain’s seed: Cain gained dominion on the earth, and the earth was filled with violence just as Cain was violent (Genesis 6:11-13).

Noah was a preacher of righteousness, telling his people to repent while the ark was preparing, and the longsuffering of the Most High waited a hundred years for them to repent (2 Peter 2:5; 1 Peter 3:20). They did not listen, and scoffed at Noah building a boat for rain that had never been seen (2 Peter 3:3-4). They were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage until Noah entered the ark, and there was no more chance to repent (Matthew 24:37-39).
judgmentFull: The Lord shut him in (Genesis 7:16). The people cried to be let in, and the Lord closed the door himself; they had a hundred years and were warned. Repentance is open now, and once that door is closed no one can open it (Revelation 3:7).

It had never rained on the earth before, and when the rain came it came with destruction (Genesis 2:5-6; Genesis 7:11). This was the first time the Most High destroyed the earth for the wickedness that was being done: the flood came because they despised the commandments, and destruction came because of sin (Genesis 7:21-23). The breath of life is twofold, the commandments given to Adam and the breathing life; everything on the dry land that breathed died, and the fish were not touched (2 Esdras 3:5; Proverbs 7:2).

As death was to Adam, so was the flood to these; only Noah and his household were left, of whom came all righteous men, through Shem’s seed to the Israelites (2 Esdras 3:10-11). Cain’s evil was the cause for which the earth was drowned (Wisdom of Solomon 10:4). After the flood those same spirits came right back through the three sons, Shem, Ham and Japheth, for there is no new thing under the sun.

The bow is the token that the waters shall no more become a flood, and the earth which is now is reserved unto fire against the day of judgment (Genesis 9:11-15; 2 Peter 3:7). The same word Noah preached to the wicked of his people mingled among the other people is preached today to the same people, before fire. As the earth was filled with violence in the days of Noah, so it is today: because of the blood shed on the earth by Esau, the so-called white man, the Lord will intervene again and destroy Cain’s descendants, with fire this time (Matthew 24:37).

cases.name: Ham and the curse on Canaan
cases.charge: Seeing the nakedness of his father and mocking him, and not covering him, against the laws concerning nakedness
cases.summary: Noah, still perfect and righteous, drank of the wine with a heavy heart, for everyone he knew outside his house had drowned (Genesis 9:20-21). Ham saw the nakedness of his father and did not cover him; he mocked him and told his brothers, while Shem and Japheth covered their father without looking, for the commandments concerning nakedness were being applied (Genesis 9:22-23). The Lord revealed it to Noah, and Noah cursed Canaan to be a servant of servants: the curse was servitude, not black skin, and the Messiah and the righteous seed would come through Shem (Genesis 9:24-26).
offenseFull: Noah began to be a husbandman, planted a vineyard, drank of the wine and was uncovered within his tent (Genesis 9:20-21). He was still perfect and righteous: a just man falleth seven times and riseth up again, and one fall does not undo righteousness (Proverbs 24:16). Understand his heart: he preached repentance for around a hundred years, and everyone he knew outside his house drowned (2 Peter 2:5). Strong drink is for him that is ready to perish, and wine for those of heavy hearts; Noah drank too much, but he remained righteous in the eyes of the Most High (Proverbs 31:6-7).

Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father and told his two brethren without, and Shem and Japheth went backward and covered their father without looking (Genesis 9:22-23). The commandments concerning nakedness were already being applied; Leviticus 18 opens those laws, and the brothers knew the law not to look upon the nakedness of their father (Leviticus 18:7). Ham did not lie with his father, as some books teach; he laughed at his father and mocked him. Shem and Japheth kept another law: they let their father know, because a witness who has seen or known a sin and does not utter it shall bear his iniquity, and Noah had taught them the laws (Leviticus 5:1).
judgmentFull: Noah was asleep, so how did he know what his younger son had done (Genesis 9:24)? The Most High speaks to man in a dream, in a vision of the night, and reveals his secret unto his servants the prophets; Noah was a preacher of righteousness, and the Lord told him (Job 33:14-16; Amos 3:7).

Noah did not curse Ham; he cursed Canaan, a servant of servants unto his brethren (Genesis 9:25). The curse was to be a servant, not black skin: they were all black from the time Adam was formed of the dust, Noah, Shem, Ham and Japheth, there is no scripture that Japheth turned white, and the first time a change of colour is read is with Esau (Genesis 2:7). There was never a curse of Ham, and never a curse of black skin; the scriptures do not teach that black people are black because they come from Ham.

Blessed be the Lord God of Shem: it was revealed that the Messiah and the righteous seed would come through Shem, for Noah was a prophet and already knew the chosen race was coming through Shem (Genesis 9:26). Israel comes out of Shem, and Canaan shall be his servant; Japheth would be enlarged and dwell in the tents of Shem, the Israelites, for everything belongs to Shem (Genesis 9:27). Whatever a servant owns belongs to his master, which is why the children of Israel were not robbers when they took the land of Canaan; the Canaanites are servants, and what they have belongs to Israel. The servant of servants also looks to the time when the Israelites rule the world, when the children of Israel will have servants (Joel 3:8).

Shem, Ham and Japheth went forth out of the ark and the whole earth was overspread from them: Ham dwelt in what is called Africa, Shem in the land toward Arabia, and Japheth went into Europe (Genesis 9:18-19). The sons of Ham are Cush, which is Ethiopia; Mizraim, which is Egypt; Phut, which is Libya; and Canaan, whose land is where Jerusalem sits, so the land of Israel is part of Africa (Genesis 10:6). The Israelites are of Shem, not of Ham; the children of Israel are Shemites scattered among the children of Ham in Africa, and Shem is the father of all the children of Eber, from whom the name Hebrew comes (Genesis 10:21).

cases.offense: Noah began to be a husbandman, planted a vineyard, drank of the wine and was uncovered within his tent (Genesis 9:20-21). He was still perfect and righteous: a just man falleth seven times and riseth up again, and one fall does not undo righteousness (Proverbs 24:16). Understand his heart: he preached repentance for around a hundred years, and everyone he knew outside his house drowned (2 Peter 2:5). Strong drink is for him that is ready to perish, and wine for those of heavy hearts; Noah drank too much, but he remained righteous in the eyes of the Most High (Proverbs 31:6-7).
cases.judgment: Noah was asleep, so how did he know what his younger son had done (Genesis 9:24)? The Most High speaks to man in a dream, in a vision of the night, and reveals his secret unto his servants the prophets; Noah was a preacher of righteousness, and the Lord told him (Job 33:14-16; Amos 3:7).

cases.name: The builders of Babel
cases.charge: Building a city and a tower under Nimrod in malice against the One who sent the flood, to make themselves a name and be one people in their own counsel, lest they be scattered abroad
cases.summary: Cush begat Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the Lord, meaning he was against the Lord, and the beginning of his kingdom was Babel in the land of Shinar, built on top of the ruins of Cain’s city (Genesis 10:8-10). One people with one language, they built a tower so they would not be scattered abroad and to make themselves a name, with the fear of the flood still on them, and the tower was raised in malice against the One who sent the flood (Genesis 11:1-4). The Most High confounded their language and scattered them, and sent every family back to where it was supposed to be (Genesis 11:5-9).
offenseFull: Cush begat Nimrod: these are Hamites, and after the flood the first ruling empire on the earth was Kush, the children of Ham, as before the flood Cain built the first city (Genesis 10:8). He began to be a mighty one in the earth, a mighty hunter before the Lord; mighty hunter means he hunted after men and was an evil ruler, and he hunted the souls of men, a stumbling block between them and the one true God, for men worshipped him as a god (Genesis 10:9; Micah 7:2). The beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar, which is Iraq, and out of that land Asshur, the Assyrians, built Nineveh (Genesis 10:10-11). History records Nimrod as the first king there and the first mortal deified at his death, the father of the gods; Nimrod, his queen Semiramis and her child Tammuz became the first pagan trinity, worshipped under other names through every nation, and Sunday sacredness, Christmas and Easter have their origin in that Babylonian sun worship. The Sumerians called Erech Unug, as in Enoch; older scholars of Assyria identified Cain’s city of Enoch with Unug, so Nimrod built on top of the ruins of Cain’s city, where the evil was, and that is why the Lord told Abraham to leave there (Genesis 4:17).

The whole earth was of one language, and they journeyed from the east to the plain of Shinar, in Babylon (Genesis 11:1-2). They built the tower so they would not be scattered abroad; the fear of the flood was still on them, and they wanted to make themselves a name (Genesis 11:3-4). The tower was not built to glorify the Most High; they knew he sent the flood, and they built it out of malice, bitter against the One who sent the flood, wanting to escape any destruction that comes. That was the wicked conspiracy of the nations, rivalry and sedition against the Most High (Wisdom of Solomon 10:5). It was not an ordinary tower of brick and slime but a technological tower, for the Lord said the people were one and nothing would be restrained from them which they had imagined to do (Genesis 11:6). All they were doing was not under the umbrella of God; it was their own counsel and their own self will.

Unity is an agreement on God’s laws. Babel was unity out of rebellion, unity with self will against the Lord’s will, as the kings of the earth set themselves and the rulers take counsel together against the Lord and against his anointed (Psalms 2:1-3). Everyone that is proud in heart is an abomination to the Lord, and though hand join in hand, he shall not be unpunished (Proverbs 16:5). The people being one was not going to produce righteousness: nothing would be restrained from what they imagined to do, and it would be evil.
judgmentFull: The Lord came down, confounded their language that they might not understand one another’s speech, and scattered them abroad upon the face of all the earth, and they left off to build the city, because it was out of order and not in the Lord’s will at all (Genesis 11:7-8). Babel means confusion (Genesis 11:9).

There has never been a doctrine in the scriptures of all nations holding hands as one. The Most High divided to the nations their inheritance and separated the sons of Adam, setting the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel; Jacob is his portion (Deuteronomy 32:7-9). After Babel the Most High sent every family back to where it was supposed to be: Ham to his place, Shem to his, Japheth to his, every one after his tongue (Genesis 10:5, 20, 31). The sons of Japheth settled what became Europe; Ham inhabited what is known as Africa; and the Israelites are of Shem (Genesis 10:2-6, 21).

The man of sin opposes this: he exalts himself above all that is called God, gathers all nations to himself as one, and deifies himself, making God and the Messiah after his own image, the same thing Nimrod did in the land of Shinar and the spirit of Nimrod all over again (2 Thessalonians 2:3-4). The Most High likens his judgment to a ring, and the same things that happened in the time of ancient Babylon happen now in Babylon the great (2 Esdras 5:42). Babylon was the first, and it ends with Babylon again, Mystery, Babylon the Great, the mother of harlots: Babylon reigned over Israel, and Babylon reigns over Israel again (Revelation 17:3-5).

cases.name: Abraham
cases.charge: Obeying the Lord’s voice, going out when he was called, and keeping his charge, his commandments, his statutes, and his laws
cases.summary: The Most High called Abram alone out of Ur of the Chaldees, ancient Babylon, out of his country, his kindred and his father’s house, and he went (Genesis 12:1; Isaiah 51:2). He believed the Lord, and it was counted to him for righteousness, and his faith showed itself in his works: at ninety and nine he circumcised every male of his house the selfsame day he received the commandment, and when the Lord demanded Isaac he rose up early in the morning and went (Genesis 15:6; Genesis 17:23-27; Genesis 22:3). The Lord’s own account of him is the law kept: Abraham obeyed his voice and kept his charge, his commandments, his statutes and his laws (Genesis 26:5).
offenseFull: The Most High called Abram to get out of his country, from his kindred and from his father’s house; he called him alone, and blessed him, and increased him (Genesis 12:1; Isaiah 51:2). Ur of the Chaldees is ancient Babylon, where Cain built and Nimrod built on top of it, and the Lord told Abraham to leave because it was so evil. Do not let your kindred hold you back from being blessed and increased; when the Most High calls you out you have to go, and confessing Christ before men sets a man at variance against his own household for the truth’s sake (Matthew 10:32-37). In thee shall all families of the earth be blessed is not talking about everybody: the children of the prophets and of the covenant are Israel, and Israel would be scattered into all nations of the earth, so through Abraham’s seed the kindreds of the earth are blessed in scattered Israel being turned from their iniquities (Genesis 12:2-3; Acts 3:25-26; Amos 2:11). The nations that treated Abraham right were blessed, their crops grew and their animals multiplied, though that did not mean they would get the kingdom of heaven; anybody that put a hand against Abraham was destroyed.

Abram believed the Lord, and it was counted to him for righteousness (Genesis 15:5-6). Righteousness is immortal, and righteousness is defined by the law: it shall be our righteousness if we observe to do all these commandments, and Abram’s faith showed itself in his works (Deuteronomy 6:25; Wisdom of Solomon 1:15; Romans 4:1-3). His seed would be a stranger in a land not theirs and be afflicted four hundred years; that prophecy was fulfilled in Egypt, where the sojourning was four hundred and thirty years, ending the selfsame day, and they came out with great substance, spoiling Egypt as they left (Genesis 15:13-14; Exodus 12:35-41). This verse is not the doctrine about America and 1619; Israel is yet this day in captivity and scattered, and the twelve tribes scattered among the nations today, the people called Blacks, Hispanics and Native Americans, are the seed this covenant history belongs to (Baruch 3:8).

At ninety and nine he was commanded to walk before the Most High and be perfect, and there is no age excuse; perfect means to walk in his statutes and keep his commandments (Genesis 17:1; 1 Kings 8:61). Circumcision is the token of the covenant, a seal of the righteousness of the faith he had yet being uncircumcised; he believed and obeyed first, and the selfsame day he received the commandment he circumcised every male of his house, which is the righteous example (Genesis 17:10-14, 23-27; Romans 4:11). When the Most High said, Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac, Abraham rose up early in the morning and went, with no hesitation and no debating with the word; the fear of God is proved in obedience, and he accounted that God was able to raise Isaac up even from the dead (Genesis 22:1-12; Hebrews 11:17-19). When his brother was taken captive he armed his trained servants, three hundred and eighteen born in his own house, and pursued them; Abram was no weak and no passive man (Genesis 14:14). The Lord knew him, that he would command his children and his household after him to keep the way of the Lord, and his whole household would keep God’s commandments (Genesis 18:19).
judgmentFull: When the Most High began dealing with Abram on a covenant level his name was changed to Abraham, a father of many nations, and kings would come out of him (Genesis 17:4-6). Father of many nations does not mean everybody is spiritually a child of Abraham: the same promise passed to Jacob, named Israel, and the blessing of all men and the covenant rested upon the head of Jacob and were divided among the twelve tribes, and out of that seed comes Christ, the King of kings (Genesis 35:10-11; Ecclesiasticus 44:19-23). The covenant is with Abraham’s seed after him, and seed is literal offspring, not a spiritual metaphor; Israel is the nation that carries the seed of Abraham (Genesis 17:7; Isaiah 41:8). Ishmael received a blessing, but the covenant passed to Isaac, for in Isaac shall thy seed be called, and the children of the promise are counted for the seed (Genesis 17:20-21; Romans 9:7-9). His seed shall possess the gate of his enemies, the remnant of Edom and of all the heathen, and that is why all nations cannot be inside this covenant; in his seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed, and those nations are the twelve tribes (Genesis 22:17-18; Amos 9:11-12; Numbers 24:18).

Abraham kept the laws of God before Moses, and in Egypt he showed their customs to be vain and void of truth, for the law of God is the truth (Psalms 119:142). He was admired there as a very wise man, because keeping the laws of God is how wisdom is gained, and he communicated to the Egyptians arithmetic and the science of astronomy, which came from the Chaldeans into Egypt and from there to the Greeks. The oath sworn to him stood because Abraham obeyed the voice of the Lord and kept his charge, his commandments, his statutes and his laws, the past tense of what he was doing that proved his faith; he kept the laws, statutes and commandments just as Noah did (Genesis 26:5).

cases.name: Pharaoh and Abimelech, who took Sarah
cases.charge: Taking another man’s wife into the king’s house
cases.summary: Twice Abraham said of Sarah, She is my sister, for fear the men of the place would kill him for his wife’s sake, and twice a king took her into his house (Genesis 12:11-15; Genesis 20:1-2). The Lord plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, and to Abimelech God came in a dream: he was but a dead man, for the woman was a man’s wife (Genesis 12:17; Genesis 20:3). Adultery was sin in Genesis, way before the law was written at Sinai, and the Most High plagues a household over the prophet’s wife; he does not play about that.
offenseFull: A famine sent Abram into Egypt, as it would send Jacob later (Genesis 12:10). Sarai was around the same age as Abram, about ten years apart, and she was still a very fair woman to look upon in her sixties; the saying began at Egypt, that they would kill him but save her alive, so she was to say she was his sister, and she was taken into Pharaoh’s house (Genesis 12:11-15). Abraham said it again in Gerar, and Sarah was still that fair to look upon even at ninety, and Abimelech king of Gerar sent and took her (Genesis 20:1-2).

Technically she was his sister, the daughter of his father but not of his mother, who became his wife, and the sister saying was their agreement in every strange land (Genesis 20:12-13). The laws that curse him that lieth with his sister, the daughter of his father or of his mother, and call it a wicked thing, were written by Moses some four hundred years after Abraham, so there is no contradiction in the Bible (Deuteronomy 27:22; Leviticus 20:17). Brother and sister are also used of those from your tribe and as a term of endearment: Lot, Abram’s brother’s son, is called his brother because Lot was a Hebrew as well, as Christ was called the son of David, being of the same tribe (Genesis 14:12-16; Matthew 21:15).

God came to Abimelech in a dream: he was but a dead man, for the woman he had taken was a man’s wife (Genesis 20:3). Adultery was sin in Genesis, way before the seventh commandment was given, and the Most High said he withheld Abimelech from sinning against him (Genesis 20:6; Exodus 20:14). Abimelech had acted in the integrity of his heart, and the Most High withheld him from touching her; he was to restore the man his wife, for Abraham was a prophet and would pray for him (Genesis 20:5-7). Abimelech called it what it is, a great sin: adultery is one of the weightier matters, and there is no animal sacrifice that atones for it (Genesis 20:9). Abraham had thought, surely the fear of God is not in this place (Genesis 20:11).
judgmentFull: The Lord plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, and Pharaoh sent Abram away with his wife and all that he had; the Most High protected the household of Abram in Egypt (Genesis 12:17-20). There Abraham acquired Hagar (Genesis 12:16; Genesis 16:1).

Behind the scenes the Lord had fast closed up all the wombs of the house of Abimelech because of Sarah, and when Abraham prayed, God healed them (Genesis 20:17-18). The same happened with Pharaoh before: it happened both times she was taken. The Most High plagues a household over the prophet’s wife, and he does not play about that.

The Lord said he would bless them that bless Abraham and curse him that curseth him (Genesis 12:3). When Abimelech saw Sarah and took her, his house began to be plagued, and the Lord visited him to tell him that man was his prophet and that was his wife: whoever looked out for Abraham was all right, and whoever tried to curse Abraham was destroyed.

cases.name: Hagar, and the God who seeth
cases.charge: Returning to her mistress and submitting herself under her hands when the angel of the Lord sent her back
cases.summary: Hagar, Sarai’s Egyptian handmaid from the servants Pharaoh gave, was given to Abram, whose sole purpose was the seed, not multiple wives (Genesis 16:1-3). When she conceived she got high minded and stopped submitting, and when Sarai dealt hardly with her she fled (Genesis 16:4-6). The angel of the Lord found her by the fountain in the way to Shur and sent her back to submit herself under her mistress’s hands, and she humbled herself and went back; over her son he gave the word that he would be a wild man, his hand against every man, dwelling in the presence of all his brethren (Genesis 16:7-12).
offenseFull: Hagar was Sarai’s Egyptian handmaid, from the servants Pharaoh gave when Abraham was in Egypt (Genesis 16:1; Genesis 12:16). Sarai, restrained from bearing, gave her maid to Abram that she might obtain children by her (Genesis 16:2-3). When Hagar conceived, her mistress was despised in her eyes: she got high minded and stopped submitting because she carried Abram’s child, and grew very disrespectful to Sarai (Genesis 16:4). Sarai laid the wrong on Abram, and Abram answered that her maid was in her hand; he did not say my wife, for he had no attachment to Hagar, and his sole purpose was the seed, not multiple wives (Genesis 16:5-6). Abram kept the laws of the Most High, and this account is not to be used to justify taking multiple wives; the purpose was the promised inheritance, and Sarai dealt with her maid as mistress over her.

The angel of the Lord found Hagar by the fountain in the way to Shur and sent her back to return to her mistress and submit herself under her hands (Genesis 16:7-9). She was to stay in her place: Sarai was the mistress and she was the servant, and she was not to be arrogant. Humble yourself and go back.
judgmentFull: Her seed would be multiplied exceedingly, that it should not be numbered for multitude, and that goes into Ishmael: the multitude of Arabs all over the world today is that prophecy (Genesis 16:10). While the child was still in her womb she was told to call his name Ishmael, which means affliction heard, because the Lord had heard her affliction, and his name is important to future prophecy (Genesis 16:11). He would be a wild man, his hand against every man and every man’s hand against him, for he was a warrior skilful with the bow; that happened then, and it is also future prophecy concerning the Arabs (Genesis 16:12). Ishmael became the ancestor of the nomad desert tribes from the Sinai desert across the Negev to southern Jordan, and the Arabs venerate Ishmael as their forefather; they dwell in the presence of all their brethren to this day, nation beside nation through that whole region. She called the Lord that spoke to her the God who sees her, and the well was called Beer-lahai-roi (Genesis 16:13-14).

Abram was eighty six when Hagar bare Ishmael; Ishmael was Abram’s firstborn, but the covenant did not go to Ishmael, for the covenant goes through the twelve tribes of Israel (Genesis 16:15-16). Ishmael received a blessing, twelve princes and a great nation, but the covenant passed to Isaac, and Ishmael was born of the flesh, of Sarai’s plan, with no word from God ordaining it (Genesis 17:20-21). When Sarah saw the son of Hagar mocking Isaac, she said to cast out the bondwoman and her son, for the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with Isaac; it was grievous to Abraham, but God said to hearken unto her voice, for in Isaac shall thy seed be called, and Sarah was right (Genesis 21:9-12). Ishmael would still be made a nation, because he was Abraham’s seed (Genesis 21:13). Abraham gave Hagar bread and a bottle of water and sent her away with the child, though the Arabs speak of themselves as descendants of Abraham and of the Abrahamic religions (Genesis 21:14).

When the water was spent she cast the child under a shrub and wept, and God heard the voice of the lad and opened her eyes to a well of water; the lad could not die there, for the prophecy of chapter 16 stood over him (Genesis 21:15-19). Ishmael dwelt in the wilderness of Paran and became an archer, learning the skills of combat and war according to his nature, and his mother took him a wife out of Egypt (Genesis 21:20-21).

cases.judgment: Her seed would be multiplied exceedingly, that it should not be numbered for multitude, and that goes into Ishmael: the multitude of Arabs all over the world today is that prophecy (Genesis 16:10). While the child was still in her womb she was told to call his name Ishmael, which means affliction heard, because the Lord had heard her affliction, and his name is important to future prophecy (Genesis 16:11). He would be a wild man, his hand against every man and every man’s hand against him, for he was a warrior skilful with the bow; that happened then, and it is also future prophecy concerning the Arabs (Genesis 16:12). Ishmael became the ancestor of the nomad desert tribes from the Sinai desert across the Negev to southern Jordan, and the Arabs venerate Ishmael as their forefather; they dwell in the presence of all their brethren to this day, nation beside nation through that whole region. She called the Lord that spoke to her the God who sees her, and the well was called Beer-lahai-roi (Genesis 16:13-14).

cases.name: Sodom and Gomorrah
cases.charge: Pride, fulness of bread, abundance of idleness, and abomination; the whole city, old and young, compassing Lot’s house to know the two angels
cases.summary: The cry of Sodom and Gomorrah was great and their sin very grievous: pride, fulness of bread, abundance of idleness, no strengthening of the hand of the poor and needy, and abomination (Genesis 18:20; Ezekiel 16:49-50). The city was glorious and rich, and its people were filthy. The men of the city, old and young, from every quarter, compassed Lot’s house to know the two angels, not to greet them but to rape them (Genesis 19:4-5). When Lot entered into Zoar, the Lord rained brimstone and fire upon Sodom and Gomorrah (Genesis 19:23-25).
offenseFull: The Lord said the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah was great and their sin very grievous (Genesis 18:20-21). The iniquity of Sodom was pride, fulness of bread, and abundance of idleness; she strengthened not the hand of the poor and needy, was haughty, and committed abomination (Ezekiel 16:49-50). The men of Sodom were wicked and sinners before the Lord exceedingly: lawless, without principles, and given to sexual freedom, and that is why the city was overthrown (Genesis 13:13). It was not one sin alone: women were promiscuous, there was every kind of uncleanness, and everything was sexualized.

Lot lifted up his eyes and chose the plain of Jordan because it was well watered everywhere, even as the garden of the Lord, and pitched his tent toward Sodom; toward Sodom became in Sodom (Genesis 13:10-12; Genesis 14:12). It was not a regular place: the area was beautiful and glorious and the city was rich, but its people were filthy. The same iniquities fill the land that is spiritually called Sodom today: pride, wealth, idleness from morning to night, and abomination made law (Revelation 11:8). This place is spiritually Sodom because sodomy is legalized here.

Two angels came to Sodom at even, and before they lay down the men of the city, both old and young, all the people from every quarter, compassed Lot’s house and demanded the men, that they might know them (Genesis 19:1-5). To know in scripture is to lie with: of Rebekah it is written that no man had known her (Genesis 24:16). They came not to greet the angels but to rape them. Old and young means the young were in it, and for the old to raise no objection shows it was legal there: Sodom framed mischief by a law (Psalms 94:20).

Lot went out, shut the door after him, and begged them as brethren not to do so wickedly (Genesis 19:6-7). This is Genesis, long before Leviticus: sodomy was already wickedness and already unlawful before the law was written at Sinai (Leviticus 18:22; Leviticus 20:13). Sin has levels, and the deepest are called the depths of Satan (Revelation 2:24); Lot offered his two daughters rather than let them have the men, because this sin is another level (Genesis 19:8). They refused and said they would deal worse with him than with them; that is how inflamed the pride was (Genesis 19:9). Smitten with blindness, they still wearied themselves to find the door and would not go home; that is an evil spirit (Genesis 19:10-11).

The Most High told only Abraham what he would do (Genesis 18:17-21). Abraham negotiated because his nephew Lot dwelt in Sodom, from fifty righteous down to ten; below ten there was no more negotiating, and the Lord went his way (Genesis 18:23-33).
judgmentFull: The angel said he could do nothing until Lot had come to Zoar: the destruction waited on the righteous being brought out, as the angels hold the four winds until the servants of God are sealed (Genesis 19:22; Revelation 7:1-3).

The sun was risen upon the earth when Lot entered into Zoar, and the Lord rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire out of heaven, and overthrew those cities, all the plain, all the inhabitants, and that which grew upon the ground (Genesis 19:23-25). The border of the Canaanites reached unto Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboim, and those cities went into the destruction with them (Genesis 10:19; Deuteronomy 29:23).

Lot’s sons in law took him as one that mocked, and they perished; when the warning comes, treating it as a joke is death (Genesis 19:14). The Lord spared not the place where Lot sojourned, but abhorred them for their pride (Ecclesiasticus 16:8).

Sodom and Gomorrah, giving themselves over to fornication and going after strange flesh, are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire (Jude 1:7; 2 Peter 2:6). What was done there on a small scale is done in spiritual Sodom on a greater scale, and the example stands; America read the example and legalized gay marriage anyway. America is modern-day Babylon, and it shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah; as in Sodom, they do not know it is coming (Isaiah 13:19; Luke 17:28-30).
Just Lot was delivered, and his wife became a pillar of salt; the waste land that smokes is a testimony of their wickedness to this day (Genesis 19:26; 2 Peter 2:7-8; Wisdom of Solomon 10:6-7).

cases.name: Lot
cases.charge: A just man, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked; pressing the strangers into his house and standing at the door between them and the men of the city
cases.summary: Lot was a just man, one that does what is lawful and right, a commandment keeper, and dwelling in Sodom he vexed his righteous soul from day to day with the unlawful deeds of the wicked (2 Peter 2:7-8). He sat in the gate, knew the two angels for who they were, pressed them into his house because he knew the men of Sodom, made them a feast, and went out at the door to stand between the men of the city and his guests (Genesis 19:1-7). When he lingered, the angels laid hold on his hand, the Lord being merciful to him, and God, remembering Abraham, sent him out before the fire fell (Genesis 19:16, 29).
offenseFull: To be just is to do that which is lawful and right, a commandment keeper; righteous Lot, dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds (Ezekiel 18:5; 2 Peter 2:7-8). A righteous man cannot be at home with that conduct. To survive in this wicked world you have to be like Lot, and the question is whether these things vex you or entertain you. Lot was not comfortable in Sodom (Luke 17:28-29).
Haran begat Lot and died in Ur of the Chaldees, and Lot went out with Abram from that place; Ur means fire, and the Chaldees is Babylon (Genesis 11:27-31).

Two angels came to Sodom at even while Lot sat in the gate; he rose up to meet them and bowed himself with his face toward the ground, showing respect to the angels (Genesis 19:1). Lot knew who they were, as Abraham knew who they were (Genesis 18:6-8). The angels of God are dark, burnt in appearance; their appearance is like burning coals of fire, and there is an honour in having dark skin (Ezekiel 1:13). Lot pressed upon them greatly to stay at his house, because he wanted a blessing and because he knew the men of Sodom; he made them a feast, and they did eat, for angels have bodies and functions like men (Genesis 19:2-3).

When the men of the city, old and young, compassed the house and demanded the men, Lot went out at the door, shut the door after him, and begged them as brethren not to do so wickedly (Genesis 19:4-7). He called that sin wickedness long before the law was written at Sinai. He offered his two daughters rather than let them have the men, because to him this sin was another level (Genesis 19:8). They said this one fellow came in to sojourn and would needs be a judge, and pressed sore upon him to break the door, and the angels pulled him into the house and smote the men at the door with blindness (Genesis 19:9-11).

Lot went out and warned his sons in law to get out of the place, for the Lord would destroy the city, and he seemed to them as one that mocked (Genesis 19:12-14). You will have people in your own house who do not see what you see spiritually, and they will not take you seriously.
judgmentFull: While Lot lingered, taking his time, the angels laid hold upon his hand and upon the hand of his wife and of his two daughters, the Lord being merciful to him, and set him outside the city, and told him to escape for his life and not look behind him (Genesis 19:15-17). Lot wanted to survive. The angel could do nothing until Lot had come to Zoar; the destruction waited on the righteous being brought out (Genesis 19:22). The Lord knows how to deliver the godly out of temptations (2 Peter 2:9).

God remembered Abraham and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthrow (Genesis 19:29). The Lord had told only Abraham, and on the day of destruction he sent the angels to get Lot out of the city because of Abraham, for Lot was Abraham’s nephew. Lot was delivered because he was vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked.

Afterward he feared to dwell in Zoar and dwelt in a cave in the mountain with his two daughters. They thought Sodom had been the whole world and that no man was left on the earth to give them seed, so they made their father drink wine and lay with him, and he perceived not when they lay down nor when they arose (Genesis 19:30-36). Take no wayward idea from it: uncovering the nakedness of a father is against the laws of the Most High; it was unlawful then and it is unlawful now (Leviticus 18:7). The firstborn bare Moab, father of the Moabites, and the younger bare Benammi, father of the children of Ammon, unto this day; those nations are the peoples known today as the Chinese and the Japanese (Genesis 19:37-38).

cases.name: Lot’s wife
cases.charge: Looking back from behind her husband toward Sodom against the angel’s command, because she loved the life of the city
cases.summary: The angels brought Lot’s wife out of the city by the hand and told them to escape for their lives and not look behind them (Genesis 19:16-17). She looked back from behind him and became a pillar of salt, a standing monument of an unbelieving soul (Genesis 19:26; Wisdom of Solomon 10:7). She was materialistic and loved the life of Sodom, and for her to look back means she never agreed to leave in the first place. Christ made her a warning in three words: Remember Lot’s wife (Luke 17:32).
offenseFull: The instruction came with the rescue: escape for thy life, look not behind thee, stay not in all the plain, escape to the mountain (Genesis 19:17). She had already been taken out by the hand together with her husband and her two daughters, the Lord being merciful unto them (Genesis 19:16). Yet she looked back from behind him, against the instruction (Genesis 19:26).

The city was filthy, and still she looked back, because she was filthy and materialistic and loved the life of Sodom and Gomorrah. Sodom was not an old looking city; it looked glorious, rich in gold, jewelry and fashion. There were homosexuals there, rapes, and the abuse of children, and she did not care; she loved the life. She looked back for all her possessions and her wealth, for she liked the comforts there. She was grieving, looking back at the burnt ashes of Sodom: all she had was gone, and her lifestyle was finished.

Lot wanted to survive, but his wife did not want to leave that area, and before the destruction came she was giving him a hard time over why they had to leave. For her to look back means she never agreed to leave in the first place. Why look back at a city like that unless she was not vexed with it and missed something in it (2 Peter 2:7-8)? The lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes and the pride of life are not of the Father but of the world, and that is what was in Sodom and Gomorrah (1 John 2:15-17). Lot rose up against the evildoers; his wife did not want to stand up against evil (Psalms 94:16).
judgmentFull: She became a pillar of salt (Genesis 19:26). The standing pillar of salt is a monument of an unbelieving soul, and the waste land that smokes is a testimony to this day (Wisdom of Solomon 10:6-7).

Remember Lot’s wife: three words among the weightiest in the scriptures (Luke 17:32). As it was in the days of Lot, they ate, drank, bought, sold, planted and builded until the day the fire fell; so shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed, and he that is in the field is not to return back (Luke 17:28-31). Let all of it go, all the things gained here in Babylon; you cannot take it with you.

This place has an end, and whoever wants to bring Babylon into the kingdom is looking back like Lot’s wife; no man, having put his hand to the plough and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God (Luke 9:62). When you come to this truth, there is no turning back. Flee the ways of the beast now, and do not be like Lot’s wife (Jeremiah 51:6). Stay away from filthiness, or be destroyed as she was. If you find yourself reminiscing after the old life, remember Lot’s wife.
