cases.name: Babylon, the lady of kingdoms
cases.charge: Shewing no mercy to the people the Lord was wroth with and gave into her hand; laying her yoke very heavily upon the ancient; saying in her heart, I am, and none else beside me; trusting in her wickedness, her wisdom, and the multitude of her sorceries
cases.summary: Isaiah told the virgin daughter of Babylon to come down and sit in the dust without a throne: the Lord gave his people into her hand, and she showed them no mercy, laid her yoke heavily on the aged, and said in her heart that she was, and none beside her (Isaiah 47:1; Isaiah 47:6-8). Loss of children and widowhood would come on her in one day, and the burden of Babylon and the proverb against its king carry the same sentence (Isaiah 47:9; Isaiah 13:19; Isaiah 14:4-23). This is not ancient Babylon but the daughter of Babylon, which is America.
offenseFull: The daughter of Babylon is Edom, the children of Edom who cried to raze Jerusalem to its foundation (Psalms 137:7-8). Edom is called the daughter of Babylon because they assisted the Babylonians, and when they came completely into power they became Babylon the great (Obadiah 1:11). She is told to come down from ruling, feared beyond Babylon, Persia, Greece and Rome, to the point that she can manufacture a war, and to go from the richest and wealthiest country to desolate and poor in the dust (Isaiah 47:1; 2 Esdras 12:13). Her shame uncovered is Mystery Babylon revealed, a land not seen as wicked by those who live in it, which taught the world how to be evil (Isaiah 47:2-3; Revelation 17:5). The Lord will take vengeance through his Son, who returns with the armies of heaven (Isaiah 47:3; Jude 1:14-15; Revelation 19:14).

God was angry with us because we broke his laws and commandments, scattered us among the nations, and gave us into Edom’s hand; Edom, the so-called white man, showed us no mercy here, laid a heavy yoke even on the old men and women, and polluted us with their holidays (Isaiah 47:6). The heathen helped forward the affliction, making the captivity worse than God intended: when the iniquity of slavery had an end, Esau created the Klan, Jim Crow, the black codes and convict leasing, and carried it on behind the scenes through government policy (Zechariah 1:15; Ezekiel 35:5). She dwells carelessly and says in her heart, I am, and none else beside me, the very words God says of himself: a nation putting itself in the seat of God is blasphemy (Isaiah 47:8; Isaiah 46:9). America dwells carelessly, doing what she wants to others and to her own people, passing laws secretly, and making her citizens care less, read less and think less. She trusted in her wickedness and said none saw her: they believed nobody would ever know what was done at Tulsa or Seneca Village, and the intelligence agencies destabilise countries in the dark, but God sees it; her wisdom and knowledge, all her technology, perverted her into thinking she is God (Isaiah 47:10). Her sorceries were laboured in from her youth: 1776 is their youth; the sorceries are the imagery, the television and the movies that deceive the nations, and the multitude of her counsels are the think tanks (Isaiah 47:12-13; Revelation 18:23).

The king of Babylon in Isaiah 14 is the United States of America, the oppressor and the golden city, the richest country on the earth (Isaiah 14:4). He smote the peoples with a continual stroke: this land was taken with bloodshed, violence and force, the indigenous people massacred and pushed onto reservations, and our people dragged here against their will for hundreds of years of free labour (Isaiah 14:6). Lucifer is the king of Babylon of verse 4, a man and a nation, America; Esau mixes Jude with Isaiah 14 to make a fallen-angel doctrine, and heaven here is rulership, as in Lamentations 2:1 (Isaiah 14:12). He would exalt his throne above the stars of God and sit upon the mount of the congregation in the sides of the north: we are the stars of God, the Lord’s congregation held in captivity in this hemisphere, and their throne is sitting on us (Isaiah 14:13).
judgmentFull: Loss of children and widowhood would come on her in a moment, in one day, in their perfection (Isaiah 47:9). Nobody has attacked America on its own soil like this, and it will come in one day, as the plague of the firstborn came in one night; in their perfection means nothing misses. Her astrologers could not save her, and her merchants, the corporations, would wander every one to his quarter, back to their homelands; it is the same Babylon the great (Isaiah 47:13-15; Revelation 18:21-23).

Isaiah 13 carries the burden of Babylon, the destruction of Edom and the rest of the nations in the day of the Most High: the banner is the Bible, the weapons of his indignation are the nuclear weapons that will be used, the darkened stars the satellites, the arrogant one Esau, and the earth removed out of her place by nuclear destruction (Isaiah 13:2-13). First the Lord makes a man more precious than fine gold, the Israelite man, and he cannot bring the destruction until he has made these new men (Isaiah 13:12). Every man shall flee into his own land, a word against marrying into the nations (Isaiah 13:14). The Lord stirs up the Medes and Persians, Iran, against America and Israel, and their bows are missiles; ancient Babylon fell from within, but this Babylon shall be as Sodom and Gomorrah, overthrown with fire, the United States of Babylon (Isaiah 13:17-19).

The king of Babylon is brought down to the pit, and those who see him look narrowly and ask whether this is the man that made the earth to tremble and opened not the house of his prisoners (Isaiah 14:15-17). Not a fallen angel: Lucifer is a man, the man of sin, and the Bible is what will reveal who these people really are. We are his prisoners, and he will never let go; many think they are free, but they were never free. The Lord sweeps Babylon with the besom of destruction, a broom of twigs, wiped out completely (Isaiah 14:22-23). On the other side stands the reversal: the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and those who held Israel captive will become their captives, and Israel shall rule over their oppressors (Isaiah 14:1-2).

cases.name: The elders with idols in the temple (Ezekiel 8)
cases.charge: The image of jealousy at the gate; seventy ancients with censers before creeping things and idols portrayed on the wall in the dark, saying, the Lord seeth us not; women weeping for Tammuz; twenty-five men with their backs to the temple worshipping the sun toward the east
cases.summary: Ezekiel was carried in the visions of God to Jerusalem and shown the abominations inside the Lord’s house: an image of jealousy at the gate, seventy elders burning incense before idols portrayed on the walls of a dark chamber, women at the north gate weeping for Tammuz, and twenty-five men with their backs to the temple worshipping the sun (Ezekiel 8:3-16). The elders said the Lord did not see them; the Lord said these things drove him from his sanctuary and he would deal in fury and not spare, and the glory went up from the midst of the city (Ezekiel 8:12; Ezekiel 8:18; Ezekiel 11:22-23).
offenseFull: In the sixth year, as the elders of Judah sat before Ezekiel in the captivity, the spirit carried him in the visions of God to Jerusalem (Ezekiel 8:1-3). The Lord was showing Ezekiel what Israel was doing behind closed doors, in secret, in the temple, and the reasons why they were allowed to go into captivity: the leaders of Israel were going off, and the Lord grew tired of it. Before this, Manasseh had built altars in the house of the Lord and seduced the people to do more evil than the nations the Lord destroyed before them: we went crazier than the heathen (2 Kings 21:1-9). At the gate stood the image of jealousy, and the Lord asked whether Ezekiel saw the great abominations that drove him far from his own sanctuary; the Lord was saying, I cannot be around you all (Ezekiel 8:5-6). The children of Israel were committing great abominations in secret, and it is no different today.

Ezekiel dug through the wall and saw every form of creeping thing, abominable beasts, and all the idols of the house of Israel portrayed upon the wall round about (Ezekiel 8:7-10); it is like putting images of Cesare Borgia or Guadalupe on the walls today. An idol is not always the image of another god; an idol can be many things, even your children. When Judah saw the Chaldeans portrayed on the wall in vermilion she was enticed by the flashy artwork and gold, as a harlot is enticed by a man flashing his wealth, and sent messengers to them (Ezekiel 23:14-16); that is why the Lord gave the fringes, for with the eyes they went whoring (Numbers 15:39). Seventy of the ancients of the house of Israel stood before those pictures, Jaazaniah the son of Shaphan among them, each with his censer and a thick cloud of incense, saying the Lord did not see them and had forsaken the earth (Ezekiel 8:11-12). The Lord showed the elders first, the leaders; what do you do in the dark? Your secret sins, hidden so that nobody knows, but God sees it. Men loved darkness rather than light because their deeds were evil; a man can be comfortable and even do well in the darkness he was raised in, and refusing the change the light requires is what condemns him (John 3:19).

Then greater abominations: at the north gate Israelite women sat weeping for Tammuz, and they knew what they were doing (Ezekiel 8:13-14). Tammuz is the son of Nimrod and Semiramis, the baby god, and Nimrod is the sun god; Tammuz died as an infant and was born on the 25th, which is why the mother and the forever baby Jesus are always shown and never grown, and why many of our people weep for the baby Jesus, a custom from ancient Babylon (Jeremiah 10:2-4). Women weeping for Tammuz in the Lord’s house is what is celebrated at Christmas. In the inner court about twenty-five men stood with their backs to the temple and their faces to the east, worshipping the sun (Ezekiel 8:15-16), and that is where the Sunday service comes from: sun worship. They also filled the land with violence and put the branch to their nose (Ezekiel 8:17): a branch with an aroma, smelled in the worship of Nimrod, a pagan custom showing allegiance to another god.
judgmentFull: The Lord answered that he would deal in fury, his eye would not spare, and though they cried in his ears with a loud voice he would not hear them (Ezekiel 8:18). That was the beginning of how Babylon came and took over. The eyes of the Lord are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, and he sets our secret sins in the light of his countenance (Ecclesiasticus 23:19; Psalms 90:8). The slaughter began at the sanctuary: the elders sat in the temple doing wickedness, and that is why the Most High sent the Babylonians to destroy it; those who were spared were carried captive to Babylon, the Daniels, the Ezekiels and the Mordecais (Ezekiel 9:1-6). The mark was set on those who sighed and cried for the abominations, and to sigh and cry for the abominations you must know God’s laws (Ezekiel 9:4). The glory of the Lord went up from the midst of the city and stood upon the mountain on the east side, and the spirit took Ezekiel into Chaldea to the captives, where he told them all the things the Most High had shown him (Ezekiel 11:22-25). We were born right here in Babylon the great and learned the Babylonian customs, and we keep them earnestly without asking questions, though the Lord said learn not the way of the heathen (Jeremiah 10:2).

cases.name: Pelatiah and the princes at the east gate
cases.charge: Devising mischief and giving wicked counsel in the city, telling the people that judgment was not near and that Jerusalem, the iron pot, would protect them
cases.summary: Twenty-five men stood at the east gate of the Lord’s house, among them Jaazaniah the son of Azur and Pelatiah the son of Benaiah, princes of the people, who devised mischief and gave wicked counsel in the city (Ezekiel 11:1-3). They told the people that Jerusalem, the iron pot, would protect them, giving a false sense of security. While Ezekiel prophesied against them, Pelatiah died, put to death by the Most High (Ezekiel 11:4-13).
offenseFull: Ezekiel 11 through 14 run on one thread, false security: wicked counsellors, false prophets and lying women told our people that Jerusalem was a safe iron pot and that judgment would never fall. There was a lot of idolatry going on at that time; the ancients of the house of Israel, Jaazaniah the son of Shaphan among them, burned incense in the dark, every man in the chambers of his imagery, saying the Lord did not see them (Ezekiel 8:6-12).

At the east gate were twenty-five men, among them Jaazaniah the son of Azur and Pelatiah the son of Benaiah, princes of the people; remember the name Pelatiah (Ezekiel 11:1). They gave wicked counsel: judgment was not near, they should build houses, the city was the cauldron and they the flesh (Ezekiel 11:2-3). The northern kingdom had already been carried away and some of our people were already in captivity, yet the counsel was that Jerusalem, the iron pot, would protect them, giving the people a false sense of security.

The Most High knows the things that come into their minds, every one of them (Ezekiel 11:4-5). They had filled the streets with the slain, for the land was full of blood and violence; those dead were the flesh and the city the cauldron, but He would bring the counsellors out of it (Ezekiel 11:6-7).

The princes of the bloody city used their power to shed blood, oppressed the stranger, vexed the fatherless and the widow, and profaned His sabbaths (Ezekiel 22:6-9). They broke all manner of the immoral laws of Leviticus 18, took gifts to shed blood, being put on the take and paid off to shed a man’s blood, and greedily gained by extortion: these are wicked leaders (Ezekiel 22:10-12). He sought a man to make up the hedge and stand in the gap, and found none (Ezekiel 22:30); that is the one who rises up against the evildoers and would turn the Lord’s wrath from the people (Psalm 94:16).
judgmentFull: They feared the sword, and He would bring a sword upon them, meaning He would bring the nations against Jerusalem (Ezekiel 11:8). He would deliver them into the hands of strangers and judge them in the border of Israel (Ezekiel 11:9-11). We are judged because we do not keep the Most High’s laws, the same then as today: they had done after the manners of the heathen round about them (Ezekiel 11:12), which is the immoral laws and spiritual idolatry we followed back then and still follow today (Leviticus 18:3). The land spews out the defiled; that is why Israel was put out of Jerusalem, for we could not abide in the land with our sins (Leviticus 18:24-28).

While Ezekiel prophesied, Pelatiah the son of Benaiah died, one of the wicked men that had given wicked counsel, put to death by the Most High (Ezekiel 11:13). Ezekiel fell upon his face and cried whether the Lord would make a full end of the remnant of Israel.

The answer was for the captives, to whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem had said to get far from the Lord (Ezekiel 11:14-15). Though He scattered them among the countries, He would be to them a little sanctuary where they came (Ezekiel 11:16; Deuteronomy 4:27): even though He cast us off into these lands, He would not cast us off from being His people. We were scattered first through the sub-Saharan slave trade and then through the transatlantic slave trade (Deuteronomy 28:68). The little sanctuaries are the schools IUIC is setting up in all our scattered lands, where you come and learn the word of God; there is a school near you, with elders in every city (Titus 1:5). We need them because the Christian church never taught us who we are.

He would gather them and give them the land of Israel, and they would take away its detestable things: the Most High will purge the evil from us, as the thirteenth chapter of Zechariah shows (Ezekiel 11:17-18; Zechariah 13). He would give them one heart and a new spirit, and take out the stony heart, the rebellious mind that rebels against His laws, and give them a heart of flesh, a new mind, the spirit to keep the laws (Ezekiel 11:19-20). Our people need the Spirit of God in them, for we are a traumatized people. But on the wicked Israelites who walk after their detestable things He will recompense their way; there is a big payback when you will not keep His laws (Ezekiel 11:21). Then the cherubims, the angels of the wheels of the first chapter, lifted their wings, and the glory of the Lord went up from the city (Ezekiel 11:22-23; Ezekiel 1:15-21).

cases.name: Edom, in the day of his brother
cases.charge: Standing on the other side in the day that strangers carried away Jacob captive, and being as one of them; rejoicing over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction; entering the gate, laying hands on the substance, standing in the crossway to cut off those that escaped, and delivering up those that remained
cases.summary: The whole vision of Obadiah is one charge against Edom: the pride of Esau in the clefts of the rock, what Esau did in the day his brother Jacob was carried away captive, and the reward that returns on his own head (Obadiah 1:1-15). When strangers carried Jacob away and cast lots on Jerusalem, Esau stood on the other side and took part, rejoicing over Judah, laying hands on its substance, cutting off those who escaped and handing over the rest (Obadiah 1:11-14). Esau is Edom, and Edom is the so-called white man today (Genesis 36:1). The house of Jacob will be a fire and the house of Esau stubble, and the kingdom shall be the Lord’s (Obadiah 1:18; Obadiah 1:21).
offenseFull: The Lord made Edom small among the heathen and greatly despised (Obadiah 1:1-2). Esau is Edom: he came out of the womb red, his blood seen through his skin for lack of melanin, while Jacob was not described, because the man of melanin needed no description (Genesis 36:1; Genesis 25:25). The pride of his heart deceived him, dwelling in the clefts of the rock (Obadiah 1:3). The clefts are Mount Seir, where Esau dwelt (Genesis 36:8), and Petra, the buildings carved out of the rock; in the Middle Ages they lived in the Caucasus mountains, which is why they call themselves Caucasian; today the clefts of the rock are the governments, the high places and the skyscrapers. America has the arsenal to say nobody can bring it down.

He exalted himself as the eagle and set his nest among the stars (Obadiah 1:4). Edom’s nations take the eagle for their symbol: Rome, Greece, Spain, France, Britain, Russia and America; the great seal holds arrows for war in one claw and the olive branch of peace in the other, and they come with peace while war is in their heart. The nest among the stars is space travel, the satellites and the space force; when they landed on the moon in 1969, they said the eagle has landed (Isaiah 14:13-14).

A regular thief steals till he has enough, and grape gatherers leave some grapes (Obadiah 1:5), but Esau leaves nothing behind: he takes every grape, the stem, the root and the ground, the house, the people inside the house, the land, the race and the identity; he is like the ocean, all the rivers run into it and it is never full. His hidden things will be searched out (Obadiah 1:6): God puts His spirit on us, and we go forth and reveal him. Esau is greatly despised for what the record shows: the papal bulls Dum Diversas and Romanus Pontifex gave leave to capture and subdue the Saracens, the pagans and all other enemies of Christ and reduce their persons to perpetual slavery, and perpetual slavery is perpetual hatred, which began when Esau purposed to slay his brother (Genesis 27:41); then the atrocities in the Congo under Belgium and the massacres at Ponce and Utuado.

The charge is his violence against his brother Jacob (Obadiah 1:10). In the day strangers carried away Jacob’s forces and cast lots on Jerusalem, Esau stood on the other side and took part (Obadiah 1:11); Edom was complicit in the Babylonian capture of Jerusalem in 586 BC, and the Edomites burned the temple when the Chaldees made Judea desolate (1 Esdras 4:45). They rejoiced when we were destroyed and laid hands on us, robbing us too; when we were escaping, Edom blocked our way, held us in, and gave us up to the Babylonians (Obadiah 1:12-14). Edom is the daughter of Babylon, because they assisted the Cushite Babylonians (Psalm 137:7-8). Edom, the so-called white man, dealt against Judah by taking vengeance (Ezekiel 25:12): he used the legislative, judicial and executive branches to take vengeance, and weaponized the police against us, the original slave catchers.
judgmentFull: From his nest among the stars the Lord will bring him down (Obadiah 1:4): once you reach that height, the bringing down begins, and from the 1960s the truth has been coming out like never before. The men of his confederacy will bring him to the border and deceive him, and those who eat his bread will lay a wound under him (Obadiah 1:7). The men of his confederacy are the European Union; the ten kings give their kingdom to the beast for a time, then hate the whore and make her desolate (Revelation 17:12-17): his own confederacy turns on him, as it did in the world wars.

The wise men will be destroyed out of Edom and the mighty men of Teman dismayed (Obadiah 1:8-9); Teman, Esau’s grandson, is Germany, out of which much of the world’s science and weapons technology has come, and the word says that wisdom will be destroyed. For his violence against Jacob shame will cover him and he will be cut off for ever (Obadiah 1:10). Because of what he started in Babylon, God has not forgotten any of it to this very day. We are not to walk around with actual hatred, but we must remember our history and what was done to us, and know who the enemy is.

The day of the Lord is near upon all the heathen: as he has done, it will be done to him, and his reward will return on his own head (Obadiah 1:15). The heathen will drink and be as though they had not been (Obadiah 1:16), from America to those who came back to the land in 1948 and brought murder and bloodshed with them. On Mount Zion will be deliverance, and the house of Jacob will be a fire and the house of Joseph a flame, the southern and northern kingdoms, and the house of Esau stubble, with none remaining; the Lord spoke it, not us (Obadiah 1:17-18).

The Lord will lay His vengeance upon Edom (Ezekiel 25:13-14). That is future prophecy that has not yet come to pass, for the Most High must first change our minds (Zechariah 9:13; Wisdom of Solomon 3:6-8); the day of righteous vengeance is coming, but now is not that time. Saviours will come up on Mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau, and the kingdom shall be the Lord’s (Obadiah 1:21): we are the herald to Christ, letting you know what is going to happen.

cases.name: The prince of Tyre
cases.charge: Saying, I am a God, I sit in the seat of God, in the midst of the seas; setting his heart as the heart of God because of the riches gotten by his wisdom and his traffick
cases.summary: The word came to Ezekiel for the prince of Tyrus, whose heart was lifted up so that he said he was a god sitting in the seat of God in the midst of the seas, though he was a man and not God, wiser than Daniel and rich by his wisdom and traffic (Ezekiel 28:1-5). The Lord would bring strangers upon him, the terrible of the nations, to bring him down to the pit, and he would die the deaths of the uncircumcised by the hand of strangers (Ezekiel 28:6-10). Tyre was a city in Lebanon, and the prince of Tyrus is also a similitude for Edom, the so-called white man, for America (Hosea 12:10).
offenseFull: God has multiplied visions and used similitudes by the prophets (Hosea 12:10): Ezekiel reads of a country that did exist, but God is not only talking about that country. Tyrus is Lebanon; Tyre was a city in Lebanon, and Tyre and Zidon were the Hamite nations of Canaan that sold the children of Judah to the Grecians and delivered up the whole captivity to Edom (Joel 3:4-6; Amos 1:9). The prince of Tyrus is also a metaphor for today, for Edom, for America (Ezekiel 28:1-2).

He said he was a god sitting in the seat of God in the midst of the seas (Ezekiel 28:2). No other nation on earth did what America has done in the midst of the seas. He sits in the seat of God because he is in space, in rulership, the superpower in the midst of the nations, like the woman who sits upon many waters (Revelation 17:1). Yet he is a man and not God: a man made of dust, water and blood, no matter the crown and the seal (Isaiah 14:16).

He was wiser than Daniel, and no secret could be hidden from him (Ezekiel 28:3): there is no secret you can hide from the white man; everything you type on these devices is recorded, and nothing disappears. With his wisdom he gathered gold and silver into his treasures (Ezekiel 28:4): the Treaty of Fort Laramie of 1868 was violated the minute gold was discovered, and the forts sit where the gold is. By his traffic, meaning trade, he increased his riches, and his heart was lifted up (Ezekiel 28:5): by the way they traded slaves they became who they are today, and Haiti was made to take American rice at a three percent tariff until it depended on America’s food imports. You read this and it sounds profound, but it is all in the negative.

This is prosperity attributed to his own powers instead of to its true source, which may be called the insanity of prosperity; the warning reaches Sennacherib, Nebuchadnezzar, Pharaoh and Herod, and the one foretold in 2 Thessalonians 2, who is America (Ezekiel 29:3; Acts 12:21-23; 2 Thessalonians 2:4). The scripture is manifold: when it says Tyrus, it is not always referring to that area. Tyrus said Aha against Jerusalem, the gate of the peoples, expecting to be replenished from her ruin; Tyrus saw our loss of Jerusalem as her come-up and profit (Ezekiel 26:2).

The king of Tyrus had been in Eden, the garden of God, and the workmanship of his tabrets and pipes was prepared in him in the day he was created (Ezekiel 28:12-13). This is Cain, who was in the garden in the loins of Adam, and whose line handled the harp and organ (Genesis 4:21). He is the anointed cherub that covers (Ezekiel 28:14): Cain, and Esau after him on the line, raised up to cover the truth, our history, and the way to the tree of life (Genesis 3:24). Esau is Cain again: he covers in lies, watches everything and whitewashes everything. He was perfect in his ways until iniquity was found in him, and he killed his brother Abel; by the multitude of his merchandise he was filled with violence (Ezekiel 28:15-16).
judgmentFull: Because he set his heart as the heart of God, the Lord would bring strangers upon him, the terrible of the nations (Ezekiel 28:6-7). The terrible of the nations are terrorist groups; terrible and terrorist come from the same root. They will draw their swords against the beauty of his wisdom and test the wisdom of America, and like the daughter of Babylon he will lose his citizens and his allies in one day (Isaiah 47:8-9). They will bring him down to the pit, and he will die the deaths of the slain in the midst of the seas (Ezekiel 28:8); in the hand of him that slays him he will be a man and not God (Ezekiel 28:9-10).

Against the city He brought many nations like the waves of the sea, and Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon from the north, and Babylon served as His sword against the nations that thought our downfall was their gain (Ezekiel 26:3-12). The princes of the sea would come down from their thrones and lament the renowned city of seafaring men (Ezekiel 26:15-18), the fall of the great seafaring city that reflects Esau’s nation today, where every shipmaster and sailor stands afar off and cries at the smoke of her burning (Revelation 18:17-19; Isaiah 14:12). She would be sought for and never found again, because she said Aha when we suffered judgment (Ezekiel 26:21). The fire on the wall of Tyrus is what is seen today, missiles and bombs devouring the cities of Lebanon (Amos 1:10).

The Lord would cast the covering cherub as profane out of the mountain of God, out of our land, the homeland of Israel, and destroy him from the midst of the stones of fire; his heart was lifted up because of his beauty, for he gained authority on the earth (Ezekiel 28:16-17). A fire would come from his own midst and bring him to ashes in the sight of all who beheld him, and he would be a terror, and never be any more (Ezekiel 28:18-19).

cases.name: Pharaoh-hophra and Egypt
cases.charge: Saying, My river is mine own, and I have made it for myself; being a staff of reed to the house of Israel that brake when they leaned upon it
cases.summary: Through Ezekiel 27, 28 and 29 the Most High speaks against the nations, delivering His judgments upon Tyrus, Zidon, and now Egypt. Pharaoh, the great dragon in the midst of his rivers, said the river was his own and he had made it for himself, and Egypt had been a staff of reed to Israel, breaking when they leaned on it (Ezekiel 29:1-7). The Lord made Egypt desolate forty years, from Syene to the border of Ethiopia, and afterward the basest of kingdoms, no more the confidence of Israel; and He gave Pharaoh-hophra into the hand of his enemies, as He gave Zedekiah to Nebuchadnezzar (Ezekiel 29:8-16; Jeremiah 44:30).
offenseFull: In the tenth year, the tenth month, the twelfth day, the word came to Ezekiel to set his face against Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great dragon that lies in the midst of his rivers, who said his river was his own and he had made it for himself (Ezekiel 29:1-3). That is prosperity attributed to his own powers instead of to its true source, the insanity of prosperity, the same warning given to Sennacherib, Nebuchadnezzar and Herod.

Egypt had been a staff of reed to the house of Israel: when they leaned on it, it broke and tore their shoulder (Ezekiel 29:6-7). The Rabshakeh called Pharaoh the same broken reed in Hezekiah’s day (Isaiah 36:6), for we loved Egypt and put all our trust in Egypt. Rather than relying on God for resources, protection or war, we always relied on the surrounding nations; many kings went down to Egypt for protection and covering, and so the king of Assyria was sent against Egypt and Ethiopia to take away that hedge, and Israel was ashamed of Ethiopia their expectation and Egypt their glory (Isaiah 20:1-6; Isaiah 30:1-3). Jeremiah told Israel to submit when Nebuchadnezzar came and not to go to Egypt, and Israel made a league with Egypt, adding sin to sin.

The same problems we had back then are the same problems our people have today: we trust in America, we trust in democracy, we trust in America’s military, and we do not seek the Holy One of Israel (Isaiah 31:1). After Gedaliah, the remnant went to the same reed, dwelling at Migdol, Tahpanhes, Noph and Pathros and burning incense to other gods there, cutting themselves off to become a curse and a reproach among the nations (Jeremiah 44:1-8). The men did not rule their houses and their wives were in the midst of idolatry, the same disorder seen spiritually in Egypt, in Babylon the great, today (Jeremiah 44:15-19).
judgmentFull: The Lord would put hooks in Pharaoh’s jaws, bring him up out of his rivers, and leave him thrown into the wilderness (Ezekiel 29:4-5). He would bring a sword on Egypt and make the land utterly waste and desolate from the tower of Syene to the border of Ethiopia, uninhabited forty years (Ezekiel 29:8-12): Nebuchadnezzar slaughtered Egypt’s military, and the Egyptians were scattered among the nations. Syene is Aswan today. Egypt in the Bible included Egypt and Sudan; Britain later named that part Sudan.

At the end of forty years He would bring them again to Pathros, the land of their habitation, and they would be a base kingdom, the basest of kingdoms, no more to rule over the nations or be the confidence of the house of Israel (Ezekiel 29:13-16). Pathros is Upper Egypt, and Pathros is Sudan. Base is the bottom of all bottoms, the lowest; that is why the Egyptians are not seen as a mighty empire today, and when the Greeks came they were no problem. Egypt would never be exalted as a world superpower again, and those who try to glorify ancient Egypt cannot resurrect it. God destroys all that we rely on: everything in which you find confidence He will make base, so that you have one thing only to turn to, and that is Him. Everywhere Israel touches down we bring blessings to that territory, and once we leave, empires begin to crumble and fall.

In the twenty-seventh year Nebuchadnezzar’s army served a great service against Tyrus and had no wages for it, so the Lord gave him the land of Egypt as wages for his army, because they wrought for Him; in that day the horn of the house of Israel would bud forth (Ezekiel 29:17-21).

To the remnant in Egypt the Lord gave a sign that His words would stand against them: He would give Pharaoh-hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies, as He gave Zedekiah into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar (Jeremiah 44:29-30). Hophra, called Apries, was overthrown by his own general Amasis, whom the rebellious soldiers proclaimed king, in the civil war of about 570 to 567 BC; he was given into the hands of Amasis and later died, and Jeremiah prophesied it sixteen years before it happened. Evil does not come merely by chance: there is no evil in a city that the Most High has not done, and none can deliver out of His hand (Amos 3:6; Deuteronomy 32:39).

He would bring a sword on Egypt and make the land utterly waste and desolate from the tower of Syene to the border of Ethiopia, uninhabited forty years (Ezekiel 29:8-12): Nebuchadnezzar slaughtered Egypt’s military, and the Egyptians were scattered among the nations. Syene is Aswan today. Egypt in the Bible included Egypt and Sudan; Britain later named that part Sudan.

cases.name: The shepherds of Israel
cases.charge: Feeding themselves and not the flock; eating the fat and clothing themselves with the wool; not strengthening the diseased, healing the sick, binding up the broken, bringing again the driven away, or seeking the lost; ruling with force and with cruelty
cases.summary: Ezekiel was sent against the shepherds of Israel, who fed themselves and not the flock, ate the fat, wore the wool, did not heal, bind up, bring back or seek the lost, and ruled with force and cruelty, until the sheep were scattered and became meat to every beast of the field (Ezekiel 34:1-6). Shepherd is another word for pastor. The Lord declared Himself against the shepherds and said He would search out His sheep Himself, and set over them one shepherd, His servant David, who is Christ (Ezekiel 34:10-11; Ezekiel 34:23-24).
offenseFull: What Jeremiah prophesied is very similar to what Ezekiel prophesied: woe to the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of His pasture, and He will visit upon them the evil of their doings (Jeremiah 23:1-2). In Christianity they scatter the sheep by sending them to the Baptist church, the Catholic church, the holiness church, whatever denomination, dividing us rather than uniting us as the twelve tribes of Israel, and driving them away from the truth that they are the Israelites. The Lord promised pastors according to His heart, who would feed them with knowledge and understanding of His laws (Jeremiah 3:15).

Woe to the shepherds of Israel that feed themselves (Ezekiel 34:2): they are concerned with filling their pockets. They eat the fat and clothe themselves with the wool, but do not feed the flock (Ezekiel 34:3): they get the best clothes, still in gators and suits to this day. Their message is bring your tithes, bring your money, and because the people are not studying, they stay blinded in those churches. The job of a shepherd was to help Israel come out from under the curse.

They did not strengthen the diseased, heal the sick, bind up the broken, bring again the driven away or seek the lost, but ruled with force and cruelty (Ezekiel 34:4). The driven away are the twelve tribes that were scattered, and Ezekiel was writing in the Babylonian captivity. With force and cruelty they rule over us, and they are not here to help us understand that we are the Israelites, that we broke God’s laws, and that we are living a curse.

The sheep were scattered for lack of a shepherd and became meat to all the beasts of the field, meaning all the nations (Ezekiel 34:5). They wandered through all the mountains and upon every high hill, which represent countries and cities, and none searched or sought after them (Ezekiel 34:6). None of these pastors are searching or seeking for the twelve tribes, and there are Israelite groups too, comfortable at home on the internet, whose whole campaign is trying to stop the Israelites who are actually doing the work. We think of being prey only to the nations, but our own people prey upon us as well (Ezekiel 34:22).

The chapter is turned on the leaders among us as well: they receive the benefits of being the head and get to eat first, but our job is to serve you, and it cannot be for money or opportunity. Force and cruelty is not healing the people, not teaching them, not making them whole with God; it should not be named among us. The leader confesses himself among the sinners, as Nehemiah confessed that he and his father’s house had sinned (Nehemiah 1:6-7). The hireling sees the wolf coming and flees, because he is a hireling and does not care for the sheep (John 10:12-13).
judgmentFull: The Lord is against the shepherds: He will require His flock at their hand, cause them to cease from feeding it, and deliver His flock from their mouth (Ezekiel 34:7-10). He Himself will search out His sheep and seek them (Ezekiel 34:11). Who is that I? Christ, who was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel; that is what Christ was doing, and what Paul and the apostles were doing in the great commission (Matthew 15:24; Matthew 28:19).

When He returns He will seek out His sheep, the slaves scattered through all the four corners of the earth, and deliver them out of all places where they were scattered in the cloudy and dark day (Ezekiel 34:12). The cloudy and dark day is not rain clouds: the sun and the moon will not give their light because of the war, when the nuclear bombs go off (Matthew 24:29-30). He will bring them to their own land and feed them in a good pasture upon the mountains of Israel, which is the kingdom (Ezekiel 34:13-15).

He will seek the lost, which is our people, bring again the driven away, bind up the broken, for we were broken, and strengthen the sick, for we are the sick ones (Ezekiel 34:16). He will destroy the fat and the strong: the nations, and also the leaders among us that are fat, making their bread and not teaching our people what they need to heal their spirit. He will feed them with judgment, which is His laws.

He will judge between cattle and cattle, between the righteous Israelites and the wicked Israelites, and that is where Christ’s separating of the sheep from the goats comes from (Ezekiel 34:17-22; Matthew 25:32-33). He will set up one shepherd over them, His servant David: the good shepherd is Christ, set over the Israelites, the righteous Branch raised unto David, whose name plainly refers to Christ (Ezekiel 34:23-24; John 10:11; Jeremiah 23:5-6). Afterward the children of Israel will return and seek the Lord their God and David their king (Hosea 3:5). He will make with them a covenant of peace; that is why He is the Prince of Peace (Ezekiel 34:25). The earth will yield her increase, as it would not yield its strength to Cain, and none will make them afraid: right now we live in fear, but nobody is going to make us afraid ever again (Ezekiel 34:26-28; Genesis 4:12). They will know that the Lord their God is with them, and that they, the house of Israel, are His people (Ezekiel 34:30-31).

cases.name: Jonah
cases.charge: Rising up to flee unto Tarshish from the presence of the Lord instead of going to Nineveh to cry against it
cases.summary: The word of the Lord sent Jonah the son of Amittai to cry against Nineveh, and he rose up to flee to Tarshish from the presence of the Lord (Jonah 1:1-3). The storm found him asleep in the ship; he owned that he was the cause and was cast into the sea, and the Lord prepared a great fish in which he lay three days and three nights, praying, until he was put out on dry land (Jonah 1:4-17; Jonah 2:1-10). Sent the second time, he cried against the city, and when the Lord spared it he was angry; the Lord answered him with the gourd, and Christ made his three days and three nights the sign given to His generation (Jonah 3:1-4; Jonah 4:1-11; Matthew 12:39-40).
offenseFull: Jonah the son of Amittai prophesied in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, who restored the coast of Israel by his word, for the Most High saw the bitter affliction of Israel and would not blot out their name (2 Kings 14:25-27). The word came to him to go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it, for its wickedness had come up before the Lord (Jonah 1:1-2). Christians read Ninevites and think Assyrians, but the Ninevites that Jonah preached to were the ten tribes led captive into Nineveh: Tobit of the tribe of Naphtali, of the northern kingdom, was carried there, and the Israelites heard the preaching of Jonah and took heed to it (Tobit 1:1-3; Tobit 14:8). That is why Jonah preached to Nineveh: the northern kingdom was exiled there.

He rose up to flee to Tarshish from the presence of the Lord, went down to Joppa, found a ship, paid the fare and went down into it (Jonah 1:3). Tarshish is Spain (Genesis 10:1-5; Ezekiel 27:12): Jonah looked on Tarshish as a safe haven with a hospitable people, because he knew his people would be there. He fled because he was afraid of the people of Nineveh; fear clouded his judgment and he leaned on his own understanding, and like Adam he tried to hide from God. He fled also, as he himself says, because he knew the Lord was gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and would spare them (Jonah 4:2).

The Lord sent a great wind and the ship was like to be broken; the mariners cried every man unto his god, and Jonah lay fast asleep in the sides of the ship (Jonah 1:4-5). Jonah is the picture of the slack spirit: he wanted nothing to do with prophesying to wake his people up, and he slept while the tempest was ready to break the ship. America is that spiritual ship that is going to sink, and a lot of our people are asleep in the middle of the chaos. The lot fell on Jonah, because the lot belongs to the Lord, and he confessed that he was a Hebrew who feared the Lord, the God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land (Jonah 1:7-10).
judgmentFull: He told them to cast him into the sea, for the tempest was on his account (Jonah 1:11-12). That is integrity: to stand up and own that you are in the wrong, unlike Achan, whose secret sin kindled the Lord’s anger against all of us (Joshua 7:1). They rowed hard, prayed not to be charged with innocent blood, and cast him in, and the sea ceased from her raging; the men feared the Lord, for all the nations know there is only one true living God, the God of Israel (Jonah 1:13-16).

The Lord had prepared a great fish, Leviathan (Job 41), and Jonah was in its belly three days and three nights (Jonah 1:17). He cried to the Lord out of the belly of hell, which is the grave, and the Lord brought up his life from corruption, which is death (Jonah 2:1-6). At the beginning he fled from the Lord; now he sought Him, as in their affliction they will seek Him early (Hosea 5:15). When his soul fainted he remembered the Lord (Jonah 2:7). Our people in Nineveh were observing lying vanities, as our people observe them today in Babylon, in America: a white Jesus, Christmas and the holidays (Jonah 2:8). In the fish he repented of his fear and his doubt, and the fish vomited him out on dry land (Jonah 2:9-10).

The word came the second time, to preach the preaching the Lord bade him, saying what he was given and not what came out of his own heart; that is how a false prophet is known (Jonah 3:1-4). The city repented, and God repented of the evil (Jonah 3:5-10). Then Jonah had an attitude problem: he was very angry that God did not destroy the people, as James and John wanted to call fire from heaven (Jonah 4:1-2; Luke 9:54). He asked to die, feeling that the people would see him as a false prophet or a liar (Jonah 4:3). We are not to do things for our own glory; it is for the Lord’s glory (1 Peter 4:11). With the gourd, the worm and the east wind the Lord showed him that he pitied a plant he had not laboured for, and asked whether He should not spare Nineveh (Jonah 4:4-11).

The Lord held off because His people were there, and they repented; but the word still stood, and Nineveh was destroyed (Tobit 14:8). Christ gave that generation no sign but the sign of Jonas: as Jonah was three days and three nights in the fish, the Son of man would be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth (Matthew 12:39-40). Friday night and Saturday night are two days and two nights, so the count rules out Good Friday to Sunday morning. As Jonah’s life was brought up from corruption, so the Holy One’s soul would not be left in the grave nor see corruption (Psalm 16:10). Jonah is actually about us: the God who heard Jonah out of the fish’s belly does not change, so why can we not pray the same way Jonah prayed (Malachi 3:6)?

cases.name: Nineveh under Nahum
cases.charge: A bloody city, full of lies and robbery, whose prey departeth not; the den of the lions that emptied Jacob; the harlot that sold nations; the wicked counsellor that imagineth evil against the Lord
cases.summary: The burden of Nineveh opens with who the Most High is toward his adversaries and toward them that trust in him, and ends with the yoke broken off Judah and the feet upon the mountains that publish peace (Nahum 1:1-15). Nahum 2 and 3 are the judgment on Nineveh, the bloody city, told as a siege that comes on her the way she came on others (Nahum 2:1-13; Nahum 3:1-19). Nineveh fell in 612 BC to the Medes and the Babylonians (Tobit 14:15). Nineveh, the capital of Assyria, and America are one and the same, and the bloody city is Mystery Babylon the Great (Nahum 3:1; Revelation 17:5).
offenseFull: The burden is not only about ancient Assyria, whose capital was Nineveh; it is about Babylon and her allies, for the earth burning at his presence did not happen in ancient Assyria (Nahum 1:1-5). The Lord will take vengeance on his adversaries, the nations, and he reserves wrath for America, for China, for Europe, for all the evil they did to Israel (Nahum 1:2). He has been slow to anger, a patient God, because he needs more of his people to repent; and he will not at all acquit the wicked (Nahum 1:3). The so-called white man, and the Arabs too, think they have been acquitted of all the slavery and oppression they did to Israel; to acquit is to forgive, to let bygones be bygones, and there will be no acquittal. His way is in the whirlwind and in the storm: he visits in these storms against Esau and the other nations, because he is angry with what they have done to his people (Nahum 1:3).

Nineveh had been spared once: when Jonah prophesied, the Lord held off because his people were there, and they repented; but it was still understood that Nineveh would be destroyed, and it was (Jonah 3:10). Jonah stayed the destruction, but Nineveh did not change Israel, who were there in idolatry, and eventually Nineveh fell. Tobit, of Naphtali, buried his brethren whose bodies were cast about the walls of Nineveh: they killed Israel’s people and left them in the streets, and the Assyrians did much wickedness to Israel, all because of Israel’s sins (Tobit 1:17-18). The emptiers emptied Jacob, and the lion filled his holes with prey (Nahum 2:2; Nahum 2:11-12).

Out of Nineveh came one who imagines evil against the Lord, a wicked counsellor (Nahum 1:11). That is America, the elites, the top kingdom from which all wisdom is said to come. It is not one man but a system of people, the horns of Daniel 7 that represent NATO and the European Union (Daniel 7:8). Woe to the bloody city: this is America, which spilled much Israelite blood in this land and is still doing it, and the great number of carcasses are the carcasses of Israel’s forefathers (Nahum 3:1-3). Nahum called Esau the bloody city: the land is drenched with Israel’s blood (Ezekiel 35:5). Full of lies and robbery, she robbed all the nations, and Israel too, of their lands, their identity, their culture, even their minds (Nahum 3:1). The prey that departs not is Israel in captivity: in captivity the people wax old in mind and will not depart, as Israel was the prey in Egypt and did not want to leave (Exodus 14:12).

The well-favoured harlot, the mistress of witchcrafts that sold nations through her whoredoms, is America, and Israel was sold into slavery (Nahum 3:4). The harlot of Nahum is the mother of harlots, Mystery Babylon the Great: the two have the same attributes (Revelation 17:5).
judgmentFull: The Lord is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble, and he knows them that trust in him (Nahum 1:7). Trouble is coming and Israel’s trial is coming, and the Lord is good in the day of trouble if you keep the law; his people will have no choice but to depend on one another.

With an overrunning flood he will make an end of Babylon and the lands, and darkness shall pursue the militaries of the world (Nahum 1:8). Affliction shall not rise up the second time: Babylon shall sink and not rise again, and once the Lord finishes with the nations they will not rise up and afflict Israel again (Nahum 1:9; Jeremiah 51:64). The Lord allowed Israel to be afflicted, but he promised to afflict them no more; he will break the yoke of the white man and the nations off his people and burst their bonds, the mental bonds of slavery (Nahum 1:12-13). The Lord gave commandment that no more of her name be sown, and the one addressed is Esau, Edom: the seed of evildoers shall never be renowned (Nahum 1:14; Isaiah 14:20).

He that dashes in pieces came up, the palace was dissolved, and she was empty, void and waste (Nahum 2:1-10). The Lord of hosts was against her; her bruise had no healing, and all that heard of her clapped their hands, for her wickedness had passed upon everyone continually (Nahum 2:13; Nahum 3:5; Nahum 3:19). Babylon and the Medes teamed up to take down the Assyrian: in 612 BC Cyaxares, the Median king, attacked Nineveh, which was taken by the joint Median and Babylonian forces after three months of siege (Tobit 14:15). The Median army turned the city into ruined hills and heaps of debris; the Assyrians had been vicious and cruel to all the nations they conquered, and when they were conquered their city was destroyed to nothing, and by 600 BC the Assyrian kingdom was completely destroyed. Before he died Tobit heard of the destruction of Nineveh and rejoiced, because they had killed Israel’s people and left them for dead in the streets (Tobit 14:15).

cases.name: The adversaries of Judah and Benjamin
cases.charge: Offering to build with Judah in order to hinder the work; weakening the hands of the people and troubling them in building; hiring counsellors to frustrate their purpose; writing accusations to the king; and making the work cease by force and power
cases.summary: The adversaries of Judah and Benjamin, the peoples the king of Assyria had brought into the land, came to Zerubbabel asking to build with them, claiming to seek the same God since Esarhaddon, and they were refused (Ezra 4:1-3). They wanted to share in the building to hinder it, and after being refused they used secret plots and persuasions to stop it (1 Esdras 5:73). They weakened the hands of Judah, hired counsellors from Cyrus until Darius, wrote accusations to the king, and made the Jews cease by force and power until the second year of Darius (Ezra 4:4-24). No sentence on them is recorded; the work went on when the prophets stirred up the leaders, and Darius commanded the adversaries to leave it alone (Ezra 5:1-2; Ezra 6:6-12).
offenseFull: The scripture calls them adversaries before they even speak, and adversary means enemies; the forefathers discerned in the spirit that these were not friends. They were the nations the king of Assyria placed in Samaria in place of the children of Israel, which is real gentrification; they feared not the Lord, and even after the lions every nation made gods of its own, so they lied when they said they had sought Israel’s God (2 Kings 17:24-33). These settler nations feared the Most High yet served their graven images to this day, and as a nation Israel does the same, serving the gods of the nations (2 Kings 17:41).

Zerubbabel, Jeshua and the chief of the fathers answered that the strangers had nothing to do with them; they themselves together would build to the Lord, as Cyrus had commanded (Ezra 4:3). The forefathers understood that the work of the Most High is not shared with other nations; this is not an all-inclusive thing but meant for Israel only. Zerubbabel was not subcontracting work to the heathen, for he knew the scriptures: make no covenant with the inhabitants of the land, nor marriages, for they will turn away thy son to serve other gods (Exodus 34:12; Deuteronomy 7:2-4). Never trust thine enemy: though he pretends to help, his whole objective is to undermine the build, and when he has what he came for his countenance changes (Ecclesiasticus 12:10-18). We ourselves together is a strong four words, and the nations do not like it, for they broke Israel in slavery to be dependent on them. J. Edgar Hoover named the unity of the so-called Black people the greatest threat to the United States: unity under the Bible, under Christ, Blacks, Hispanics and Natives coming back as the twelve tribes of Israel.

Then the people of the land weakened the hands of Judah and troubled them in building: the whole purpose of the other nations coming to join is to weaken the hands of Israel so that it cannot build (Ezra 4:4). The objective of their joining Israel’s movements, from the founding of the NAACP onward, has been to weaken the movement and make it of none effect, and the FBI records show the surveillance and disruption of Black leaders and civil rights organizations. Such offers are infiltration, like the informant in the Black Panthers, and J. Edgar Hoover had informants in all the groups; it is the same today, the secret plots, popular persuasions and commotions of 1 Esdras (1 Esdras 5:70-73). They hired counsellors against them all the days of Cyrus until Darius, a hindrance stretching across the kings in between, and the temple was delayed about twenty years (Ezra 4:5). They have taken crafty counsel against thy people and consulted against thy hidden ones, Israel today, that the name of Israel be no more in remembrance; the first of that confederacy is the tabernacles of Edom, the so-called white man (Psalms 83:3-6).

Rehum the chancellor and Shimshai the scribe wrote against Jerusalem, joined by the very nations the Assyrian king had set in Samaria, calling it a rebellious and bad city that would pay no tribute (Ezra 4:8-16). It is called propaganda, slander against Israel; they used the kings who had rebelled, such as Jehoiakim and Zedekiah, to stop the rebuilding, and they were successful. The same is seen today in labels such as black identity extremists, put forth to stop the spiritual temple from being built and to weaken the hands of Israel, but they will not prevail (Matthew 16:18).
judgmentFull: The king answered that the records showed Jerusalem had made insurrection of old, and commanded the work to cease until he gave commandment (Ezra 4:17-22). Rehum and Shimshai went up in haste and made the Jews cease by force and power: by force meaning military, and by power meaning more extreme legislative laws, which is coming (Ezra 4:23). For two years nothing was built, not one tool, not one brick, until the second year of Darius (Ezra 4:24; 1 Esdras 5:73).

Then Haggai and Zechariah stirred up the leaders, and Zerubbabel and Jeshua rose again to build; the work of the house does not get done unless the prophets and the people gather and labour together (Ezra 5:1-2; Zephaniah 2:1-3). The heathen always keep records on the children of Israel, so the matter had to be proven from the rolls, and the roll of Cyrus’s decree was found at Achmetha (Ezra 5:17; Ezra 6:1-2). Darius commanded Tatnai and his companions to leave the work alone, the cost to be paid from the king’s tribute beyond the river; once a Persian decree was made it was upheld rather than vetoed (Ezra 6:6-8; Esther 8:8). Whoever altered the decree was to be hanged on timber pulled from his own house, and God was called on to destroy any king or people who tried to destroy the house (Ezra 6:11-12). The house was finished, and the children of the captivity kept the dedication with joy (Ezra 6:14-16).

The curses are a revolving door: the stranger that is within thee, the other nations, gets up above Israel very high, and Israel comes down very low, at the bottom then and at the bottom today (Deuteronomy 28:43-44). Israel is yet this day in captivity, scattered for a reproach and a curse and subject to payments, according to the iniquities of the fathers (Baruch 3:8).

cases.name: Zerubbabel and Joshua the high priest
cases.charge: Obeying the voice of the Lord their God and the words of Haggai the prophet; humbling themselves under the prophet’s correction, fearing before the Lord, and rising up to work in the house of the Lord of hosts
cases.summary: In the second year of Darius the word came by Haggai to Zerubbabel the governor and Joshua the high priest, to a people saying the time was not come to build the Lord’s house, and it turned their attention to what had been happening to their own labour while that house lay waste (Haggai 1:1-11). Zerubbabel, Joshua and all the remnant obeyed the voice of the Lord and the words of Haggai and feared before him, and the Lord stirred up their spirit and they worked on his house (Haggai 1:12-14). They humbled themselves, because they knew it was the word of the Lord (Haggai 1:12). The Most High promised that the glory of the latter house would be greater than the former and made Zerubbabel as a signet (Haggai 2:9; Haggai 2:23).
offenseFull: Zerubbabel means born in Babylon; one of Israel’s forefathers was named Zerubbabel. He was one of the king’s bodyguards, of noble character, and when the three guards contended he cut down the answers that sought favour and spoke for truth (1 Esdras 4:13-41). He asked nothing for himself, no silver, no gold, no woman to marry, but that the king remember his vow to build Jerusalem and the temple the Edomites burned; he thought about his people and the temple, and that should be Israel’s mentality (1 Esdras 4:42-46). With Jeshua he built the altar as written in the law of Moses, despite fear of the surrounding peoples, and laid the foundation (Ezra 3:1-13).

Then the heathen of the land hindered the building by secret plots, popular persuasions and commotions for the space of two years (1 Esdras 5:72-73). Zerubbabel and Joshua were given a job to do, and they fell back into battle fatigue, when fear and the lust of temptation come upon you and you renege on the promise you made to the Lord. They gave in to the secret plots, popular persuasions and commotions of the nations; they just gave up, and the Lord sent Haggai to them. The top two men fell back and took care of their own personal lives, living in the nice house with the new roof while the Lord’s house was a shambles (Haggai 1:4).

Consider your ways means examine yourself, and it is not only for Zerubbabel (Haggai 1:5; 2 Corinthians 13:5). They sowed much and brought in little and put their wages in a bag with holes, because the Lord’s house lay waste while every man ran to his own house (Haggai 1:6-9). That is why many of Israel are always struggling after the forty-eight and fifty-two hours they give the job: God is always second or third, just as with Zerubbabel. Joshua stood before the angel clothed in filthy garments, with Satan at his right hand to resist him, and the Lord rebuked Satan and called Joshua a brand plucked out of the fire (Zechariah 3:1-3). The filthy garments mean his spirit was not right, like the guest without a wedding garment; the wedding garment is being clothed with God’s laws (Matthew 22:11).

Then Zerubbabel, Joshua and all the remnant obeyed the voice of the Lord and the words of Haggai, and feared before the Lord (Haggai 1:12). They took heed; they did not say, I am over you, for they knew it was the word of the Lord. Joshua was the high priest and Zerubbabel the governor, and Haggai held neither position; Zerubbabel could have had him arrested, but he recognised the word of the Lord and humbled himself, and correcting a brother is love.
judgmentFull: Joshua’s iniquity was caused to pass from him and he was clothed with change of raiment and a fair mitre: the change of raiment is Israel becoming righteous, keeping the commandments, putting the Most High first and dealing rightly with him and with Israel’s own people (Zechariah 3:4-5; Psalms 132:9). The Lord promised to bring forth his servant the BRANCH, which is the remnant of Israel, Judah and Benjamin and Levi (Zechariah 3:8). The Branch is also Christ, whose line runs through Zerubbabel, and the iniquity of the land removed in one day is Christ dying on the cross (Zechariah 3:9; Matthew 1:12-16).

To Zerubbabel the word was not by might nor by power but by my spirit: he was one of the top fighters who could break bones, but the spirit of the Lord is what overcomes (Zechariah 4:6). The great mountain that became a plain before him is Babylon the Great, the destroying mountain, Babylon then and Babylon today, America, which destroys all nations (Zechariah 4:7; Jeremiah 51:25). Not only would Christ come from Zerubbabel’s lineage; Zerubbabel would bring forth the headstone, and his hands that laid the foundation also finished the temple, and these verses also go into the last days (Zechariah 4:7-9). The two olive trees, the two anointed ones that empty out the golden oil, which is the word of God, are Moses and Elijah; the reading is in layers, for they are also Joshua and Zerubbabel and the northern and southern kingdoms (Zechariah 4:11-14; Revelation 11:4).

The shaking of all nations is the third woe, when the Lord destroys all nations; the desire of all nations is their gold, silver, pearls and riches, all that the nations have been stealing and storing coming back to Israel, and the latter house is the third temple (Haggai 2:6-9). The latter house is also the house that Christ builds, greater than the house Solomon built (Haggai 2:9). The peace promised in that house has not come to fruition yet, because there is no peace in Israel now (Haggai 2:9).

He would make Zerubbabel as a signet, for he had chosen him: God chose a prominent figure, a governor, to do his work, and those in prominent positions can still be used by the Lord (Haggai 2:23). Zerubbabel was as a signet on the right hand, and so was Jesus the son of Josedec, who in their time built the house (Ecclesiasticus 49:11-12). The house was finished in the sixth year of Darius, in the month Adar (Ezra 6:14-15). Israel should walk in the footsteps of Zerubbabel: not deceitful with one another, not envious, not hateful, not filled with guile.

cases.name: Ezra
cases.charge: Preparing his heart to seek the law of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments; proclaiming a fast at the river Ahava, and being ashamed to ask the king for soldiers after saying the hand of God is upon all them that seek him
cases.summary: Ezra, of the true priestly line of Aaron and a ready scribe in the law of Moses, went up from Babylon in the seventh year of Artaxerxes, for he had prepared his heart to seek the law of the Most High, to do it, and to teach statutes and judgments in Israel (Ezra 7:1-10). At the river Ahava he proclaimed a fast and was ashamed to ask the king for soldiers, having testified that the hand of God is upon all who seek him for good, and the Lord brought them through (Ezra 8:21-32). In Jerusalem he read the law in the open street while the Levites gave the sense (Nehemiah 8:1-8).
offenseFull: His genealogy runs through Zadok and Phinehas to Eleazar the son of Aaron, marking him a priest of the true line, and the king granted all his requests because the hand of the Most High was upon him (Ezra 7:1-6). He came on the scene roughly fifty-eight to sixty years after the temple was built, around 458 BC; the history of Esther fits between Ezra 6 and Ezra 7. Preparing the heart means setting the mind and spirit in order, examining oneself and putting away the weak nature of sin before teaching others; it is setting the house in order and casting off mortal thoughts (Ezra 7:10; 2 Esdras 14:13-14). Ezra had very great skill, so that he omitted nothing of the law, and that skill came because he prayed and fasted to understand; whoever lacks wisdom may ask of God, who gives liberally (1 Esdras 8:7; James 1:5). He prepared his heart to teach the law at home in Jerusalem because he understood that Israel went into captivity for not keeping the commandments, and the reason Israel is still suffering to this day is that it rejects God’s commandments. Pastors and leaders are not able to give the sense of the scriptures because they do not prepare their heart to seek the law of the Lord and to do it; Ezra did, and so did David, Christ, Paul and the apostles, and the formula is keeping the commandments of God and the faith of the Son of God.

Artaxerxes and his counsellors gave silver and gold for the house of God, even from the king’s treasure, letting the captivity return with the treasures of Babylon, as the nations will one day bring back all Israel’s substance (Ezra 7:15-20; Isaiah 60:5-6). The priests and Levites were freed from toll, tribute and custom: this is using the favour of those set over you without abusing it (Ezra 7:24). A heathen king supported the work of the prophets though he was not an Israelite, and Ezra blessed the Most High who put it in the king’s heart (Ezra 7:27-28). Finding none of the sons of Levi at Ahava, Ezra knew which men among him had understanding and called on them to bring ministers for the house (Ezra 8:15-20).

He proclaimed a fast that they might afflict their souls and seek a right way for themselves, their little ones and their substance; to afflict the soul is to fast, taking neither food nor water, and one may fast and pray for wisdom and a right path (Ezra 8:21; Isaiah 58:5). The Jews had enemies in the lands they had to pass through, from the decree of Haman in Esther’s time, and they would have to travel among those who wanted to destroy them. He would not go back and ask the king for soldiers when he had just told him that God fights for those who keep his commandments, and that his power and wrath are against all who forsake him (Ezra 8:22). Unlike Ezra, Nehemiah was sent with captains of the army and horsemen (Nehemiah 2:9).
judgmentFull: They fasted and besought God, and he was entreated of them (Ezra 8:23). Twelve of the chief priests weighed the money so they knew the balance, and it was weighed again at Jerusalem to make sure there was no foul play; the hand of God delivered them from the enemy and from such as lay in wait by the way (Ezra 8:24-34; 1 Esdras 8:54-64).

In Jerusalem all the people gathered as one man before the water gate, and Ezra read the law from morning until midday to men and women and all that could understand (Nehemiah 8:1-3). The Most High does not favour camps and closed rooms: Ezra stood in the open street to teach, men and women together (Nehemiah 8:3-4). The Levites read distinctly and gave the sense, and teaching is meant to bring understanding, not merely to be recited (Nehemiah 8:8). That is the model of teaching: read distinctly, give the sense, cause the people to understand; you hear the law, thou shalt not steal, then learn what it means and when to apply it. It is the job of the prophets to give the sense, and that is the clear distinction between the real prophets of the Most High and the false pastors. Ezra stood above all the people as their leader, the chief priest and reader, and the people lifted up their hands, bowed their heads and worshipped with their faces to the ground; that is how you pray (Nehemiah 8:5-6; 1 Esdras 9:49). They kept the feast of tabernacles in booths as not since the days of Joshua (Nehemiah 8:13-18).

The law was burnt, and the forefathers had grown up seventy years in Babylon not keeping tabernacles or the laws; no man knew the works of God, but Ezra knew, for he was brought up in the law (2 Esdras 14:21). He asked the Most High to send the Holy Ghost into him to write all that had been done since the beginning, that men may find the path; and as Moses went up to Sinai forty days, Ezra was forty days with five men ready to write swiftly (2 Esdras 14:22-26). He drank the cup like fire, his heart uttered understanding and his spirit strengthened his memory, and in forty days they wrote two hundred and four books, the last seventy kept for the wise among the people (2 Esdras 14:38-47). The spirit strengthened his memory, but it cannot strengthen your memory if you have nothing in your memory: Ezra read the whole Bible many times. They that remain shall rejoice within four hundred years, counted from the time of Ezra to Christ (2 Esdras 7:28).

cases.name: The returned exiles who married strange wives
cases.charge: Not separating themselves from the people of the lands; taking their daughters for themselves and for their sons, so that the holy seed mingled itself with the people of those lands; the princes and rulers chief in the trespass
cases.summary: Ezra mourned and confessed the sin as the same trespass that carried the fathers into captivity, and the congregation made a covenant to put away the strange wives and the children born of them (Ezra 9:3-15; Ezra 10:1-17). A generation later Nehemiah found Jews married to wives of Ashdod, Ammon and Moab and contended with them (Nehemiah 13:23-28).
offenseFull: The princes reported that the people, the priests and the Levites had not separated themselves from the people of the lands, doing after their abominations (Ezra 9:1). The sin is interracial marriage with the nations: they took their daughters for themselves and their sons, so that the holy seed mingled itself with the people of those lands, and it was not only the common people but the Levites, the leaders, that were chief in the trespass (Ezra 9:2). That was always Israel’s issue, from the time of Numbers until now: the desire to mix and mingle with the strange nations round about, and Israel today is no different (1 Esdras 8:69). The commandment was to make no marriages with the nations, not giving daughters to their sons nor taking their daughters, because they would turn the children away from following the Most High (Deuteronomy 7:3-4). Solomon was the prime example: the woman of the nation was not serving the God of Israel, and he was enticed to serve and please her, set up idols and turned from the Lord (1 Kings 11:1-4).

Ezra rent his garment, plucked off the hair of his head and beard and sat astonished, in distress that the people did this after the Most High showed mercy to bring them out of Babylon (Ezra 9:3-4). On his knees he confessed that since the days of the fathers they had been in a great trespass, and for it they, their kings and their priests had been delivered to the sword, to captivity and to spoil; the nation is privy to all the captivities it came from, Egypt, Assyria and Babylon, and knows why it went, yet does the same sins (Ezra 9:5-7). Confusion of face is what Daniel spoke of: Israel was given to confusion of face because it intermingled with the other nations, so that Esther passed for someone of another nation, some of the northern kingdom pass as East Indians or Arabs, and Israel today carries all the complexions of the nations (Ezra 9:7; Daniel 9:7). Ephraim in Latin America looks so mixed because Ephraim mixed himself among the people and the holy seed was mixed (Hosea 7:8; 1 Esdras 8:69).

For a little space grace was shown to leave a remnant and give a little reviving in their bondage: though they were bondmen the Most High extended mercy in the sight of the kings of Persia to set up the house of God, the very leeway that let them come back to the land (Ezra 9:8-9). The Most High had punished them less than their iniquities deserved: Assyria, Babylon, the temple destroyed, the law burnt and hard bondage were less than the nation deserved, for that is how merciful God is (Ezra 9:13). Should they again break the commandments and join in affinity with the people of these abominations, he would be angry until no remnant was left; yet even though the Levites and Israel committed this sin, the Most High still showed them mercy and let them stay in the land (Ezra 9:14-15).
judgmentFull: As Ezra wept and confessed, a very great congregation gathered, and Shechaniah said they had trespassed, yet there was hope in Israel: let them covenant to put away all the wives and the children born of them, according to the law (Ezra 10:1-3). Ezra made all Israel swear to it, the same way an oath was made to keep the commandments (Ezra 10:5). They sat in the street trembling because of the matter and the great rain, which was foul weather, a mighty storm; knowing they had sinned and married strange wives, they were afraid, for the storm and tempest come from the Lord (Ezra 10:9; 1 Esdras 9:6).

Ezra told them to make confession, do the Lord’s pleasure, and separate themselves from the people of the land and from the strange wives; doing his pleasure today is the same, separating from unclean people (Ezra 10:10-11). It pleases God to separate: contrary to what Christianity teaches, there is no interracial marriage with God, and whoever keeps a wife of the other nations and tries to pass her off as Israel must separate and put away the strange wife. If you want the judgment of God to turn from you, repent (Ezra 10:14). Those who had not taken other nations sat and judged, for one who is himself in the sin cannot judge it, and they made an end by the first day of the first month, three months to separate all the men (Ezra 10:16-17). They were able to do it because they had a registry of lineages, a hall of records, of who each one’s father and mother were.

Some put away only the wives and some the wives and children born of them, and the parallel account states plainly that they put away the strange wives together with their children (Ezra 10:44; 1 Esdras 9:36). That covenant meant putting away those particular wives and children; it does not mean an Israelite today with a child by another nation must put away the child (Ezra 10:3). In today’s terms, if the mother of that child wants custody the man will lose in court, and a child raised by a mother of another faith is raised in confusion, so he must count that child and that woman a loss.

Yet the sin came back: Nehemiah saw Jews married to wives of Ashdod, Ammon and Moab, whose children could not speak the Jews’ language, because the fathers were not truly in the house and the children learned their mother’s tongue and customs instead of Hebrew and the law (Nehemiah 13:23-24). He contended with them and made them swear not to give or take daughters in marriage with those nations, reminding them that Solomon, though beloved of his God, was caused to sin by outlandish women, and he chased away the high priest’s grandson, son-in-law to Sanballat, for defiling the priesthood (Nehemiah 13:25-29). Let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall; no one is above the temptation that took Solomon down (1 Corinthians 10:12).
