cases.name: Nehemiah
cases.charge: Fasting and praying before the God of heaven for the remnant; building the wall in fifty-two days with a sword at every builder’s side; taking no governor’s bread; ending the usury of the nobles; shutting the gates on the Sabbath; remember me, O my God, for good
cases.summary: Nehemiah, the Persian king’s cupbearer, came about twelve years after Ezra; when he heard that the remnant in Judah was in affliction and the wall of Jerusalem broken down, he wept, fasted and prayed, confessing the sins of Israel and pleading the promise of gathering (Nehemiah 1:1-11). The king sent him with letters, timber and captains of the army, and the wall was finished in fifty-two days despite all the plots (Nehemiah 2:7-9; Nehemiah 6:15). He refused the governor’s bread for twelve years, made the nobles restore what they had exacted, cast Tobiah out of the temple chamber and shut the gates before the Sabbath, closing the book with the prayer, remember me, O my God, for good (Nehemiah 5:6-18; Nehemiah 13:4-31).
offenseFull: Nehemiah was born at Shushan the palace, in Babylon, and had never seen Jerusalem, though his ancestors had lived and died there; he had heard the stories and read the history, and when he got word that it was in shambles he wept (Nehemiah 1:1-4). The cupbearer held a high-level position in the king’s court, with the king every single day, and still he mourned for the state of his people; no matter how high up he went, he never forgot his people. He confessed the sins of the children of Israel, himself and his father’s house included, and held the Most High to what Moses had taught, both the scattering and the gathering from the uttermost parts when they turn and keep his commandments (Nehemiah 1:6-9; Deuteronomy 30:1-4).

A cupbearer must be of a cheerful countenance, and when the king saw his sorrow Nehemiah was very sore afraid (Nehemiah 2:1-2). It is the same today when Israel’s people are expected to come to work happy and smiling before their employers no matter what is going on. He prayed to the God of heaven before he answered, seeking the Most High even in that moment before the king, and he asked to be sent to build the city of his fathers’ sepulchres (Nehemiah 2:3-5). The king granted him letters and timber according to the good hand of his God upon him: it is not that the heathen love Israel, but that the Lord moves a king to deal well with his remnant (Nehemiah 2:8; Jeremiah 15:11). Sanballat and Tobiah were grieved that a man had come to seek the welfare of Israel; the nations are not happy that Israel repents and keeps the commandments, so do not expect them to throw a party (Nehemiah 2:10).

He never said the work was of his own knowledge or wisdom, but that the Lord’s hand was upon him, and he put that same vision on the men around him so they strengthened their hands (Nehemiah 2:17-18). The wall rose to half its height, for the people had a mind to work: this is the pattern for Israel United in Christ today, a people with a mind to work who understand the condition of their people and the mission to rebuild their minds (Nehemiah 4:6). He set the people by their families with swords, spears and bows, and the answer to fear is to remember the greatness of the Most High and to fight for the family and the people; every builder had his sword at his side, and they put off their clothes only for washing, of one mind to finish the wall (Nehemiah 4:13-23).

When the nobles exacted usury of their brethren he was very angry and rebuked them, for their own brethren were enslaving them over debt though they were one flesh, one people just come out of captivity (Nehemiah 5:1-7). The leaders were taking the people’s land, putting usury on them and having them mortgage their land for food, and Nehemiah instructed them to restore everything they took (Nehemiah 5:9-12). For twelve years he refused the provision owed to his office, because of the fear of God and because the bondage was heavy upon the people; he was about the work and for the people, not the usury of the people (Nehemiah 5:14-19). When a hired prophet urged him to hide in the temple, he answered, should such a man as I flee: real leaders do not run and hide when trouble comes while other men are out in the forefront risking their lives (Nehemiah 6:10-13). The heathen always believe that if they smite the shepherd the sheep will scatter, but it will not work against those that fear God and keep his commandments: kill one leader, and another will rise up. Returning from the king, he cast Tobiah’s household stuff out of the chamber, set the Levites back in their place, and shut the gates when they began to be dark before the Sabbath, for buying and selling on the Sabbath is breaking the commandment (Nehemiah 13:4-22).
judgmentFull: The wall was finished in fifty-two days, and the enemies and the heathen were much cast down, recognising that this was the work and pleasure of the Most High (Nehemiah 6:15-16). Among the elect was Nehemiah, whose renown is great, who raised up the walls that were fallen and set up the gates and bars (Ecclesiasticus 49:13). He founded a library of all Israel’s records, the acts of the kings, the prophets, and David (2 Maccabees 2:13).

He asked the Most High to think upon him for good according to all he had done for the people, and not to wipe out his good deeds for the house of God (Nehemiah 5:19; Nehemiah 13:14; Nehemiah 13:31). God is not unrighteous to forget the work and labour of love shown toward his name, and Nehemiah is remembered by God for his good deeds to this day (Hebrews 6:10). He was so humble that he made sure everybody around him got their names placed in his book, written down one by one, so that they would be remembered by God for generations to come (Nehemiah 3:1-32). Do not be the noble of Tekoa who would not put his neck to the work of the Lord, and be remembered by God in his Bible for that, no matter what status you hold in society (Nehemiah 3:5).

cases.name: Sanballat, Geshem, and Noadiah
cases.charge: Being grieved that a man had come to seek the welfare of Israel; mocking the builders and lying that they would rebel; conspiring to fight against Jerusalem; drawing Nehemiah to Ono to kill him; hiring Shemaiah, with the prophetess Noadiah and other prophets, to put him in fear
cases.summary: Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite, and Geshem the Arabian were other nations, not Israelites, and the record calls them our enemies (Nehemiah 2:10; Nehemiah 6:1). It grieved them that a man had come to seek the welfare of Israel; they mocked the builders, lied that they would rebel against the king, and conspired to fight against Jerusalem (Nehemiah 2:19; Nehemiah 4:1-8). When the wall stood they sought to draw Nehemiah to Ono to kill him, sent an open letter of invented charges, and hired Shemaiah and the prophetess Noadiah to put him in fear (Nehemiah 6:1-14). Nehemiah committed them to the judgment of the Most High, and the wall was finished in fifty-two days (Nehemiah 6:14-16).
offenseFull: When Sanballat and Tobiah heard that Nehemiah had come with the king’s letters, it grieved them exceedingly that a man had come to seek the welfare of the children of Israel, the same opposition seen when the nation tried to rebuild before (Nehemiah 2:9-10). Whenever a man rises up to seek the welfare of his people, he is deemed a threat by the nations, and they will try to buy him off, or demonize him, or kill him. J. Edgar Hoover is an example: COINTELPRO and other operations were set up to assure the destruction of any black leader, and Fred Hampton, Malcolm X, and Medgar Evers are prime examples; he said one of the most dangerous things is black unity, or a black messiah. Stop thinking the nations are going to be happy that our people repented, that the sisters now wear dresses and head wraps and the brothers wear fringes and keep the Sabbath; by keeping the commandments our people are vexing the enemy.

When the building began, they laughed the builders to scorn and asked whether they would rebel against the king (Nehemiah 2:19). These were lies and false accusations, for Nehemiah had the king’s orders and letters, and the heathen do the same thing today. Nehemiah answered that the mockers had no portion, right, or memorial in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 2:20): God is not dealing with you, so what we are doing is none of your business. These other nations are not going to rebuild the nation of Israel; it is going to be us (Lamentations 4:17).

Sanballat mocked the feeble Jews before the army of Samaria, and Tobiah said a fox would break down their wall, the same way the heathen today mock the men who go out in one mind to do the work of the Most High (Nehemiah 4:1-3). When the breaches began to be stopped, the enemies conspired to fight against Jerusalem and slay the builders by surprise (Nehemiah 4:7-11). They saw Israel being productive and did not like it. The same will happen in our day, when the dragon, the other nations, primarily Esau, makes war with the remnant that keep the commandments of God (Revelation 12:17).

With the wall standing, Sanballat and Geshem sent four times for Nehemiah to meet them in the plain of Ono, thinking to do him mischief: they wanted to kill him (Nehemiah 6:1-4). Then came an open letter saying he built the wall to rebel and be their king (Nehemiah 6:5-7). Nehemiah understood propaganda: it was to put fear in them and make them stop the work (Nehemiah 6:8-9). The same is said today, that gathering blacks and Latinos means planning to overthrow the country, and anytime someone looks out for their welfare it is called racist and hatred.

Then Tobiah and Sanballat hired Shemaiah to tell Nehemiah to hide in the temple, so that he would be afraid, sin, and give them matter for an evil report (Nehemiah 6:10-13). The heathen hired one of his own people to convince the leader to run and hide; he sold his people out. It is a sin to stop the work of God out of fear. Nehemiah also named the prophetess Noadiah and the rest of the prophets; a woman of our own people joined with them (Nehemiah 6:14). The heathen hire certain of our people to come among us and make us afraid in order to hinder the building, and it happens today.
judgmentFull: Nehemiah was doing a great work and could not come down, and his attitude is our attitude: why should the work of God cease (Nehemiah 6:3)? The charges were feigned out of their own heart (Nehemiah 6:8). Should such a man as he flee (Nehemiah 6:11)? Real leaders do not run and hide when trouble comes.

The builders prayed that their reproach be turned upon their own head (Nehemiah 4:4), and Nehemiah asked God to think upon Tobiah, Sanballat, Noadiah, and the prophets according to their works, committing them to the judgment of the Most High; he was praying for God to destroy these evil people (Nehemiah 6:14). No penalty carried out on them is recorded.

The wall was finished in fifty-two days, and the enemies were much cast down, for they perceived that this work was wrought of our God (Nehemiah 6:15-16). They are cast down the same way when they see our people organized and working together, the people of God, the people of the book.

Yet the nobles of Judah kept sending letters to Tobiah, for many in Judah were sworn to him by marriage (Nehemiah 6:17-19). To the end the enemy used those inside to frighten Nehemiah, and anything that can be done to stop the work of the Most High is still done today; the people must keep their spiritual eyes open to see it. The men set over our people must fear God and hate covetousness, not hired the way Sanballat and Tobiah hired that man against Nehemiah; they cannot be bought off or silenced with money (Exodus 18:21).

cases.name: The nobles who exacted usury of their brethren
cases.charge: Exacting usury every one of his brother; taking the lands, vineyards, and houses of their own people and bringing their sons and daughters into bondage
cases.summary: While the wall was being built, a great cry of the people and their wives rose against their brethren the Jews: in the famine they had mortgaged their lands and houses to buy corn and borrowed money for the king’s tribute, and their sons and daughters were brought into bondage (Nehemiah 5:1-5). Redeemed out of captivity and back in their own land, Israel was putting Israel in captivity. Nehemiah rebuked the nobles and the rulers, set a great assembly against them, and made them swear before the priests to restore the lands, the houses, and the hundredth part they had exacted, and the people did according to the promise (Nehemiah 5:6-13).
offenseFull: Even in the middle of the outside threat, a wrong rose up inside the camp among the people themselves (Nehemiah 5:1). Some had to trade for corn simply to keep their large households alive; some had mortgaged their lands, vineyards, and houses to buy corn because of the dearth; some had borrowed money for the king’s tribute upon their lands and vineyards (Nehemiah 5:2-4). The heavy tax drove the people into debt against the very land they depended on.

Their flesh was as the flesh of their brethren, yet their sons and daughters were brought into bondage to be servants, and they had no power to redeem them, for other men had their lands and vineyards (Nehemiah 5:5). Their own brethren were enslaving them over debt, though they were one flesh, one people just come out of captivity. We were redeemed from the Persians and Medes and were back in our own land, and now we were putting each other in captivity.

The cry was against the nobles and the rulers (Nehemiah 5:6-7). The nobles were a group of intellects who were very wealthy: the bourgeoisie of that day. The rulers were the governors ruling before Nehemiah came, and they were exploiting the people: they put taxes on the people, laid usury on them, had them mortgage their lands to get food, and took their land whenever they could not pay it back. That tribute was the usury Nehemiah was speaking of. The same history happened again over here, and our leaders are selling our people back into slavery today.

The law is plain. Usury means interest: you cannot charge your brother or sister interest; if you lend twenty dollars, you get twenty dollars back, nothing more, nothing less (Exodus 22:25). If thy brother be waxen poor, relieve him, though he be a stranger or a sojourner; the stranger there is not a heathen but your own brother sojourning away from his land, and brother, neighbour, and the children of thy people all mean the same thing (Leviticus 25:35; Leviticus 19:18). Take no usury of him, or increase, but fear thy God; lending for the opportunity to make a profit off your own people is evil (Leviticus 25:36-37). A brother waxen poor and sold is not to be compelled to serve as a bondservant, but as an hired servant (Leviticus 25:39-40).
judgmentFull: Nehemiah was very angry when he heard their cry; the oppression of the people by their own brethren stirred his anger (Nehemiah 5:6). He consulted with himself, rebuked the nobles and rulers for exacting usury every one of his brother, and set a great assembly against them (Nehemiah 5:7). Nehemiah got all Israel against the nobles. Sometimes a show of force is necessary to get the rich among our people off the backs of the poor, because at times they will do worse to you than the white man.

He reminded them that after their ability they had redeemed their brethren the Jews which were sold unto the heathen; would they now sell their own brethren? They held their peace and found nothing to answer, for they knew they were guilty (Nehemiah 5:8). It was not good what they did; they ought to walk in the fear of God because of the reproach of the heathen their enemies, which proves that the heathen are our enemies (Nehemiah 5:9). Whenever we were desolate and in ruins and the heathen were able to come against us, it was because of sin and evil in the land, and here it was the rulers dealing wickedly with the people.

He pleaded that they leave off this usury and restore that same day the lands, vineyards, oliveyards, and houses, with the hundredth part of the money, corn, wine, and oil they had exacted: give all their stuff back, give them their children back, and ask nothing else (Nehemiah 5:10-11). They promised to restore it and require nothing, and he took an oath of them before the priests (Nehemiah 5:12). He shook his lap, that God would shake out every man from his house and labour who did not perform it, and all the congregation said Amen and praised the Lord, and the people did according to the promise (Nehemiah 5:13). The principle of restitution still applies among brothers and sisters in the body (Exodus 22:1).

Nehemiah set the example. For twelve years as governor he did not eat the bread of the governor, while the former governors had been chargeable to the people and their servants bore rule over them; he did not do so because of the fear of God (Nehemiah 5:14-15). Leaders must always deal right with the people. He bought no land and gave himself and his servants to the work of the wall, because the bondage was heavy upon the people (Nehemiah 5:16-18). He was about the work and for the people, not the usury of the people, and he committed his labour to the remembrance of the Most High (Nehemiah 5:19).

cases.name: Eliashib and Tobiah the Ammonite
cases.charge: Eliashib the priest, allied unto Tobiah the Ammonite, preparing him a great chamber in the courts of the house of God where the offerings and the tithes of the Levites were laid; a grandson of the high priest son in law to Sanballat the Horonite
cases.summary: They read in the book of Moses that the Ammonite and the Moabite should not come into the congregation of God for ever, and the people separated from Israel all the mixed multitude (Nehemiah 13:1-3). Yet Eliashib the priest, who had the oversight of the chambers of the house of God, was allied unto Tobiah the Ammonite and gave him a place to live in the temple of God, and one of the sons of Joiada, the high priest’s son, was son in law to Sanballat the Horonite (Nehemiah 13:4-5; Nehemiah 13:28). Nehemiah came back, cast out Tobiah’s household stuff, cleansed the chambers, set the Levites back in their place, and chased away the son of Joiada (Nehemiah 13:7-14; Nehemiah 13:28-29).
offenseFull: On that day they read in the books of Moses that the Ammonite and the Moabite should not come into the congregation of God for ever, because they met not Israel with bread and water but hired Balaam against them to curse them, and the Most High turned the curse into a blessing (Nehemiah 13:1-2; Deuteronomy 23:3-5). When the people heard the law they separated from Israel all the mixed multitude, cutting off what the law said to cut off (Nehemiah 13:3).

But before this, Eliashib the priest, having the oversight of the chamber of the house of God, was allied unto Tobiah, and prepared him a great chamber where they had laid the meat offerings, the frankincense, the vessels, and the tithes of corn, new wine, and oil for the Levites, the singers, and the porters (Nehemiah 13:4-5). Eliashib gave Tobiah a place to live in the temple of God, when that people were not even allowed among us. This heathen came back in because time had passed: while Nehemiah was gone they began to intermingle themselves again and had the mixed multitude back among us.

This shows why Sanballat and Tobiah knew what was going on all through the building: they were allies, and letters went back and forth (Nehemiah 6:17-19). The nobles of Judah, the bourgeoisie of that day, sent many letters to Tobiah, the enemy of our race, and they reported his good deeds before Nehemiah: these are good people, good folks. There is always a snake among us, a Judas, who aligns himself with the heathen to hinder the building; it is always among our own people, someone feeding the enemy what we are doing.

Eliashib’s own house was bound to the enemy, for one of the sons of Joiada his son was son in law to Sanballat the Horonite, the same Sanballat who was plotting to kill Nehemiah and was in league with Tobiah (Nehemiah 13:28). All this took place while Nehemiah was not at Jerusalem, for in the two and thirtieth year of Artaxerxes he had gone back to the king (Nehemiah 13:6). Malachi filled in for Nehemiah in his absence. A lot of the chief priests and Levites made leagues with the other nations, causing the people to sin: they departed out of the way, caused many to stumble at the law, corrupted the covenant of Levi, and were partial in the law (Malachi 2:7-9).
judgmentFull: When Nehemiah came back and understood the evil Eliashib had done for Tobiah, it grieved him sore; he cast forth all the household stuff of Tobiah, commanded the chambers cleansed, and brought back the vessels of the house of God (Nehemiah 13:7-9). He threw Tobiah’s stuff out of the temple into the street, for according to the law that man should not even have been in the temple. The chamber had to be cleansed because the heathen had been living in it, not keeping the commandments of God but worshipping idols.

He found that the portions of the Levites had not been given, so that the Levites and the singers had fled every one to his field; he contended with the rulers, asked why the house of God was forsaken, set the Levites back in their place, and made faithful men treasurers to distribute unto their brethren (Nehemiah 13:10-14).

The son of Joiada who was son in law to Sanballat he chased away, and he asked God to remember them, because they had defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and of the Levites (Nehemiah 13:28-29). For being partial in the law the Lord made the priests contemptible and base before all the people, and that is why our people Levi, living in Haiti today, are base before the people (Malachi 2:9).

So he cleansed them from all strangers and appointed the wards of the priests and the Levites, every one in his business (Nehemiah 13:30-31). The Bible is not about assimilation or integration; it is about separation, because the Lord says we are a royal priesthood and a holy nation, and he has severed us from all people; we are not to mingle our royal blood with the heathen.

cases.offense: On that day they read in the books of Moses that the Ammonite and the Moabite should not come into the congregation of God for ever, because they met not Israel with bread and water but hired Balaam against them to curse them, and the Most High turned the curse into a blessing (Nehemiah 13:1-2; Deuteronomy 23:3-5). When the people heard the law they separated from Israel all the mixed multitude, cutting off what the law said to cut off (Nehemiah 13:3).
cases.judgment: When Nehemiah came back and understood the evil Eliashib had done for Tobiah, it grieved him sore; he cast forth all the household stuff of Tobiah, commanded the chambers cleansed, and brought back the vessels of the house of God (Nehemiah 13:7-9). He threw Tobiah’s stuff out of the temple into the street, for according to the law that man should not even have been in the temple. The chamber had to be cleansed because the heathen had been living in it, not keeping the commandments of God but worshipping idols.

cases.name: The Sabbath traders of Jerusalem and Tyre
cases.charge: Treading winepresses, bringing in sheaves, and carrying burdens into Jerusalem to sell on the Sabbath day; men of Tyre selling fish and all manner of ware on the Sabbath to the children of Judah
cases.summary: The people had sworn that if the people of the land brought ware or victuals to sell on the Sabbath, they would not buy it (Nehemiah 10:31). Yet while Nehemiah was away, men of Judah trod winepresses and brought burdens into Jerusalem on the Sabbath, and men of Tyre sold fish and all manner of ware to the children of Judah (Nehemiah 13:15-16). Buying and selling on the Sabbath is breaking the commandment. Nehemiah contended with the nobles, shut the gates when it began to be dark before the Sabbath, and warned the merchants that he would lay hands on them, and from that time they came no more on the Sabbath (Nehemiah 13:17-21).
offenseFull: When the covenant was sealed the people swore that if the people of the land brought ware or victuals on the Sabbath day to sell, they would not buy it of them on the Sabbath or on the holy day: on the Sabbath we did not buy things from anyone (Nehemiah 10:31).

In those days Nehemiah saw some in Judah treading winepresses on the Sabbath, bringing in sheaves, lading asses, and bringing wine, grapes, figs, and all manner of burdens into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day to sell (Nehemiah 13:15). There dwelt men of Tyre also, merchants bringing in fish and all manner of ware, and they sold it on the Sabbath to the children of Judah and in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 13:16). The same is done today when merchants move into a black or urban community, set up shop, and make their money off of us. When you see the stores open on the Sabbath day, that is evil.

While Nehemiah was away with the king, the rulers again allowed the other nations to come in: Tobiah the heathen was back in the temple, they were intermixed again with Moab and Ammon, and men of Tyre came in buying and selling on the Sabbath (Nehemiah 13:4-6; Nehemiah 13:16).

The commandment is to remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy (Exodus 20:8-10). The word says remember because Israel would forget it: in this captivity the people were forced to serve other gods and their religions, and the Sabbath was lost through forced conversion. The Sabbath is a sign between the Most High and the children of Israel for ever; the nations do not have this Sabbath, and adopted Sunday worship is not the true Sabbath given to the children of Israel (Exodus 31:13-17). There is no buying or selling on the Sabbath or on the holy day, so gas and food are bought before sundown.
judgmentFull: Nehemiah contended with the nobles of Judah for profaning the Sabbath: their fathers had done the same, and God brought all this evil upon the city, yet they brought more wrath upon Israel (Nehemiah 13:17-18). Buying and selling on the Lord’s Sabbath profanes it. We had gone into captivity for breaking God’s law, and on the return from the Persian captivity to Jerusalem there were people trying to get us to sin again.

When the gates of Jerusalem began to be dark before the Sabbath he commanded that they be shut and not opened till after the Sabbath, and set his own servants at the gates so that no burden would be brought in on the Sabbath day (Nehemiah 13:19). This shows that the Sabbath begins when it is dark: it starts Friday at sundown and runs until sundown on the seventh day, from even unto even, and does not begin at sunrise (Leviticus 23:32).

The merchants and sellers of all kind of ware lodged without Jerusalem once or twice, waiting by the wall and the gates to sell to us their products (Nehemiah 13:20). He testified against them and said that if they did so again he would lay hands on them, and from that time forth they came no more on the Sabbath (Nehemiah 13:21). This laying on of hands is not a blessing but a serious warning, and the merchants knew he was not joking. Our forefathers did not play games, especially when it came to these other nations. The prophets of God were not mealy mouthed and soft like the pastors of today, and the elders trembled at their coming (1 Samuel 16:4).

He commanded the Levites to cleanse themselves and to come and keep the gates to sanctify the Sabbath day, and asked God to remember him and spare him according to the greatness of his mercy (Nehemiah 13:22).

cases.name: Bigthan and Teresh
cases.charge: Two of the king’s chamberlains, of those which kept the door, being wroth and seeking to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus: a plot to kill the king from within his own house
cases.summary: While Mordecai sat in the king’s gate, two of the king’s chamberlains that kept the door, Bigthan and Teresh, were wroth and sought to lay hands on king Ahasuerus, plotting a coup against him (Esther 2:21). Mordecai told it to Esther, Esther told the king in Mordecai’s name, and when it was searched out and found true both were hanged on a tree, and it was written in the book of the chronicles (Esther 2:22-23). Haman sought to harm Mordecai and his people because of the two eunuchs, for Haman was behind the plot (Rest of Esther 12:6). That record came up on a sleepless night and turned Haman’s purpose back on him (Esther 6:1-11).
offenseFull: Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjamite, was carried away from Jerusalem with Jeconiah king of Judah (Esther 2:5-6). Saul and Mordecai came out of the same line; this was not a regular line but a mighty Benjamite line (1 Samuel 9:1-2). Esther was the daughter of Mordecai’s uncle: they were cousins, not uncle and niece. Her parents died, and Mordecai took her for his own daughter and raised her (Esther 2:7).

In those days, while Mordecai sat in the king’s gate, two of the king’s chamberlains, Bigthan and Teresh, of those which kept the door, were wroth and sought to lay hands on king Ahasuerus, plotting a coup against him (Esther 2:21). Chamberlains are eunuchs, the men that protect the king, that are by the bed and around the women. The Rest of Esther names them Gabatha and Tharra, the two eunuchs of the king and keepers of the palace: Bigthan and Teresh are the same men as Gabatha and Tharra in the Greek (Rest of Esther 12:1). Mordecai heard their devices and searched out their purposes (Rest of Esther 12:2).

Haman the Agagite, who was in great honour with the king, sought to molest Mordecai and his people because of the two eunuchs (Rest of Esther 12:6). Haman was behind these two men plotting to kill the Persian king; they were set up by Esau. He was second to the king, and if the king was killed he would take over the throne, so Mordecai and his people were in the way. Greece was always in the mix trying to overthrow Persia; the two eunuchs were part of Haman’s people, the assassins he hired to take the Persian throne from inside, for his whole goal was to translate the kingdom of the Persians to the Macedonians (Rest of Esther 16:12-14).
judgmentFull: Mordecai told it to Esther, and Esther told the king in Mordecai’s name; it was found true, both were hanged on a tree, and it was written in the chronicles (Esther 2:22-23). Mordecai told the king these men were plotting to take his life, and that is what a man is supposed to do. He was following the law that a witness who has seen or known of a matter must tell it (Leviticus 5:1). Because of that the Most High blessed Mordecai and Esther, and Israel was saved from that point on.

The king examined the two eunuchs, and after they had confessed it they were strangled; they were strangled, and they were hung on the tree (Rest of Esther 12:3). The king made a record of these things, Mordecai also wrote of them, and the king commanded him to serve in the court and rewarded him (Rest of Esther 12:4-5). Israel wrote down our history and our chronicles, and this deed of Mordecai’s would later help our whole nation.

That night the king could not sleep, and he called for the book of records of the chronicles to be read before him; it was found written that Mordecai had told of Bigthana and Teresh, and that nothing had been done to honour him for it (Esther 6:1-3). The Lord is a mastermind in how he moves, moving even a king’s sleeplessness to set his purpose in motion. At that very moment Haman had come into the outer court to ask that Mordecai be hanged on the gallows he had prepared (Esther 6:4).

Haman, so full of himself that he assumed the king must mean him, laid out the highest honour he could imagine and was made to do it all to Mordecai the Jew, parading him through the street (Esther 6:6-11). What Haman planned for himself was given to the man he hated. This is how the Most High works, and it should put a smile on your face.

cases.name: Haman the Agagite
cases.charge: Thinking scorn to lay hands on Mordecai alone and seeking to destroy all the Jews throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus; slandering Israel as a malicious people; offering ten thousand talents of silver for their destruction; making a gallows fifty cubits high for Mordecai
cases.summary: King Ahasuerus promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, an Amalekite of the line of Esau, above all the princes, and when Mordecai would not bow, Haman sought to destroy all the Jews in the kingdom (Esther 3:1-6). He cast Pur, slandered Israel to the king, offered ten thousand talents of silver, sent letters sealed with the king’s ring to kill every Jew in one day, and at his wife’s counsel built a gallows fifty cubits high for Mordecai (Esther 3:7-15; Esther 5:14). He was made to honour Mordecai, was named by Esther as the adversary, and was hanged on the gallows he had made: this is the Most High, a man of war, and this is how he moves (Esther 6:10-11; Esther 7:6-10).
offenseFull: After Mordecai saved the king’s life, the king promoted Haman the Agagite and set his seat above all the princes, the right hand of the king over Persia (Esther 3:1). This is a descendant of the same Agag whom Saul spared and Samuel hewed in pieces; the Agagites descend from Agag king of the Amalekites, and Amalek descends from Esau (1 Samuel 15:8-9; 1 Samuel 15:33; Genesis 36:12). Haman is an Amalekite, an Edomite. The second letter calls him a Macedonian, a stranger from the Persian blood (Rest of Esther 16:10). Mordecai called him by his real name, Agagite, and the Persians called him a Macedonian: two different names, the same race. Esau was already beginning to change his name.

All the king’s servants bowed and reverenced Haman, but Mordecai bowed not: it is not our custom to bow to any man, the same as the three Hebrew children did not bow to the image in Babylon, for we pledge allegiance to none but the Most High (Esther 3:2-4). When Haman saw it he was full of wrath, and thought scorn to lay hands on Mordecai alone; he sought to destroy all the Jews throughout the whole kingdom (Esther 3:5-6). Why all of them? Remember what Saul was sent to do to Amalek. Haman’s people kept the records, and he knew Mordecai’s line, the line of Kish, was the line sent to destroy his forefathers. Esau forgave Jacob, but his children hold the grudge from generation to generation; they do not forget, and we do. Edom’s hatred sought a death sentence for the entire nation, to erase us out of history.

They cast Pur, the lot, before Haman from Nisan to Adar, and he told the king there was a certain people scattered abroad whose laws were diverse from all people, offering ten thousand talents of silver to have them destroyed; the king gave him his ring (Esther 3:7-10). This is putting a hit out on the entire nation of Israel. The letter painted Israel as a malicious people with laws contrary to all nations, continually despising the commandments of kings, so that the uniting of the kingdoms could not go forward (Rest of Esther 13:4-5). That is the same slander used on us today: they are malicious, they are violent, they are a problem. Is it evil or malicious to teach that a man should not kill, or for a woman to wear a dress, adorn herself in modest apparel, and walk chaste? To the other nations it is, because when Israel keeps God’s commandments they cannot rule.

Letters went out in the king’s name to kill all Jews, young and old, little children and women, in one day, and the king and Haman sat down to drink (Esther 3:12-15). Zeresh his wife and his friends counselled a gallows fifty cubits high, and the thing pleased Haman (Esther 5:14). It was the wife’s idea, for the enemy’s women are in league with the work against Israel; do not think the women or the children of Esau are not like that.
judgmentFull: That night the king learned from the chronicles that Mordecai had saved his life, and Haman, coming to ask for Mordecai’s death, was so full of himself that he assumed the king’s honour must be meant for him; he was made to array Mordecai and proclaim him through the city (Esther 6:1-11). His wise men and his wife told him that if Mordecai was of the seed of the Jews, before whom he had begun to fall, he would not prevail but would surely fall before him (Esther 6:13).

At the second banquet Esther pleaded for her life and the life of her people, sold to be destroyed, and named the adversary and enemy, this wicked Haman (Esther 7:3-6). When Haman fell upon the bed where Esther was, the king took it as an assault on the queen in his own house (Esther 7:7-8). Harbonah told of the gallows fifty cubits high, and they hanged Haman on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai (Esther 7:9-10). This is the Most High, a man of war, and this is how he moves. Haman’s own tongue fell upon himself, and this prophecy will come to pass again: the tables are going to be turned and the people of God delivered (Psalm 64:8).

Everything Haman had was given to Esther and Mordecai (Esther 8:1-2). The Jews in every city were granted to stand for their life, and the ten sons of Haman were slain and hanged on the gallows (Esther 8:11; Esther 9:10-14). His wicked device returned upon his own head, and the days were called Purim after Pur, the lot he cast to consume the Jews, a feast that commemorates the destruction of Israel’s enemies (Esther 9:24-26).

The second letter exposed him: he went about to deprive the king of his kingdom and life, and thought to translate the kingdom of the Persians to the Macedonians (Rest of Esther 16:10-14). He was a spy, undercover in the nation of Persia, a sleeper cell in the Persian government. The Jews whom he delivered to utter destruction were found to be no evildoers but to live by most just laws, and Haman was hanged at the gates of Susa with all his family, the Most High rendering vengeance according to his deserts (Rest of Esther 16:15-18).

cases.name: Mordecai and Esther
cases.charge: Mordecai: bowing not to Haman, nor doing him reverence, for he was a Jew. Esther: gathering the Jews to fast three days, and going in to the king not according to the law: if I perish, I perish
cases.summary: Mordecai would not bow to Haman the Agagite, and when Haman’s wrath became a decree against all the Jews he mourned, prayed, and charged Esther to go in to the king (Esther 3:2-6; Esther 4:1-8). Esther made an excuse, but at Mordecai’s word she fasted three days with the Jews of Shushan and went in not according to the law, ready to perish (Esther 4:10-16). The Most High turned the king’s heart, Haman was hanged on his own gallows, Purim was ordained, and Mordecai was made next to the king (Esther 7:10; Esther 9:20-32; Esther 10:3).
offenseFull: The king promoted Haman the Agagite, of the Agag whom Saul spared; Haman is an Amalekite, an Edomite, which explains his deep disdain for Israel (Esther 3:1; 1 Samuel 15:20). All the king’s servants bowed to him, but Mordecai bowed not, for he had told them he was a Jew (Esther 3:2-4). It is not our custom to bow to any man: we pledge allegiance to none but the Most High, as the three Hebrew children did not bow to the image. Mordecai refused not from contempt or pride: he could have kissed the soles of Haman’s feet for the salvation of Israel, but he would not prefer the glory of man above the glory of God (Rest of Esther 13:12-14).

Because Mordecai would not bow, Edom’s hatred sought a death sentence for the entire nation, to erase us out of history (Esther 3:5-6). Esau forgave Jacob, but his children hold the grudge from generation to generation; they do not forget, and we do. One personal vendetta came upon the whole race, and we go through the same thing on our jobs: because you keep the commandments and wear fringes, the co-worker asks in front of everyone why you dress as you do, then complains to the supervisor. We are the Israelites and we will be persecuted; it may cost your job, but keep the faith, for it may be part of the Most High’s plan.

Haman told the king of a people scattered abroad whose laws were diverse, the same slander used on us today: they are malicious, they are violent, they are a problem (Esther 3:8-9; Rest of Esther 13:4-5). The letters went out to kill all Jews, young and old, little children and women, in one day (Esther 3:13), the curse of a nation that would not regard the old nor show favour to the young (Deuteronomy 28:50). Esau has never shown mercy to us, through the Greek and Roman captivities to the captivity today.

Mordecai put on sackcloth and cried bitterly, and in every province there was mourning and fasting (Esther 4:1-3). A law was passed that every Israelite be put to death without mercy; these things will happen again, and laws are going to be passed under which you cannot be an Israelite or keep God’s commandments. He prayed that if the Most High has appointed to save Israel no man can gainsay him (Rest of Esther 13:8-11).

Charged by Mordecai to go in to the king for her people, Esther answered that whoever came uncalled died (Esther 4:10-11); she made an excuse, though she was the queen the king loved above all the women. Mordecai would not take a weak answer: she would not escape in the king’s house, deliverance would arise from another place, and she and her father’s house would be destroyed (Esther 4:13-14; Romans 15:4). She was put in her position for this very purpose, and the deliverance of Israel cannot be held back: whoever is slothful in the work, the Lord will raise up somebody else, because it will not be stopped.

Esther had the Jews of Shushan fast three days and resolved to go in not according to the law: if she perished, she perished (Esther 4:15-17). She had her mind set right, ready to risk her life for her people. In ashes she confessed that Israel was given to its enemies because it worshipped their gods, the same confession our people must make about why we went into captivity (Rest of Esther 14:1-11). From her youth she had heard how the Lord took Israel from among all people: she was raised right. She abhorred the sign of her high estate as a menstruous rag; unlike our people who love the seats of government and do not fight for their people, she despised the position and fought for her people (Rest of Esther 14:15-16).
judgmentFull: On the third day she stood in the inner court; the king looked fiercely upon her and she fainted, and God changed his spirit into mildness (Esther 5:1-2; Rest of Esther 15:1-16). The king’s heart is in the hand of the Lord (Proverbs 21:1), and the king so easily persuaded by Haman was now persuaded by Esther.

At her banquet she named Haman, and they hanged him on the gallows he had made for Mordecai (Esther 7:3-10). This is the Most High, a man of war, and this is how he moves. The king gave Mordecai his ring, and a second decree let the Jews from India to Ethiopia stand for their lives (Esther 8:1-11); Israel was scattered all through the Persian empire, which shows we have history in these lands (Deuteronomy 28:64). The second letter declared the Jews no evildoers but children of the most high and most mighty living God, the plain testimony of who Israel is (Rest of Esther 16:15-16).

Many of the people of the land became Jews, for the fear of the Jews fell upon them (Esther 8:15-17), a picture of the future when the fear of Israel will be on all nations and they will serve the Most High. Mordecai wrote to keep the fourteenth and fifteenth of Adar every year, the month turned from sorrow to joy; Israel still keeps Purim today (Esther 9:20-28). Purim is a memorial of destruction, the destruction of our enemies and the Lord’s mercy in delivering us, not a day about presents and gifts (Rest of Esther 16:21-23).

Mordecai was next to the king, seeking the wealth of his people (Esther 10:3), and declared that the Most High had done all these things (Rest of Esther 10:4-5). We are going through days of sorrow, but joy is coming as long as we stay in the commandments and trust in the Lord.

cases.offense: The king promoted Haman the Agagite, of the Agag whom Saul spared; Haman is an Amalekite, an Edomite, which explains his deep disdain for Israel (Esther 3:1; 1 Samuel 15:20). All the king’s servants bowed to him, but Mordecai bowed not, for he had told them he was a Jew (Esther 3:2-4). It is not our custom to bow to any man: we pledge allegiance to none but the Most High, as the three Hebrew children did not bow to the image. Mordecai refused not from contempt or pride: he could have kissed the soles of Haman’s feet for the salvation of Israel, but he would not prefer the glory of man above the glory of God (Rest of Esther 13:12-14).
cases.judgment: On the third day she stood in the inner court; the king looked fiercely upon her and she fainted, and God changed his spirit into mildness (Esther 5:1-2; Rest of Esther 15:1-16). The king’s heart is in the hand of the Lord (Proverbs 21:1), and the king so easily persuaded by Haman was now persuaded by Esther.

cases.name: Daniel
cases.charge: Purposing in his heart not to defile himself with the portion of the king’s meat nor with the wine which he drank; kneeling and praying three times a day with his windows open toward Jerusalem, as he did aforetime, after the decree was signed
cases.summary: Daniel, of the king’s seed of Judah, was carried to Babylon with the best and most educated of Israel’s youth to build up a kingdom not their own, and he purposed not to defile himself with the king’s meat and wine; the Most High gave him favour, and he and his companions were found ten times better than all the king’s wise men (Daniel 1:1-20). Under Darius, when his rivals could find no fault in him except concerning the law of his God, he kept praying three times a day toward Jerusalem after the decree was signed, and God shut the lions’ mouths (Daniel 6:1-23). He prospered under Darius and Cyrus and was told he would stand in his lot at the end of the days (Daniel 6:28; Daniel 12:13).
offenseFull: Nebuchadnezzar besieged Jerusalem and carried part of the vessels of the house of God to the treasure house of his god, exactly as the prophets had warned; Isaiah had told Hezekiah that his sons would be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon (Daniel 1:1-2; 2 Kings 20:16-18). The king had the master of his eunuchs bring children of the king’s seed and of the princes, without blemish and skilful in wisdom, to be taught the tongue of the Chaldeans (Daniel 1:3-5). They took the best and the most educated among us and set them to build up their kingdom. Babylon did not take any old body, and Esau did the same thing: they said they needed the best ones, and they put them in North America. It is the same today, where our people serve in the governments and congresses and are used to build up a system that is not our own; often those chosen are not loyal to their own people, assimilated to believe they are a part of the system, and well rewarded for it.

The prince of the eunuchs gave Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah new names, Belteshazzar, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, part of assimilating them into the king’s service (Daniel 1:6-7). Daniel was named after one of the king’s gods, the same thing as Hadassah, whose name was changed to Esther; the heathen always changed our names, and in slavery here they changed them too.

But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the portion of the king’s meat nor with the wine which he drank (Daniel 1:8). God brought him into favour and tender love with the prince of the eunuchs: the Lord said it shall be well with his remnant, and he will cause the enemy to entreat it well in the time of evil (Jeremiah 15:11). They were captives, as we are captive in America, yet they were treated well, because this was part of the Lord’s plan. Daniel asked for ten days’ proof on pulse and water (Daniel 1:9-14). Pulse is vegetables, the green herb the Most High gave for meat in the beginning, when even the animals ate only green herbs (Genesis 1:29-30). At the end of ten days they looked fairer and fatter than all who ate the king’s meat (Daniel 1:15-16).

Under Darius, the presidents and princes sought occasion against Daniel and could find none, because he was faithful and no error or fault was found in him; he was blameless (Daniel 6:1-4). This is how our forefathers lived, and the same spirit we should live in, keeping a conscience void of offence toward God and toward men (Acts 24:16). He lived up to a name, integrity. When Daniel knew the decree was signed, he went into his house, and with his windows open toward Jerusalem he kneeled three times a day and prayed and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime (Daniel 6:10). Toward Jerusalem is the point: not only to the east, but toward our homeland from wherever you are. We should pray at least three times a day, as Daniel did, and the Lord was with Daniel through both captivities.
judgmentFull: God gave the four children knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom, and Daniel understanding in all visions and dreams, and in all matters of wisdom the king found them ten times better than all the magicians and astrologers in his realm (Daniel 1:17-20). The Most High gave them that understanding, and it is impossible that they could be outdone, the same as Moses before the magicians of Egypt. Young Daniel had that understanding when he separated the two elders who accused Susanna and convicted them of false witness by their own mouths (Susanna 1:45-62). Daniel continued even to the first year of Cyrus (Daniel 1:21).

Cast into the den, he told the king that God had sent his angel and shut the lions’ mouths, because innocency was found in him, and he came up unhurt because he believed in his God (Daniel 6:16-23). As he sat in the den the Most High sent the prophet Habakkuk by an angel to carry him food, for he does not forsake them that seek and love him (Bel and the Dragon 1:33-39). When a man’s ways please the Most High, he makes even his enemies to be at peace with him; Daniel was operating in a righteous spirit (Proverbs 16:7). Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius and of Cyrus the Persian (Daniel 6:25-28); he had a wise and humble spirit, and is one of the few well known men of the Bible about whom nothing negative is written; his life was marked by faith, prayer, courage, consistency, and lack of compromise.

Daniel was told to go his way till the end, for he would rest and stand in his lot at the end of the days (Daniel 12:13). Rest means he shall die, and this is the Most High sending these leaders back to us. When the book is unsealed and the knowledge of who the Israelites are comes back in the time of the end, Daniel will be there raising up his people, understanding what was not expounded to him when he was alive. He is on the earth in the end times, of the tribe of Judah, teaching the twelve tribes of Israel to repent and keep the commandments of God and unsealing the mysteries hidden from ancient times; we do not know who he is.

cases.name: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego
cases.charge: Not serving the king’s gods nor worshipping the golden image he had set up, according to the law; not careful to answer the king, for their God was able to deliver them, and if not, they would still never bow
cases.summary: Nebuchadnezzar set up a golden image in the plain of Dura and commanded every people to fall down and worship it at the sound of the music, on pain of the burning fiery furnace (Daniel 3:1-6). Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, set over the province, would not bow, because of the law, and told the raging king that their God was able to deliver them, and that even if he did not, they would not serve his gods (Daniel 3:12-18). They were cast bound into a furnace heated seven times over, walked unhurt in the fire with a fourth, and came out without even the smell of smoke; the king blessed their God and promoted them (Daniel 3:19-30).
offenseFull: Nebuchadnezzar made an image of gold sixty cubits high, about a hundred and ten feet, and gathered the rulers of the provinces to its dedication (Daniel 3:1-3). It was like the dedication and ribbon-cutting ceremony held when a monument or a new federal building goes up. Nebuchadnezzar had set up a one world religion, the same thing they are trying to do today: a man sets himself up as the Messiah on earth, and Daniel 3 is coming to life in our time.

When the music sounded all were to fall down and worship or be cast into the furnace (Daniel 3:4-7). The national anthem at ball games and ceremonies, hat off and hand over the heart, is a form of worshipping the image of the eagle today. In the last days all that dwell on the earth worship the image of the beast: Rome, the mother of the Christian denominations, made war with the saints, the twelve tribes, and enslaved them, and the whole world worships its image as Jesus (Revelation 13:6-8).

Certain Chaldeans accused the three men (Daniel 3:8-12). They were high up in that organization, way up in government, and they still refused to bend. A believer today might show up to the Christmas party at work because he does not want to get fired; these men would not. They did not bow because of the law: no other gods, no graven image, no standing image set up to bow down to it (Exodus 20:3-5; Leviticus 26:1). Israel had images in the temple, the great angels and the ox, but nobody bowed down to them.

Brought before the king in his rage, they were asked who is that God that could deliver them out of his hands (Daniel 3:13-15). He was talking tough, talking big, challenging our God, though he had already admitted, when his dream was answered, that the God of Israel is a God of gods; after that he fell back into forgetfulness (Daniel 2:47). They answered that they were not careful to answer him, not worried: their God was able to deliver them, but if not, they would not serve his gods nor worship the image (Daniel 3:16-18). This is exactly what was read in the law. They understood that God does what he wants, that no one can force the Lord to save him, and that the body is temporal but the spirit lives on. Regardless of anything, they were never bowing down to these images.

The king had the furnace heated seven times more and the three cast in bound, and the flame slew the men who took them up (Daniel 3:19-23). In the fire Azariah confessed that all the Lord had brought upon them was true judgment, because Israel broke the commandments and the curse of the law came upon it (Song of the Three Holy Children 1:3-9). He prayed that they had been delivered into the hands of lawless enemies and an unjust king, the most wicked in all the world. They worked for that king, yet never called him a friend because he gave them position. The other nations give our people position, and they think they must love them; we do not have to hate them or be hateful toward them, but we have to recognize the enemy, for the Lord said we would serve our enemies whom he sent against us (Deuteronomy 28:48).
judgmentFull: The flame streamed forty-nine cubits, about seventy-three and a half feet, and burned the Chaldeans about the furnace, but the angel of the Lord made the midst of it as a moist whistling wind (Song of the Three Holy Children 1:23-27). The fire did not get out of control: fire is a spirit created for vengeance and takes commandments, and the Lord killed those men (Ecclesiasticus 39:28-29).

The king saw four men loose and unhurt in the fire, and the form of the fourth was like the Son of God (Daniel 3:24-25). Nebuchadnezzar did not know, but the translators understood the fourth was Christ. The sons of God are the angels, and the king himself said their God had sent his angel (Daniel 3:28). The fire had no power on their bodies: not a hair singed, their coats unchanged, not even the smell of smoke on these brothers, because they did not bow to the idol (Daniel 3:26-27).

The king blessed the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who delivered his servants that trusted in him and yielded their bodies rather than serve or worship any god except their own God, decreed that anyone who spoke amiss against their God be cut in pieces, and promoted them in the province (Daniel 3:28-30). We have to apply this to ourselves today: nothing shall stop us from keeping the laws of God, and nothing can keep us from the love of Christ (Romans 8:35). The king understood then that we had our own God; why do people not understand that today? When the nations are brought low they come to know who has the real, true, living God; the Most High is in the midst of Israel, and his people shall never be ashamed (Joel 2:27). But Nebuchadnezzar did not hold true to it; he went right back to his idolatrous ways, and these events will occur again.

cases.name: The Chaldeans who accused the Jews
cases.charge: Coming near and accusing the Jews to the king, that Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego served not his gods nor worshipped the golden image, because the righteous would not bow down to it
cases.summary: When all the peoples fell down before the golden image, certain Chaldeans came near and accused the Jews, naming Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, whom the king had set over the province, because the righteous would not bend themselves down and worship (Daniel 3:7-12). The three were cast into the furnace and came out unharmed; the flame slew the men who took them up, and the Lord killed the Chaldeans about the furnace (Daniel 3:19-30).
offenseFull: Nebuchadnezzar set up an image of gold and decreed that all should fall down and worship it at the sound of the music or be cast into the furnace (Daniel 3:1-7). The national anthem at ball games, hat off and hand over the heart, is a form of worshipping the image of the eagle today. Nebuchadnezzar had set up a one world religion, the same thing they are trying to do today; a man sets himself up as the Messiah on earth, and Daniel 3 is coming to life in our time.

They accused the Jews to the king because the righteous would not bend themselves down and worship (Daniel 3:8-12). Their message was: these men you have set over the kingdom are not listening to you; they are a poor example; you must do something. Daniel and the three were promoted over them, and this was their chance to get them killed, win their positions back, and have these four men removed. These men were good but not fully like them, so they highlighted what the Jews were not doing rather than what they were doing: what gets noticed is the birthday card that was not signed. It was opposition; it was a set up.

The reason they did not bow was according to the law: no other gods, no graven image, no bowing down to them (Exodus 20:3-5; Leviticus 26:1). These men were high up in that organization, way up in government, and they refused to bend. The same idolatry came again in Greece; it is like a ring, it is going to continue, and America is not absolved from this (1 Maccabees 1:41-50). It was no longer lawful to keep Sabbath days or ancient feasts or to profess to be a Jew, and that law was just passed in France: that is why they dissolved the IUIC school in France, for to say that you’re a Jew in France is anti-Semitic, hate speech. Some of us may think that will never happen here in America. Don’t be surprised (2 Maccabees 6:6).
judgmentFull: Nebuchadnezzar in his rage threatened the three with the furnace, talking tough, talking big, challenging our God; they answered that their God was able to deliver them, and that they would not serve his gods in any case (Daniel 3:13-18).

Full of fury, the king had the furnace heated seven times more than it was wont, and the flame slew the men who carried the three up to it (Daniel 3:19-22). The flame streamed out above the furnace and burned the Chaldeans it found about it, while the angel of the Lord made the midst of the furnace like a moist wind for the three (Song of the Three Holy Children 1:23-27). People would say the fire got out of control and burnt the Chaldeans, but fire is a spirit, created for vengeance, alive and taking commandments, and it was commanded to kill those Chaldeans. The fire was not just so hot it burnt them up; the Lord killed them (Ecclesiasticus 39:28-29). The king had just seen his men burned, and he did not care; to him they were only soldiers.

The fire had no power on the three, and not even the smell of smoke was on these brothers, because they didn’t bow to the idol (Daniel 3:24-27). The king blessed their God, decreed that whoever spoke amiss against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego be cut in pieces, and promoted the three (Daniel 3:28-30). When the nations are brought low they come to know who has the real, true, living God (Joel 2:27). But Nebuchadnezzar did not hold true to that at all; he went right back to his idolatrous ways, and these events will occur again.
No sentence on the Chaldeans who accused the Jews is recorded.

cases.name: Nebuchadnezzar
cases.charge: Pride: a year after he was warned, boasting of the great Babylon he had built by the might of his power and for the honour of his majesty, with no recognition of the Most High who set him up
cases.summary: Nebuchadnezzar dreamed of a great tree hewn down to a stump till seven times passed, and Daniel told him the tree was he and counselled him to break off his sins by righteousness and his iniquities by showing mercy to the poor (Daniel 4:4-27). A year later he boasted of the great Babylon he had built by his own power, and while the word was in his mouth the kingdom departed from him; he was driven out to eat grass as oxen until he knew that the Most High rules (Daniel 4:28-33). At the end of the days his understanding and his kingdom returned, and he praised the King of heaven, who is able to abase those that walk in pride (Daniel 4:34-37).
offenseFull: Nebuchadnezzar proclaimed the signs the high God had worked toward him and told how a dream made him afraid; at last Daniel came in, named Belteshazzar after the king’s god (Daniel 4:1-9). It is the same thing as Hadassah, whose name was changed to Esther; this is not new for us. The heathen always changed our names to pertain to their religion, in slavery here and as a nation today.

He saw a great tree reaching to heaven, and a watcher and a holy one commanded it hewn down, its stump bound with iron and brass, till seven times passed, to the intent that the living may know that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men and sets over it the basest of men (Daniel 4:10-17). That is what we see today, the basest of men ruling the earth. Base is the root of basement, the lowest level: the Most High has set the lowest of the nations over this world, and the so-called white man, who is thought so high and mighty, is by this verse a base people. Nebuchadnezzar acknowledged that he was that base man whom God set up. The nations are waiting for Israel to wake up, shake off its sins, and take its place as the kings and priests of the earth (Romans 8:19).

Daniel, astonished for an hour, told him the tree was he; the stump meant his kingdom would be kept for him once he knew that the heavens rule (Daniel 4:18-26). Daniel counselled him to break off his sins by righteousness and his iniquities by showing mercy to the poor (Daniel 4:27). It was a warning: you need to walk in righteousness and show mercy to the poor, and the poor were the Israelites.

He had acknowledged Daniel’s God after the first dream, then set up the image and threw the three Hebrews into the furnace; he kept bucking against the Lord. At the end of twelve months, a year after Daniel told him the dream, he boasted of the great Babylon he had built (Daniel 4:28-30). He was very proud and boastful: by the might of his own power, with no recognition of the Most High even after the dream Daniel interpreted for him; he was still delusional.
judgmentFull: While the word was in his mouth a voice from heaven said the kingdom had departed from him, and the same hour he was driven from men, ate grass as oxen till his hairs were grown like eagles’ feathers and his nails like birds’ claws (Daniel 4:31-33). God was still listening a whole year later: do you think that when you run your mouth there is no God listening? As long as the words were still in his mouth, the Lord turned him into an animal: he made him lose his mind so that he would humble himself. The Lord takes out the heathen for their pride, as he did Titus.

At the end of the days he lifted up his eyes to heaven, his understanding returned, and he blessed the Most High, before whom all the inhabitants of the earth are reputed as nothing, and whose hand none can stay (Daniel 4:34-35). When the Most High declares a thing shall come to pass, it comes to pass. All nations before him are counted less than nothing (Isaiah 40:17), and he realized he ruled only because God allowed him to rule.

His reason and the glory of his kingdom returned, and he praised the King of heaven who is able to abase those that walk in pride (Daniel 4:36-37). The Most High brings low and lifts up (1 Samuel 2:7). Israel already understood that the Most High can bring one up and set another down, but the heathen had to learn it by being brought low, literally turned to crawl like a bird with the heart of a beast; this is divine intervention. The dark nations, as Babylon, Egypt and Persia, keep a sense that a God rules over them; Edom has no fear of God nor acknowledgement of him, and will not be humbled this way: he has to be destroyed, for though he exalt himself as the eagle, the Lord will bring him down (Obadiah 1:4). You only rule because God put you there; humble yourself before he draws the picture for you.

cases.name: Belshazzar
cases.charge: Drinking wine with his lords, his wives, and his concubines from the vessels taken out of the temple of the Lord at Jerusalem, in mockery, and praising the gods of gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and stone; not humbling his heart though he knew how the Most High had brought down his father, but lifting himself up against the Lord of heaven
cases.summary: At a feast for a thousand lords, Belshazzar had the golden and silver vessels taken out of the temple at Jerusalem brought in, and he, his princes, his wives, and his concubines drank from them in mockery and praised gods of gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and stone (Daniel 5:1-4). He knew how the Most High had humbled his father and still lifted himself up against the Lord of heaven (Daniel 5:22-23). A hand wrote on the wall, and Daniel read it: God had numbered his kingdom and finished it; he was weighed in the balances and found wanting; his kingdom was divided and given to the Medes and Persians (Daniel 5:25-28). That night Belshazzar was slain, and Darius the Median took the kingdom (Daniel 5:30-31).
offenseFull: This is Belshazzar the king, not Belteshazzar, who is Daniel (Daniel 5:1). Nebuchadnezzar was in power, then he died, and some time later his grandson or great grandson took over; where the text calls Nebuchadnezzar his father, the margin reads grandfather (Daniel 5:2).

While he tasted the wine he commanded the golden and silver vessels that Nebuchadnezzar had taken out of the temple to be brought, so that the king, his princes, his wives, and his concubines might drink from them, and they praised the gods of gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and stone (Daniel 5:2-4). They were mocking the vessels stolen from the temple of the Lord, drinking out of God’s bowls and cups in disrespect: he made the feast with the desire to mock the Most High and the enslavement of Israel. Even before the captivity Israel was warned that it would see these gods of silver and gold in Babylon and was told not to fear or worship them (Baruch 6:3-6).

Daniel set his sin before him. The Most High gave Nebuchadnezzar a kingdom and majesty; whom he would he slew and whom he would he set up, the same power America has (Daniel 5:18-19). When his heart was lifted up and his mind hardened in pride, he parted from the one true God; He was put down from his throne and driven out until he knew that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men (Daniel 5:20-21). When Daniel told him he was the head of gold, Nebuchadnezzar was lifted up in his mind and set himself up as a god, and the Lord cast him down; the Lord is the one that lifts people up and takes them down.

Belshazzar did not humble his heart, though he knew all this, but lifted himself up against the Lord of heaven, drank from the vessels of his house, and praised gods that see not, nor hear, nor know, and the God in whose hand his breath is he did not glorify (Daniel 5:22-23). He knew of his father being chased out of his kingdom and losing his mind, and he still chose to be arrogant; his son still tested the Lord, and praised gods of silver and gold that cannot even save themselves (Baruch 6:12-16). The life a man lives is not his own but lent him, and that breath will be demanded of him one day (Wisdom of Solomon 15:8).
judgmentFull: In the same hour the fingers of a man’s hand wrote on the plaster of the palace wall, and the king’s countenance changed, the joints of his loins were loosed, and his knees smote one against another (Daniel 5:5-6). Picture him sitting back drinking with his lords, wives, and concubines, having a good time, and then a hand starts writing on the wall: he was terrified out of everything. None of his wise men could read the writing (Daniel 5:7-9), for it was written in ancient Hebrew, the king’s tongue, not in Chaldee; they had taught Daniel their language, and nobody knew his. He offered the third place in the kingdom, because Nabonidus ruled first and Belshazzar second as co-regent.

The queen told him of Daniel, in whom was the spirit of the holy gods (Daniel 5:10-12). That is the Holy Spirit, the Spirit of truth, which the world cannot receive and which is given to those who love Christ and keep his commandments (John 14:15-17); those who claim to have it and keep no commandments do not have it. The same spirit that was on Daniel is to be on us. Daniel, an old man now, told the king to keep his gifts (Daniel 5:13-17).

Daniel read the writing: God had numbered the kingdom and finished it; the king was weighed in the balances and found wanting; the kingdom was divided and given to the Medes and Persians (Daniel 5:24-28). His time was up: Babylon’s seventy years were officially complete.

Belshazzar clothed Daniel with scarlet and proclaimed him third ruler, and that night, immediately after the interpretation, Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans was slain, and Darius the Median took the kingdom, being about sixty-two years old (Daniel 5:29-31). It was an inside job: the Medes and the Babylonians had allied to overthrow Assyria, and the Medes were living among the Babylonians, so Babylon was not burned but taken and given to new rulers. This Babylon never burned; the Babylon prophesied to burn is the one to come, the one we are in now.

cases.name: Daniel’s accusers
cases.charge: Seeking occasion against Daniel and, finding no fault in him, using the law of his God against him: procuring an unchangeable decree that no man petition any god or man for thirty days save the king, finding him praying, and pressing the king until he was cast to the lions
cases.summary: The presidents and princes under Darius sought occasion against Daniel and found no error or fault in him, so they used his belief against him and had the king sign a decree by the law of the Medes and Persians, which could not be changed (Daniel 6:4-9). They found him praying toward Jerusalem as before, reported him, and pressed the king until Daniel was cast to the lions (Daniel 6:10-17). The Lord shut the lions’ mouths, and the men who had accused Daniel were cast into the den with their children and their wives, and the lions broke all their bones before they reached the bottom (Daniel 6:22-24).
offenseFull: Darius set three presidents over his hundred and twenty princes, Daniel first, and thought to set him over the whole realm because an excellent spirit was in him; he was set in a very high position in government (Daniel 6:1-3). The presidents and princes sought occasion against him concerning the kingdom and could find none, because he was faithful and no error or fault was found in him; he was blameless (Daniel 6:4). This is how our forefathers lived, and the same spirit we should live in, keeping a conscience void of offence toward God and toward men (Acts 24:16).

They concluded that they would find nothing against him except concerning the law of his God (Daniel 6:5). Their thinking was: we cannot find fault with his work, so we will use his religion, his belief, against him. They really hated Daniel and knew the only way to find fault was concerning the law of his God. It is the same thing the Greeks did, and the same thing the enemy is doing today: our enemies are trying to find occasion against us now, as they did against our forefathers, and they must find no fault in us, for we are to be blameless in his laws.

Men who had been at odds with one another came together on one accord, with one mission and one objective against Daniel the Israelite, and persuaded the king to sign a decree that whoever asked a petition of any god or man for thirty days, save of the king, would be cast into the den of lions, by the law of the Medes and Persians, which alters not (Daniel 6:6-9). In the Persian empire a decree that went forth from the king could not be reversed or changed, and the king’s counsellors held him to it. They framed mischief by a law; this is what the nations put around us do, to prove us.

Daniel kept praying three times a day toward Jerusalem as he did aforetime, and these men assembled, found him making supplication, and reported that Daniel, of the children of the captivity of Judah, regarded neither the king nor his decree but made his petition three times a day (Daniel 6:11-13). It was a set up.

The king was sore displeased with himself and laboured till the going down of the sun to deliver Daniel, but the men assembled again and pressed him that no decree or statute of the Medes and Persians could be changed (Daniel 6:14-15). The people of Babylon, enraged that the king had destroyed Bel and slain the dragon, conspired against him saying the king had become a Jew, and told him to deliver Daniel to them or they would destroy him and his house (Bel and the Dragon 1:28-30). So the king had Daniel cast into the den, and the den was sealed (Daniel 6:16-17).
judgmentFull: The king passed the night fasting and could not sleep, because he cared for Daniel (Daniel 6:18-20). In the Bel and the Dragon account the seven lions were starved on purpose so that they would devour Daniel, yet they did not come near him, and the angel of the Lord carried the prophet Habakkuk to Babylon to feed him, for God does not forsake them that seek and love him (Bel and the Dragon 1:31-40).

Daniel answered that his God had sent his angel and shut the lions’ mouths, because innocency was found in him before God, and before the king he had done no hurt (Daniel 6:21-23). Then the king cried that the Lord God of Daniel is great and there is none other beside him, and cast those who had sought Daniel’s destruction into the den, and they were devoured in a moment before his face: the Lord held the lions’ hunger for those who had set Daniel up to be killed (Bel and the Dragon 1:41-42).

The king commanded, and they brought the men who had accused Daniel and cast them into the den of lions, they, their children, and their wives, and the lions broke all their bones in pieces before ever they came to the bottom of the den (Daniel 6:24). When a man’s ways please the Most High, he makes even his enemies to be at peace with him; Daniel was operating in a righteous spirit (Proverbs 16:7).
Darius decreed that in every dominion men tremble before the God of Daniel, the living God, whose kingdom shall not be destroyed, and Daniel prospered (Daniel 6:25-28).
