cases.name: The churches of Ephesus, Sardis, and Laodicea
cases.charge: Leaving the first love; a name to live while dead; lukewarm, and saying, I am rich
cases.summary: To Ephesus Christ granted the works, the labour, the patience, and the trying of false apostles, then charged them with leaving their first love and told them to remember, repent, and do the first works, or the candlestick would be removed (Revelation 2:1-5). Sardis had a name that it lived and was dead (Revelation 3:1). Laodicea said it was rich and increased with goods and in need of nothing, and did not know it was wretched, miserable, poor, blind, and naked (Revelation 3:17). Each of the three is given space to repent.
offenseFull: The seven were real congregations in Asia Minor, in what is now Turkey, built up by Paul and the brothers who travelled with him, and the angel addressed in each letter is the man set over the congregation, since the word means messenger, which is what Malachi’s own name means (Revelation 1:11,20; Malachi 2:7; 2 Esdras 1:38-39). The teaching insists these seven are alive today in the various congregations, and that the point of reading them is to examine which one you are. To Ephesus Christ first granted the works, the labour, the patience, that they could not bear them which are evil, that they had tried the false apostles and found them liars, and had laboured for his name and not fainted (Revelation 2:1-3). Not bearing the evil is itself commanded: a mark is set on the men that sigh and cry for the abominations done in the midst of the city (Ezekiel 9:4), and we are to have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness but rather reprove them (Ephesians 5:11). Then came the charge: they had left their first love (Revelation 2:4). We all know what the first love was, when we first repented and could not get enough of studying. The first love is Christ, who is the word made flesh, and it is the love David spoke of when he said how he loved the law, that it was his meditation all the day and sweeter than honey (Psalms 119:97,103; 1 John 4:19). Even David left it once from a rooftop, and had to repent and come back.

Sardis had a name that it lived and was dead (Revelation 3:1). Laodicea was neither cold nor hot, and because it was lukewarm he would spue it out of his mouth (Revelation 3:15-16). The lukewarmness is double mindedness: no man can serve two masters, and a double minded man is unstable in all his ways (Matthew 6:22-24; James 1:8). The city’s own history explains the talk. Laodicea was granted free city status by Rome and its golden age of prosperity ran on trade, so the congregation said it was rich, increased with goods, and had need of nothing, not knowing it was wretched, miserable, poor, blind, and naked (Revelation 3:17). Blindness is the state Isaiah described, groping for the wall at noonday like dead men (Isaiah 59:10). Paul had already had to write to that city and to Colossae about men creeping in with philosophy and vain deceit, beguiling them of their reward and not holding the head (Colossians 2:8,18-19).

Ephesus is told to remember from where it had fallen, repent, and do the first works, or he comes quickly and removes the candlestick out of its place (Revelation 2:5). The first works are the commandments heard from the beginning, since this is love, that we walk after his commandments (2 John 1:5-6), and they were given from the beginning to men who afterwards despised his law and denied his covenants (2 Esdras 7:24). Ephesus is commended in the same breath for hating the deeds of the Nicolaitans, which Christ says he hates also (Revelation 2:6). Sardis is told to be watchful, strengthen the things that remain that are ready to die, remember how it had received and heard, hold fast, and repent, or he comes as a thief at an hour it will not know (Revelation 3:2-3). Sardis also had a few names that had not defiled their garments, and they would walk with him in white (Revelation 3:4); spots and clean garments sat in the same congregation.

The counsel to Laodicea is to buy of him gold tried in the fire, white raiment to cover the shame of nakedness, and eyesalve for the eyes (Revelation 3:18). The buying is Isaiah’s buying, without money and without price, the wisdom and understanding that rested on the branch out of the stem of Jesse (Isaiah 55:1; Isaiah 11:1-3). Then comes the reason for the whole letter: as many as he loves, he rebukes and chastens, so be zealous and repent (Revelation 3:19). That is the same doctrine as the chastening of the son in whom the father delights, which is not to be despised or fainted under (Hebrews 12:5-11; Proverbs 3:11-12). He stands at the door and knocks, and the door is opened by keeping the commandments, since he said that if you love him you keep them, and promised the comforter to them that do (Revelation 3:20; John 14:15-17). Israel’s ancient charge was that they forsook the kindness of their youth and walked after vanity and became vain (Jeremiah 2:2-5). These three letters are that charge again, with a space to repent attached to each one, which is why the verdict is reprieve.

cases.offense: The seven were real congregations in Asia Minor, in what is now Turkey, built up by Paul and the brothers who travelled with him, and the angel addressed in each letter is the man set over the congregation, since the word means messenger, which is what Malachi’s own name means (Revelation 1:11,20; Malachi 2:7; 2 Esdras 1:38-39). The teaching insists these seven are alive today in the various congregations, and that the point of reading them is to examine which one you are. To Ephesus Christ first granted the works, the labour, the patience, that they could not bear them which are evil, that they had tried the false apostles and found them liars, and had laboured for his name and not fainted (Revelation 2:1-3). Not bearing the evil is itself commanded: a mark is set on the men that sigh and cry for the abominations done in the midst of the city (Ezekiel 9:4), and we are to have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness but rather reprove them (Ephesians 5:11). Then came the charge: they had left their first love (Revelation 2:4). We all know what the first love was, when we first repented and could not get enough of studying. The first love is Christ, who is the word made flesh, and it is the love David spoke of when he said how he loved the law, that it was his meditation all the day and sweeter than honey (Psalms 119:97,103; 1 John 4:19). Even David left it once from a rooftop, and had to repent and come back.

cases.name: Antipas, Smyrna, and Philadelphia
cases.charge: Faithful unto death; keeping the word of his patience; not denying his name in the place where Satan’s seat is
cases.summary: To Smyrna Christ said he knew their works, tribulation, and poverty, and that they were rich, and told them to fear none of the things they were about to suffer, to be faithful even to death, and he would give them a crown of life (Revelation 2:8-10). At Pergamos, where Satan’s seat is, they held fast his name and had not denied his faith even in the days when Antipas his faithful martyr was slain among them (Revelation 2:12-13). Philadelphia had a little strength, kept his word, and had not denied his name, and an open door was set before it that no man can shut (Revelation 3:7-8).
offenseFull: To Smyrna he granted the works, the tribulation, and the poverty, and then said they were rich (Revelation 2:9). All the promises belonged to them whatever their purse held. In the same verse he named the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan. The history identifies them: the house of Herod, Edomites converted in generations before and sitting in the congregations, which is how Drusilla the daughter of Herod Agrippa is called a Jewess, and how men brought up with Herod the tetrarch are found among the teachers at Antioch (Acts 13:1). Judah means the praise of the Lord, and Edom was never called that. Then the warning: fear none of those things they should suffer, for the devil would cast some of them into prison that they might be tried, and they would have tribulation ten days, and they were to be faithful even to death for a crown of life (Revelation 2:10). Christ had said the same: hands would be laid on them, they would be delivered to the synagogues and into prisons, and it would turn to them for a testimony (Luke 21:12-13); and they were not to fear them which kill the body but cannot kill the soul (Matthew 10:28). The trying is the point: then shall they be known who are my chosen, and they shall be tried as the gold in the fire (2 Esdras 16:73). He that endures to the end shall be saved (Matthew 10:22), and blessed is the man that endures temptation, for when he is tried he shall receive the crown of life (James 1:12).

At Pergamos the record names one man. Christ knew where they dwelt, where Satan’s seat is, and that they held fast his name and had not denied his faith even in the days when Antipas his faithful martyr was slain among them (Revelation 2:12-13). The account preserved of him is that John the apostle ordained him bishop of Pergamon, and that he was put to death under Nero for casting out the demons the local population worshipped, roasted inside a brazen bull shaped altar. It was not a quick death, and it came under the emperor known for burning our people alive. The city was given over to the same idolatry the apostles met at Lystra, where the people called Barnabas Jupiter and Paul Mercurius and brought oxen and garlands to sacrifice to them, and stoned Paul when he told them to turn from those vanities to the living God (Acts 14:11-19). The teaching draws the line hard: nobody threatens a man who goes along with what everybody else does. Antipas spoke against the worship of that city and they cooked him for it.
judgmentFull: To Smyrna: he that overcomes shall not be hurt of the second death (Revelation 2:11). The ones beheaded for the witness of Jesus and for the word of God, who had not worshipped the beast nor his image nor received his mark, live and reign with Christ, and on such the second death has no power (Revelation 20:4-6). That is what a crown of life is worth.

To Philadelphia, the city whose name means brotherly love, he writes as the one that is holy and true, that has the key of David, that opens and no man shuts (Revelation 3:7). That key is Isaiah’s, laid upon his shoulder (Isaiah 22:22), and it is the book sealed with seven seals that no man was found worthy to open until the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the root of David, prevailed to open it (Revelation 5:1-5), after which he opened the understanding of the disciples (Luke 24:44-45). So the open door set before them is the understanding itself, and no man can shut it, though the scribes and Pharisees shut up the kingdom of heaven against men (Revelation 3:8; Matthew 23:13). They had a little strength, kept his word, and did not deny his name. He promised to make them of the synagogue of Satan come and worship before their feet and know that he had loved them (Revelation 3:9), and because they kept the word of his patience, to keep them from the hour of temptation that comes upon all the world (Revelation 3:10). The patience is the keeping of the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus (Revelation 14:12), the law kept as the apple of the eye (Proverbs 7:1-2), and the hour is the hour in which the judgment of Babylon comes and so great riches come to nothing (Revelation 18:10,17-19). He told them to hold fast what they had, that no man take their crown, and promised the overcomer would be made a pillar in the temple of his God and go no more out (Revelation 3:11-12).

cases.name: The church in Pergamos
cases.charge: Holding among them the doctrine of Balaam and the doctrine of the Nicolaitans
cases.summary: Christ granted that the congregation at Pergamos, dwelling where Satan’s seat is, held fast his name and had not denied his faith even when Antipas was slain among them, and then charged them with having there them that hold the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balak to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Israel, and them that hold the doctrine of the Nicolaitans (Revelation 2:13-15). The sentence is repentance or the sword of his mouth, and the promise to the one who repents is hidden manna and a white stone with a new name (Revelation 2:16-17).
offenseFull: The doctrine of Balaam is not a mystery; the history is in Numbers. Balaam could not curse Israel and knew it, so he gave counsel instead, and the counsel was women. The daughters of Moab called the people to the sacrifices of their gods, and the people ate and bowed down and joined themselves to Baalpeor, and a plague ran through the congregation (Numbers 25:1-3), and Moses afterwards said these were the very women who caused the children of Israel through the counsel of Balaam to commit trespass in the matter of Peor (Numbers 31:15-16). Our enemies have always known this is the weakness. Holofernes was told plainly that if there is sin in this people it will be their ruin, and if there is no iniquity in the nation then pass them by, lest their Lord defend them (Judith 5:20-21). Keep the people in sin and you can overtake them, because the connection with God is severed. Peter describes the man himself: forsaking the right way, gone astray, following the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness (2 Peter 2:15). There were men in the body who wanted nothing but money.

The second thing was them that hold the doctrine of the Nicolaitans, which Christ says outright that he hates (Revelation 2:15). Nicolas was a proselyte of Antioch, one of the seven chosen out to serve when the widows were being neglected (Acts 6:5), a man converted first to the sacrifices and then to Christ and then set over an office. The accounts read in class say the sect that carried his name lived in unrestrained indulgence and held it a matter of indifference what a man ate and how he lived, shameless in uncleanness, which is the same fornication and the same idolatry named in the verse before it, and the same seduction of Israel into immoral and idolatrous unions with the women of Moab. It is also the exact opposite of what the apostles had settled: abstain from pollutions of idols, from fornication, from things strangled, and from blood (Acts 15:28-29). God hates it because it is the worship of other gods, and his name is Jealous (Exodus 34:14). Ephesus is commended in the same chapter for hating those deeds (Revelation 2:6).
judgmentFull: Repent, or else he comes quickly and will fight against them with the sword of his mouth (Revelation 2:16). That sword is the sharp sword that goes out of his mouth to smite the nations and rule them with a rod of iron (Revelation 19:15); with righteousness he judges the poor, and with the breath of his lips he slays the wicked (Isaiah 11:4), and the wicked whom he consumes with the spirit of his mouth and destroys with the brightness of his coming (2 Thessalonians 2:8). The warning is for our own nation as much as for the heathen: follow what the other nations do and you get what the other nations get. There is no exemption for unrepentant Israel.

On the other side of the repentance is the promise: hidden manna, a white stone, and in the stone a new name written which no man knows except the one who receives it (Revelation 2:17). The manna is Christ. Their fathers ate manna in the wilderness and are dead; he is the bread of life which comes down from heaven, that a man may eat of it and not die (John 6:31-35,48-51). It is hidden because the gospel is hid to them that are lost (2 Corinthians 4:3), which is why the world still cannot say who the black Messiah is or who he came for, and why undoing what was taught about it is the work. The verdict here is reprieve, not sentence. Christ set down what was right with them before he named what was wrong, and the sword only comes out if they will not turn.

cases.name: Jezebel of Thyatira
cases.charge: Calling herself a prophetess; teaching the servants of God to commit fornication and eat things sacrificed to idols
cases.summary: Christ granted Thyatira its works, charity, service, faith, and patience, and said the last were more than the first, then charged the congregation with suffering that woman Jezebel, who called herself a prophetess, to teach and to seduce his servants to commit fornication and to eat things sacrificed to idols (Revelation 2:19-20). He gave her space to repent and she repented not, so the sentence is that he will cast her into a bed, cast them that commit adultery with her into great tribulation except they repent, and kill her children with death (Revelation 2:21-23).
offenseFull: He grants the good first, as he does with every one of the seven. He knew their works, charity, service, faith, and patience, and said the last works were more than the first: the congregation had grown, fruitful in every good work and increasing in the knowledge of God (Revelation 2:18-19; Colossians 1:10). Then the charge, and the first word in it does the work. They suffered that woman, which means they allowed her, and the letter is addressed to the man set over the congregation (Revelation 2:20). The teaching states it plainly: that spirit cannot operate without a man weak enough to let it, and what was going on at Thyatira was male leadership allowing women a voice in the congregation and letting doctrine be pushed through the men. That is why the charge given to Timothy at Ephesus was that the woman learn in silence with all subjection, not teaching, not usurping authority over the man (1 Timothy 2:11-12), and why a bishop must be the husband of one wife who rules his own house well, since a man who knows not how to rule his own house cannot take care of the congregation of God (1 Timothy 3:1-5).

The fornication is not only sexual. Jehoram made high places in the mountains of Judah and caused the inhabitants of Jerusalem to commit fornication, which was idolatry, and he did it because he had the daughter of Ahab to wife (2 Chronicles 21:11-13). Behind that daughter stood Jezebel, daughter of Ethbaal king of the Zidonians, married to Ahab as part of the league Omri made with Tyre and Zidon; she brought Baal worship into Samaria and multiplied it, and four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and four hundred of the groves ate at her table, men taking orders from a witch (1 Kings 16:29-33; 1 Kings 18:19). Her daughter Athaliah carried the same spirit into Judah and was counsellor to her son to do wickedly, then destroyed the royal seed so she could rule alone (2 Chronicles 22:2-3,10). Spirits come back. The thing that has been is that which shall be, and there is no new thing under the sun (Ecclesiastes 1:9; Ecclesiastes 6:10). That is how a queen out of the book of Kings is named in a congregation in Asia centuries later. The idolatry prevalent in that province was woman worship, which is why the rest in Thyatira are said not to have known the depths of Satan.
judgmentFull: He gave her space to repent of her fornication, and she repented not (Revelation 2:21). That space is the whole mercy of the present time, and Esdras describes what becomes of those who waste it: they that loathed his law while they had yet liberty, when the place of repentance was open to them, understood not but despised it, and the same must know it after death by pain (2 Esdras 9:11). So the sentence follows: he will cast her into a bed, and them that commit adultery with her into great tribulation, except they repent of their deeds, and he will kill her children with death, and all the congregations shall know that he is he which searches the reins and hearts and gives to every one according to their works (Revelation 2:22-23). He knows what men think in their hearts, searches out all their works, and will put them to shame (2 Esdras 16:63).

Her children are the ones who carried her doctrine, as the sons of Belial who sat before Naboth and bore false witness against him at her letters were her children in that sense (1 Kings 21:11-13). In the old account they were killed with death literally. Jehu gathered all the prophets and priests of Baal to a great feast and then sent in the guard and the captains to slay them and pull down the house of Baal (2 Kings 10:18-27), and Jehoiada had Athaliah and all that followed her put to the sword, the house of Baal broken down, and Mattan the priest of Baal slain before the altar (2 Kings 11:15-18). To the rest in Thyatira, as many as had not this doctrine and had not known the depths of Satan, he put no other burden, only to hold fast till he come (Revelation 2:24-25). There was a remnant there as there was in Elijah’s day, when he thought he alone was left and seven thousand had not bowed to Baal (1 Kings 19:14,18). And the apostles had already settled what the servants of God abstain from, meats offered to idols and fornication (Acts 15:28-29), because the things the Gentiles sacrifice they sacrifice to devils, and we cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of devils (1 Corinthians 10:19-21).
